OHCM is named as a hybrid of oversampling, CutMix and Mixup, standard augmentation parts with no stated change, inside the EMBL long-tailed model; compared only with state-of-the-art accuracy.
DCIA is a new multiclass prototype generation method that inserts and search-adjusts class prototypes; compared only with ensemble classifiers.
NaNG-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant using a natural neighbourhood graph, noise removal and weighted subgraph-core interpolation, compared with 8 oversamplers.

A weight decision algorithm sets how many samples to create per minority example from edge-detection gradients, a new allocation; general oversampling is named only as the aim, with no comparison reported.

ILMNN is a new imbalance-aware metric learning (with reweighting and KL safeguard) that makes a space for unnamed existing oversamplers; read as an existing sampler in a learned space, though the space is the paper's own; comparators unnamed.
SB-SVM-ensemble chains standard SMOTE with Bagging and SVM, presented as the new method and compared with SMOTE-SVM and a partition-based SVM ensemble.
Searched augmentation policies enlarge the minority set, then a standard PGGAN generates minority SAR images with no stated change; evaluated only before against after.
Proposes 'liner to pattern-sampling', a new regression/correlation-based way to create samples, compared with SMOTE and classifiers; the abstract is unclear on the generation mechanism.
NC_Link_MWMOTE replaces the clustering in MWMOTE with NC_Link hierarchical clustering, a stated change; compared with an unnamed baseline.
FDFRL includes a kernel-guided adversarial generator with hierarchical adversarial refinement, read as a new generative module, within federated RL fraud detection; compared with unnamed baselines.
KTS is a new K-means triangular synthesis oversampler generating by cluster density, paired with a pinball-loss LDM; comparators not named.
RAMGANH combines range-based association-rule undersampling with a modified TGAN (a stated change); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
cCGen is a new conditional classifier-generator augmentation algorithm, compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and cWGAN-GP.
Existing synthetic oversamplers (SMOTE/ADASYN per keywords) applied in a fused image-metadata embedding space, presented as the key contribution; compared only with image-only baselines.
HSMOTE is a new SMOTE-inspired module that synthesises hypergraph vertices and their high-order correlations, within the HGHC framework; compared only with state-of-the-art.
Two new density-based sampling algorithms (undersampling, and under- plus unnamed oversampling) compared with other balancing algorithms.
Generates pseudo-fault samples by its own wavelet phase-space reconstruction of signal energy regions, a generator of the paper's own; no resampling comparison; generator kind uncertain.
GraphAdasyn extends adaptive synthetic sampling to multiclass imbalanced node classification on graphs, a stated change; compared with unnamed baselines.
New LLM-based oversampler with label-and-feature conditioning, a new permutation fine-tuning strategy and training on interpolated samples (stated changes); compared with unnamed SOTA baselines.

CorrOV-CSEn uses correlation-based oversampling with a customised rate and zone (a new way of applying SMOTE) inside a cost-sensitive AdaBoost; the abstract hints this oversampler may come from earlier work.
Uses advanced elk herd optimisation to search SMOTE sampling rates, a search for how much to oversample, before a BiLSTM IDS; no resampling comparison.
NCLO-SMOTE is a new algorithm with semi-supervised clustering, Newton-cooling overlap cleaning and cluster-weighted oversampling, compared with ten sampling methods.

NB-MIO changes SMOTE's base-instance choice to safe minority samples found by a second Tomek-link search after Tomek cleaning, a stated change rather than a plain SMOTE+Tomek chain; 15 comparators not said to be resampling.

An LLM-routing paper that also proposes text augmentation plus a perplexity-based dynamic weighted/oversampling allocation; read as a new allocation, but the parts may be standard and resampling is secondary.
SSMOTE, a newly named stable SMOTE whose change is not described, is compared with other data augmentation methods for chiller fault data.
New rough-set undersampling plus multi-objective evolutionary oversampling guided by KL divergence and attribute dependency, compared with existing resampling techniques.
GMM-SMOTE is an improved oversampler that clusters with GMM, allocates by cluster density and screens by KL distance; no resampling comparison stated.
SHAP feature selection, t-SNE latent mapping and Gaussian noise sampling of minority points, all standard parts with no stated change; no resampling comparison.

Improved SMOTE that checks class crossing from the minority distribution, generates across classes when crossing is severe and reweights non-borderline positives; compared with unnamed 'other methods'.
LoRAS is a new localized random affine shadowsampling oversampler, compared with SMOTE and several SMOTE extensions.
Develops a multi-kernel over-sampling (MKOS) that generates in the kernel space learned by its own MKMFA, a newly named oversampler with the mechanism not detailed; comparators unnamed.

OHSEC uses density-peak-guided under/oversampling with validation-based optimisation of task-specific imbalance ratios (a search for how much to resample) and evidence fusion; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
TDGN introduces a density-based WGAN (a stated modification) to reduce behavioural overlap, with a time-aware gated network; compared with unnamed competitors.
DRCW-ASEG is a new multiclass OVO algorithm that dynamically generates minority examples during competence weighting; no resampling comparison stated.

Proposes a multi-kernel over-sampling within a multi-kernel feature selection framework for nodule false-positive reduction, a newly named oversampler not described; compared with unnamed competing methods.
Oversamples with SMOTE, clusters the synthetic samples by GMM and keeps them by majority-based cluster weights (a new allocation per region), compared with SMOTE and variants.
IMSMOTE is an improved SMOTE adding randomness and probability to synthesis, used in a GRC-SVM credit risk framework; compared with unnamed existing approaches.
New multiclass oversampling technique based on intra- and inter-class distance matrices, compared with common oversampling techniques.
New hypersphere-based over/undersampling driven by boosting sample weights and learning difficulty inside a reweighted AdaBoost; no resampling comparison stated.
SDD-SMOTE is an improved SMOTE that oversamples according to a designed sample distribution density model; no comparison stated.

Standard GAN oversampling followed by a novel adaptive neighbourhood-weighted undersampler of the paper's own that removes generated and majority instances; the generator is unchanged, so this may be read as generator plus filter.
FC-SMOTE is named as fuzzy clustering plus SMOTE with no change described (a new name over standard parts), and is compared with traditional oversampling algorithms.
A deep neural network is used to oversample EEG movement data, but the abstract gives no detail of the model, so own versus standard cannot be told; evaluated before against after.
A sliding-window SMOTE is developed to preserve temporal dependencies (a changed SMOTE), alongside feature selection and BiLSTM-GRU; compared only with classifier models.
VAHMSE adds mutual information to the VAE loss to prevent posterior collapse (a stated change) for anomaly data generation; compared with state-of-the-art models only.
Improved Random-SMOTE that uses SVM support vectors as parent samples, a stated change; no comparison stated.
TDCGAN is a new triple-discriminator conditional GAN architecture, compared with SMOTE and RandomOverSampler.
Graph oversampling with SMOTE on node representations plus an edge generator trained with a new abnormal-connectivity margin loss (a stated change to the generator); no resampling comparison.
TDDMRT proposes a KNN-Jaccard minority resampling method with an enhanced drift detector for streams, compared with existing over- and undersampling techniques.
New oversampler generating minority samples by genetic crossover within K-means clusters; evaluated only with KNN and SVM.
Proposes an enhanced SMOTE guided by clustering and PCA, PPO-chosen augmentation and DQN-based sampling; no comparison with other resampling stated.

Samples tail-class features from calibrated distributions borrowed from few-shot distribution calibration, applied as is in feature space; could be read as own calibrated sampling; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
DG-SMOTE is a new genetic-programming oversampler that evolves how selected instances are combined, with a distance-angle fitness, compared with popular sampling methods.
M2M-VAEGAN adds VGM feature handling, majority pre-training with balanced fine-tuning and an auxiliary classifier to a VAE-GAN (stated changes), compared with SMOTE, CTGAN and CTABGAN.
A 1-D DCGAN, a standard architecture adapted to range profiles with no other stated change, generates HRRPs; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
GNUS is called novel but its name describes only standard Gaussian-noise upsampling with no change stated; compared with seven conventional correction methods including random oversampling.
M-D2GAN modifies the GAN with type-specific generation of mixed variables and an added normal-class discriminator, compared with the classic GAN.
MGS-GRF is a new mixed-feature oversampler using KDE with locally estimated full-rank covariances plus generalized random forest for categorical features, compared with SMOTE-NC and other strategies.

GraphBalance does SMOTE in a learned node-embedding space with a jointly trained edge generator; the abstract appears to be the GraphSMOTE abstract under a new name, so coded as an existing method; compared with unnamed baselines.
ISMOTE (2011) randomises interpolation within the ball formed by a minority instance and its neighbour, compared with SMOTE.
Extends SAM-kNN with SMOTE and kENN for drifting streams and proposes a new Informed Downsampling method shown superior to these balancing variants.
Devises a PSO-based metaheuristic data balancer (mechanism not described) with GA classifier tuning, compared with random undersampling.
Surrounding-neighbourhood SMOTE variants (Gabriel graph, relative neighbourhood graph, nearest centroid) change SMOTE's neighbour choice, compared with other oversamplers.
Improved clustering SMOTE with KNN noise removal, density-based sub-cluster weights and interpolation toward sub-cluster centres (a new allocation and interpolation); comparators not named.

A cGAN with standard spectral normalisation and self-attention, followed by a quality gate (discriminator score, SSIM, FID) and sample weighting; read as a standard generator plus filter; evaluated before against after.
Enhanced SMOTE incorporating feature correlations into synthesis, compared with traditional SMOTE and no SMOTE.
A hybrid ensemble combining existing undersampling and oversampling with Bagging/AdaBoost, no stated change, within a comparative study of resampling methods.
MOT2LD is a new oversampler weighting minority samples by local densities in a low-dimensional clustered space, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and MWMOTE.
Autoencoder dimensionality reduction plus K-means-supported oversampling, a chain of standard parts with no stated change; evaluated without resampling comparison.
BHTF introduces a novel Proximity-Driven Undersampling combined with SMOTE in a multi-label Hoeffding tree forest; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
CTD/CTDE select key minority samples for SMOTE by a cost-aware three-way decision over CCA covers, a new way of applying SMOTE; comparators unnamed.
VMSG generates samples from 'volunteer' minority instances chosen by an OC-SVM with a new BaM loss, compared with SMOTE variants, GANs and VAEs.
KNNOR is a new three-step KNN oversampler using compactness and relative density, compared with ten oversamplers.
DCI-ISSA-RF proposes Data Center Interpolation oversampling with sparrow-search RF tuning; compared with unnamed famous approaches.
GBO and SSG are named only as GAN oversampling and SVM-SMOTE chained with a GAN, standard parts with no stated change to the GAN; compared with SMOTE.
AR-GAN adds an activation reconstruction loss to image-translation GAN (a new loss), compared with classical data augmentation.
Proposes a hybrid probabilistic oversampling (newly named, not described) alongside sparse group lasso features; compared with unnamed baseline and state-of-the-art.
CASS is a new adaptive oversampler using GMM subcluster centres, proximity-density weights and tailored synthesis, compared with nine sampling algorithms.
R-SMOTE synthesises from reverse nearest neighbours of a selected minority set, a new SMOTE variant compared with four standard oversamplers.

A 3D conditional latent diffusion model conditioned on tumour mask and IDH status with two added attention modules in the UNet, read as a new architecture and conditioning; no comparison with other augmentation.
MPMU is a new algorithm that clusters by imbalance degree, penalises majority instances per cluster and upsamples the minority; no resampling comparison.
Dual-tier oversampling chains GPT-2 text generation, used as is, with SMOTE; compared only with existing models.
WOASD removes noise, sets per-sample synthesis counts from distance and density weights and synthesises with an improved SMOTE; compared with unnamed traditional methods.
Entropy-based ambiguity zones guide targeted oversampling, a new allocation of synthetic examples by region, compared with global SMOTE.
Radius-SMOTE generates within a safe radius after initial selection, a new SMOTE variant; comparators not named.
WIMOTE is a newly named within-class oversampler with a 'statistical oversample strategy' and noise removal, compared with SMOTE.
Uses an adaptive subspace self-organising map, with its own local mapping and competitive rule, to generate minority samples, compared with existing oversamplers.
GAN with a restructured Transformer-ECA generator and a dual-function classifying discriminator (new architecture); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
The diagnosis scheme contains a novel imputation-based oversampling technique whose mechanism is not described; no resampling comparison.
Applies the authors' earlier RN-SMOTE (SMOTE plus DBSCAN noise removal) to multiclass data with no change described, compared with traditional SMOTE.
Designs an oversampling approach with optimised deep clustering, inheritance theory and Mahalanobis distance for Argo error samples, within a siamese ConvLSTM; no resampling comparison.
WCB-OT is a new optimal-transport generator using Wasserstein barycentres and morphology costs, compared with StyleGAN2 and SMOTE.
NPONN is a new parameter-free natural-neighbour oversampler with noise filtering and adaptive neighbour counts; no comparison named.
Generates minority fraud records by one-point genetic crossover, an oversampler of the paper's own; only classifiers are compared.
Improved GraphSMOTE with k-hop topological constraints (a stated change) inside a temporal heterogeneous graph fraud model; compared with GNN baselines.
MC-MBRC is a new multiclass membership-based resampling with noise removal, interpolation oversampling and energy-based cleaning; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
OIRP optimises how many samples to generate and where, a search for how much to oversample applied to existing oversamplers, compared with classical and SOTA oversamplers.
A new outlier generation method reflecting body-weight volatility and periodicity, compared with SMOTE-based and GAN-based augmentation.

Introduces a modified CutMix augmentation for class imbalance (stated as modified, not described) within an attention HRNet for building localisation and damage classification; compared with state-of-the-art models.
A conditional WGAN-GP with a CBAM attention mechanism added to the generator, a stated architecture change; evaluated only across classifiers.
CCG-taming transformers improves the generator's encoder with SE and MultiRes blocks and layer normalisation (stated changes), with SMOTE-Tomek and T2T-ViT; no resampling comparison.
CAHS is a new chemistry-informed oversampler recombining BRICS fragments, with confidence-weighted loss; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
Clusters the minority with K-means, then an improved SMOTE handles continuous and discrete features separately (a stated change), before an ensemble; no resampling comparison named.
RSP-CCFD introduces SAE-SMOTE, a newly named interpolation oversampler meant to reduce overlap (mechanism not described), compared with eight data-level and algorithm-level methods.
BFGAN is a modified GAN with an added boundary-importance label and multimodality-aware structure for time series; comparators not named.
wLOF-ADASYN fuses modified LOF weights with ADASYN weights and constrains generation, a new variant compared with traditional oversamplers.

Minority attribute augmentation mixes two images and oversamples minority attribute classes (mixup-style parts with no stated change) inside a compositional zero-shot transformer; compared only on overall SoTA.

Partitions the input space by MST-based clustering into local linear partitions and applies an unnamed existing oversampler within each, like clustering then SMOTE; the boundary-aligned partitioning could be read as a new way of applying; no comparison stated.
SPWGAN adds FFT physics constraints to the adversarial training (physics-constrained generation) with spectral normalisation; no comparison with other generators stated.
SEDA is a new similarity- and feature-importance-based minority augmentation, compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.

CFA-SMOTE combines an existing instance-based counterfactual method with standard SMOTE, no change described, compared with counterfactual and class-imbalance methods; target is grass growth with outlier events treated as a minority class.
RSMOTE divides the minority into four density regions and resamples per region, a new SMOTE variant; compared only across its own region variants.
Hybrid of standard SMOTE and additive white Gaussian noise augmentation with no stated change, compared with each technique alone and undersampling; the chain contains a standard augmentation.
New entropy-maximising distance-based resampling that undersamples dense and oversamples sparse areas; comparators not named.
SW uses complete random forest space division and weights to filter noise and set the position of new samples for existing oversamplers, compared against those oversamplers.
Develops a DTW-distance variant of SMOTE for heartbeats alongside a focal-modulation network; no resampling comparison.
Introduces quantum oversampling, selecting instances with a quantum operator, as an original component with PSO-tuned imputation and feature selection; compared with unnamed algorithms.
Proposes decision-tree-based undersampling and an adaptive subregional SMOTE weighted by overlap density; compared with benchmark models.
NNW-CCRS is a new neighbourhood-weighted convex-combination oversampler; compared only with no data expansion.
BCONDS is a new oversampler generating counterfactuals from majority neighbours of borderline minority instances after isolation-forest noise removal; comparators unnamed.
MAHAKIL is a new inheritance-based oversampler, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and ROS.
TFDL-GAN adds FFT-based time-frequency dual loss to GAN training (a new loss), compared with GAN, VAE and SMOTE.
DST-GAN adds a differentiable Dempster-Shafer fusion component for multimodal oversampling (new architecture); compared with unnamed strong baselines.
ADAIN-SMOTE evolves an adaptive artificial immune network with new operators to augment the minority before SMOTE, compared with 8 oversamplers.
OS-CCD sets how many SMOTE samples each positive gets from a classification contribution degree, a new allocation, compared with six oversamplers.
Kernel-based oversampling generates in SVM feature space and maps back via pre-images, compared with an existing oversampling technique.
KTE-SMOTE chains silhouette-tuned k-means SMOTE, Tomek links and ENN but also smooths the boundary during generation (a stated change), compared with traditional SMOTE.

An improved SMOTE using a mutual-information dropout sparse autoencoder space, natural-neighbour noise removal and different oversampling for borderline and centre samples; compared only with measured data.
LATE-SMOTE is described only as SMOTE operating in the autoencoder's latent space (a new name over an existing sampler in a learned space); compared with FixMatch, not with resampling.

CoDSA fine-tunes standard pretrained generators but conditions synthesis on under-sampled regions with a theory of synthetic volume and region allocation, read as new conditioning/allocation; compared with non-adaptive augmentation.
CFCPred uses its own cluster-purity-guided resampling that synthesises from sample, neighbour and cluster relations, with fuzzy voting; no resampling comparison.

MIAC applies ADASYN only to samples on which a mutual-information classifier abstains, read as a new choice of where to oversample; it could also be read as a chain of existing parts; compared only with MIC.

CADA is a newly named cluster-based adaptive augmentation whose adaptive mechanism is not described, distinct from the cluster-based oversampling and random augmentation it is compared with alongside ROS and SMOTE.
Theoretical analysis of SMOTE leads to two new SMOTE variants, compared with SMOTE and 10 rebalancing methods including deep generative ones.
MalImgDA fine-tunes a pretrained diffusion model on few-shot malware images with no stated change; compared with unnamed commonly used approaches.
New margin-enhanced synthesis with label-propagation pruning of majority outliers and a K+1-class discriminator; compared with unnamed baselines.
New optimal-transport oversampler with a novel regularisation shifting the minority distribution; no named comparison.
BED is a new density-based resampling that removes noisy majority examples and generates minority examples, compared with SMOTE.
KHOI-SMOTE interpolates toward across-cluster sparse areas chosen by an h-outlyingness index, compared with SMOTE and its variants.
Proposes two improved SMOTE algorithms limiting the generation range, before a stacked LSTM; compared only with classifiers.
ICD-Balancer is a cGAN-based improved SMOTE approach with a proposed Gumbel-Sigmoid for mixed tabular features (a stated change), for ICU survival analysis; comparators not named.
CDAF adds a contrastive alignment loss, class-conditioned latent space and staged training to a generator (new loss and training); no named comparison.
HCAB-SMOTE removes majority noise and oversamples selected k-means clusters of the borderline, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, AB-SMOTE and CAB-SMOTE.
RBO is a new radial-basis-function guided oversampler, compared with state-of-the-art imbalanced data preprocessing methods.
Applies standard Markov-chain and LSTM text generation, used as is, to create minority texts, compared with traditional oversampling.
Proposes layer oversampling and its hybrid with error-bootstrap oversampling for ramp events, compared with other sampling methods.
An improved DCGAN (stated as improved) generates fault samples after wavelet multi-sensor fusion; no resampling comparison.
AWGSENN weights minority instances adaptively and generates with a designed Gaussian density before ENN cleaning, compared with five oversampling and two hybrid methods.
An improved CycleGAN with added spectral normalisation and weight decay (stated changes) generates fault time-frequency maps; compared only with classifiers.
New extrapolated Markov chain text oversampler estimating transitions partly from the majority, compared with prominent oversamplers.
Two-cluster segmentation then standard SMOTE and ADASYN within each cluster, presented as the method and compared with standard resampling.
Proposes an improved SMOTE (change not described) with repeated sampling and a Choquet fuzzy integral ensemble; compared only with ensemble techniques.
DSMOTE is a new oversampler using diversity and separability measures to remove abnormal samples and select seeds, evaluated against four resampling algorithms.

SynKGen is described as Gaussian perturbations, scaled by variance, applied in a kernel PCA space (a new name over a standard noise sampler in a learned space); the variance control could be read as own; compared with ADASYN and SMOTE.

SHAP-selected critical and near-boundary samples steer a classifier-guided conditional diffusion model with a Transformer denoiser, read as a new allocation and conditioning; compared with SMOTE/ADASYN and CGAN/TimeGAN.
SMOTE-IDEA is an optimised SMOTE with feature selection, sample filtering and density-weighted generation, compared with traditional SMOTE.

G-TOD applies distribution calibration with generative oversampling of the rare class on aligned features (an existing calibrated sampler in a learned space), within a cross-domain graph fraud framework; no resampling comparison.

GEP-NB is a classifier using 'a simple mechanism' to generate minority examples and gene-specific selection of them; the abstract does not say whether these are standard or new; compared only with classifiers.
An off-the-shelf LLM generates synthetic sensor samples via standard prompting strategies, used as is; compared with SMOTE and random sampling.
Modifies SMOTE (weighted SMOTE, change not described) with an expert-judgement voting ensemble; compared only with traditional models.
IADASYN improves ADASYN with LOF outlier removal and special handling of categorical features, compared with classifiers built on classical sampling methods.
SSMOTE adds support and roulette-wheel selection and heterogeneous neighbour information to SMOTE; compared with 'algorithms in pertinent literatures' not said to be resampling.

KNN typing and clustering-based undersampling of the majority plus a tabular WGAN-GP (no stated change) for the minority, standard parts combined; the undersampling scheme could be read as own; no resampling comparison.
GOIO combines a triplet-centre-loss VAE with a class-centre-prompted conditional latent diffusion model (new loss and conditioning), compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
Proposes JSO, a dynamic neighbour selection oversampler based on JS divergence, within a transfer-learning SVM tuned by a new ivy optimiser; no resampling comparison.
MKC-SMOTE is a new multiclass SMOTE scheme with class-aware seed selection, enhanced interpolation and undersampling post-processing, compared with oversampling methods.

WECOI balances stream chunks with 'our hybrid approach' of over-sampling and instance selection inside a weighted one-class ensemble, but the abstract does not say whether these techniques are new or standard; no comparison stated.
AR-ADASYN is a new adaptive oversampler using angle and radius between minority samples, compared with other oversamplers.
DENI is a new hybrid sampling framework with density-gap noise detection and density-enhanced neighbourhood oversampling; no named comparison.
Proposes stable SMOTE-based variants that remove randomness in seed, neighbour and interpolation steps, compared with the SMOTE-based techniques.
FID is a new fuzzy information decomposition method that creates minority samples while estimating missing values; compared with individual and combination methods not said to be resampling.

GO-SMOTE replaces SMOTE interpolation with sampling from a fitted GMM then ENN cleaning, i.e. standard GMM sampling and an existing cleaner under a SMOTE name; could be read as a changed SMOTE; compared with unnamed similar technologies.
Mostly a status review that 'proposed an algorithm based on de-noising oversampling technology' with no detail, so whether the oversampler is new cannot be told.

Self-adaptive integrated oversampler for sporadic EHR data that adds density vectors, sample-difference weights and a proposed noise filter to subsample alignment and structure-preserving oversampling; the stated changes make it own; compared with traditional resampling.

IPSO-SMOTE-AdaBoost chains SMOTE, a cited improved PSO and AdaBoost; the abstract states no change to the parts and does not say PSO sets the oversampling amount, so existing-parts; compared with SMOTE-PSO.

Polarity-GAN adds a classifier network to the adversarial game, autoencoder initialisation and a convex-hull condition on the generator, a modified GAN; no comparison with another resampling method is stated.
Uncertainty Guided Oversampling is a new oversampler that picks seeds by aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty and sets the generation amount itself; compared with other resampling techniques.
I-SMOTE is an improved SMOTE with noise handling and a changed interpolation coefficient; compared with SMOTE.
New oversampling technique that generates samples from the trained weights of a single-layer perceptron, a neural generator of its own; compared with SMOTE techniques.

An unmodified large language model generates synthetic pose data from prompts; prompt wording is not a stated change to the model, so a B2 standard generator; benchmarked against random sampling and a GAN.

New clustering-based oversampler in which genetic-style inheritance (dominance-weighted averaging, probabilistic categorical inheritance) makes the samples inside Mini-Batch K-Means clusters; compared with random oversampling.
MDGAN is a modified GAN with multiple generators and discriminators, an exclusive loss and a contrastive loss; compared with advanced oversampling models.

Its own spatiotemporal oversampling densely synthesises foreground samples for background subtraction (pixel-wise foreground labelling, coded segmentation); no comparison with other resampling is stated.

TabDDPM-CC is a tabular diffusion model with class conditioning, the standard conditional form, and no other change is stated, so B2; the new part is the TabPFN-CE classifier; compared with ten augmentation methods and SMOTE.
Its own kernel-space oversampling whose pre-images are found from a kernel-to-input distance relation; no existing sampler is named, so own; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
TFT-Diff is a new Transformer frequency-time diffusion architecture with a hybrid time-frequency loss; oversampling and GANs are only criticised, no comparison is stated.

SIA-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant that selects synthetic images with a siamese network and explores the decision boundary; could be read as SMOTE plus a filter; compared with ROS, SMOTE and ASN-SMOTE.
TIGAN is a new GAN architecture with Transformer and Inception branches; compared with SMOTE, noise addition and several GANs for classifying leak conditions.
Oversampling draws from a Parzen-window kernel density estimate with no stated change (B2 KDE sampling), followed by a PSO-tuned RBF classifier; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
MST-Bezier is a new oversampler that places samples on Bezier curves guided by minimum spanning trees; compared with baseline oversampling algorithms.

Random Balance draws random class proportions for each ensemble member and reaches them with SMOTE and undersampling, a new allocation of resampling, so own; compared only with other classifier ensembles.

ISODATA clustering of the minority, then each sub-cluster oversampled in proportion to keep its share; standard parts and a plain proportional allocation, so existing-parts, though the allocation could be read as new; no named comparator.
EWT-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant guided by entropy-weight TOPSIS contribution scores; gains are shown only against models without it.

Adaptive-weight node expansion in a learned graph embedding sets the position and number of new nodes, a sampler of its own rather than an existing one; comparators are not said to be resampling methods.
OSConfusion is a newly named oversampler whose mechanism is not described, own by the codebook; only with versus without OSConfusion is compared.

PEAPOD's deep density sampling selects samples by density in a latent space and adds feature-level oversampling; no sampler is named as existing, so own, but it may be a standard oversampler in latent space; compared only with HDP baselines.

TMG-GAN is a modified GAN with multiple generators, an added classifier and a cosine-similarity generator loss; compared with an advanced oversampling algorithm; intrusion detection as traffic classification.
MI-MOTE is a new oversampler that creates minority instances through multiple imputations of missing values; compared with the conventional impute-then-oversample approach.
P-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant that samples the probability distributions in the data; compared only with unnamed algorithms in the literature.

DPSE sets differential sampling numbers along an arithmetic sequence for each one-versus-all member and proposes s-Random undersampling and br-SMOTE by example type, a multiclass scheme and allocation of its own; comparators are not said to be resampling.
Combines an integrated over- and under-sampling technique with an ensemble of SVMs, with no stated change to the sampling; compared only with individual SVMs and other classifiers.

Active generative oversampling changes an ACGAN/WGAN with query-by-committee selection, relabelled selected samples for the discriminator and dynamic training epochs; compared with methods including ENN.

Budget-based active-learning oversampler for partially labelled multi-class data streams that uses budget limits and dynamic class ratios to generate instances; outperforms earlier stream oversampling methods.
Uses dynamic mode decomposition with attention-driven enhancement as its own image oversampling method; compared with ACGAN, translations and other image balancing techniques.
Asymmetric random subspace places SMOTE with random undersampling inside a random subspace ensemble with no stated change to either; no comparison is stated.

New oversampler that creates samples around KMedoids medoids with a chosen distance metric (Manhattan or Euclidean); the generation step is not shown to be standard SMOTE; compared with various oversampling methods.
FW-SMOTE is a SMOTE variant that defines neighbourhoods with a weighted Minkowski distance; compared with SMOTE and recent variants.
IMBA-MMERC's sample generation for multimodal conversations is described only by its aims, so the abstract does not show whether the generator is new or standard; no named comparison.
MAGA is stated not to be a new generator: standard Copula, TVAE, CTGAN and GREAT inside a workflow of fidelity filtering, top-up and model selection; compared with six SMOTE-family oversamplers.
IF-HA is a new entropy-based hybrid sampler that uses instance-wise difference statistics to undersample and oversample; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and SMOTE-TLNN-DEPSO.
MOKCCAS is a newly named oversampler that generates instances in KCCA adaptive subspaces with parallel processing; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
DWMO is a new density-weighted minority oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and MWMOTE for breaker fault diagnosis.
Adapts existing oversampling, undersampling and cost-sensitive learning to MapReduce and compares them with Random Forest; no change to the samplers beyond distributed execution is stated.
SOUP is a new multiclass resampling algorithm that over- and undersamples by example difficulty and class similarity; better than specialised preprocessing techniques for multi-imbalanced data.
Adapts SMOTE to high dimensions with a new distance metric over a relevant feature subset; compared with SMOTE and other oversampling variants.

CSAGAN-DE feeds the minority into a conditional self-attention GAN with no stated change and lets differential evolution set how many samples to generate; B2 keeps a chained standard generator existing-parts, but the amount search could be read as own.
UCPMOT is a newly named updated class-purity oversampler with safe-level synthesis and a new Lowest-versus-Highest multiclass scheme; compared only with unnamed benchmarking techniques.
BM-WGAN feeds the WGAN generator samples from a bootstrap estimate of the minority distribution instead of noise, a stated change to the generator; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
COS-training is a semi-supervised keyphrase extraction method combining co-training with SMOTE as is; the contribution is the learner and comparators are unnamed.

Tomek-CASUWO is a newly named oversampler that changes ASUWO to avoid overlapping boundaries and adds Tomek-link filtering; compared with other oversampling methods; a new RBF classifier is also proposed.
ImSMOTE-RSTR* pairs an improved SMOTE, whose change is not described, with rough-set editing; own by the improved-oversampler rule; no comparison is stated.

For multiple-instance learning, oversamples the target concept found in positive bags and removes borderline instances, a new way of applying oversampling rather than a plain chain; no comparison is stated.
LSSASMOTE searches the SMOTE sampling rate jointly with SVM parameters by levy sparrow search, then cleans with Tomek links; a search for how much to oversample is own; no comparison is stated.
Two algorithms that improve standard SMOTE, using Euclidean or HVDM distance; improved oversamplers whose change is barely described count as own; no comparison is stated.
Mix-ratio sampling sets a different oversampling ratio for each minority class, a multiclass allocation of its own; compared with simple oversampling; used to segment mouse brain structures.
TreeSMOTE synthesises label-consistent samples from neighbours found in a tree-induced decision space; compared with popular oversamplers, generative models and undersampling ensembles.
TA-SMOTE is a SMOTE variant with semantically constrained perturbations of packet-size and timing features; compared with RF feature selection plus SMOTE.

An improved differential evolution searches the over- and undersampling rates of a parallel hybrid sampling framework, a search for how much to resample; compared only with other heuristic optimisers.
ISBA generates synthetic samples iteratively from the support vectors of large margin classifiers and allows extrapolation; compared with SMOTE and other techniques.
GOS is a new genetic-algorithm oversampler that moves minority samples to optimal places; compared with widely used techniques that are not said to be resampling.
A parallel rather than serial arrangement of existing oversampling and undersampling, with no stated change to either; compared with two mainstream hybrid sampling frameworks.

One-versus-one decomposition with spectral clustering of each minority and oversampling by data characteristics, read as a multiclass oversampling scheme of its own; could also be read as clustering plus standard oversampling; comparators are multiclass learning methods.
Introduces a generalised oversampling function with six new linear and non-linear variants; non-linear variants are compared with the linear ones that stand for existing interpolation.
FRO synthesises minority instances guided by weighted fuzzy rules, with per-rule amounts; compared with imbalanced classification algorithms not said to be resampling.
MSGNet includes a modified SMOTE-ENN with radius-neighbour grouping of class elements, a stated change; compared only with existing works.

APCIELM decides per cluster whether to oversample by a proposed affinity-propagation hypothesis after hierarchical K-means, a new allocation by region; compared with single-stage models and existing methods.
A conditional 3D DDPM generates treatment planning data; it is called novel but no change beyond standard conditioning is stated, so B2; compared with oversampling, SMOTE, ADASYN and others.
A stacked denoising autoencoder classifier fed by cost-based oversampling of the minority; the contribution is the classifier and the comparators are autoencoder variants.
An unmodified LLM prompted with BERTopic topics and examples generates hate tweets; prompting is not a change to the model, so B2; only before versus after augmentation.
CWOS-Ord is a new cluster-based weighted oversampler for ordinal regression with complexity-based cluster sizes; compared with existing oversamplers extended to ordinal regression.
A GAN generates synthetic word embeddings instead of text; no change to the GAN is stated, so a standard generator in an embedding space (B2); compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.

Ensemble oversampling that splits bagged training data into three regions by three-way decisions and uses a different synthesis strategy per region, a new way of applying SMOTE; no other resampling compared.

A standard unpaired GAN translates small-field images into synthetic all-sky images with rare aurora forms, followed by progressive fine-tuning; no change to the GAN is stated; no resampling comparison.
MOEL includes a novel Mahalanobis-based oversampling technique to balance optimised subsets, own as a newly named oversampler; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
SMOR is a direction-aware SMOTE for ordinal regression that weights candidate generation directions; compared with typical oversampling algorithms.
New multiclass oversampler that uses hyperplane-distance ranking and density-based composite weights for within- and between-class sampling; compared with SMOTE and SVMOM.
Rock-type-conditioned CVAE with a Student-t loss, low-variance gradient estimation and a correlation penalty, all stated changes; compared only with real data alone.
UGRWO-Sampling modifies random walk oversampling with graph-based selection of minority seeds and density-based majority undersampling; compared with unnamed previous methods.

Sample-level generator that mutates subordinate latent codes under mutual-information constraints with a discriminator, plus feature repulsion and combination coding, a new generative method; compared with typical data balancing methods.
D-SMOTE is an improved discrete SMOTE that generates near-discrete accident samples after map encoding; no named comparison with other resampling.
A novel genetic-search technique for generating synthetic minority data; earlier techniques are only background and no comparison is stated.
A proposed weighted SMOTE whose change is not described, own by the codebook; gains are shown against the original and a balanced dataset with no named resampling comparator.
B-ISMOTE interpolates randomly in a sphere around borderline minority instances and their neighbours; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.

Clustering-guided allocation to sparse minority clusters plus a designed CTGAN-based auxiliary classifier GAN (ACCTGAN), a modified generator; compared with seven typical methods not said to be resampling.
Sequence-to-sequence and memory-network models that mimic kNN and output out-of-sample feature vectors, usable as a new neural oversampler; as an oversampler compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
NGOS sets a global neighbourhood radius and density-distance sampling weights, then draws samples from a Gaussian model, a new oversampler; compared with eleven unnamed methods.
MCSO and MCSU are new maximal-clique-based oversampling and undersampling methods on a neighbour graph; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

CBHS pairs newly named multi-phase K-means oversampling (KMBOS) with fuzzy C-means undersampling (FCBU); the generation step is not shown to be standard; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling and undersampling.
The resampling is FKPCM boundary cleaning plus kernel SMOTE with pre-image projection, existing parts in a kernel space; the new part is the adaptive weighted forest; compared with SMOTE variants.
Draws new minority samples by Gibbs sampling from a Parzen-window density estimate, standard KDE sampling with no stated change (B2), then trains an SVM; no comparison is stated.
Three oversampling methods that weight minority samples by injury severity, accident frequency and type from an extended accident triangle, a new allocation; no other resampling compared.
BDOP-GMM-SMOTE allocates by GMM cluster density and optimises the generation boundary with a penalty coefficient, a SMOTE variant of its own; no comparison is stated.
A hybrid whale-genetic optimisation model is said to tackle class imbalance, but the abstract does not say what it does to the data; compared with SMOTE+AdaSS+GA and other metaheuristics.
SASMOTE selects visible nearest neighbours adaptively and filters uncertain samples by self-inspection; compared with existing SMOTE-based algorithms.
A VAE module trained with a discriminator-guided reward, a stated change to the generator, inside a VAE-SHAP framework; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
Improved ADASYN with a new distance metric and generation strategy for mixed features, paired with grid-searched CatBoost; compared only with existing models.
An unmodified LLM with simple SMOTE-inspired prompting generates minority texts; prompting is not a change to the model, so B2; only gains over no augmentation are stated.

WRND filters noise with natural neighbours and assigns the number and location of synthetic samples by relative neighbourhood density, a new allocation framework; compared with representative samplers and frameworks.

A genetic algorithm searches the mix of SMOTE and GAN oversampling ratios, a search for how much to oversample (own), but the GAN is standard and B2 could be read to exclude it; compared with single techniques.
Maps fractional diversity entropy to the guidance scale of a classifier-guided diffusion model, a stated change to sampling; compared with WGAN and other synthesisers.
FMDTDE is a new hybrid sampler using weighted fuzzy distance density, tournament selection and crossover/mutation synthesis; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, SMOTEENN, MAHAKIL and others.
Genetic Dual Borderline SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE method; compared with SMOTE, Borderline SMOTE and KMeans SMOTE.
Enhanced WGAN-GP with a spectrally normalised discriminator and TTUR training, stated changes to a standard GAN; compared with other unnamed fault diagnosis methods.

AEGAN is a named model that combines an autoencoder with a GAN to generate minority gene-expression samples, read as a new hybrid architecture, plus Pathifier pathway scores; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
An oversampling strategy for broken-strand images is proposed but neither described nor built from named parts; the contribution is the detection application; no resampling comparison.
Ensemble Oversampling combines a standard GAN, SMOTE and ADASYN with no stated change, a chain holding a B2 generator; compared with each oversampler alone.
DA-NGF is a new lightweight few-shot generative model with compact latent modelling, orientation-invariant self-supervision and defect-aware attention; only gains over real data alone are stated.
DN-MWMOTE changes MWMOTE with adaptive noise removal, majority-and-minority reference selection and significance-ratio interpolation; compared with its traditional counterparts.
RF-SMOTE is a newly named Random-Forest-based SMOTE variant introduced to fix the limits of SMOTE; comparative analyses against traditional SMOTE are reported.
Incremental generation of synthetic minority samples with a control coefficient, a new way of applying four oversamplers; compared with the same oversamplers applied in the usual way.
A&O combines one-versus-all and one-versus-one decomposition and applies standard SMOTE within it; the novelty is the decomposition, not the resampling; comparators are unnamed.
KASMOTE (k-nearest-neighbour average SMOTE) is introduced as a novel SMOTE variant for transformer oil data; only classifiers are compared.
A new parameter-free cleaner for SMOTE output based on constructive covering and a pair-wise deletion strategy, not an existing cleaner; compared with unnamed methods.
PSOSMOTE uses particle swarm optimisation to set a different sampling rate per minority instance in multi-label data, a search for how much to oversample; comparisons are with classifiers.
DVS creates samples that inherit most feature values and redraw the rest from per-feature KDE models, a changed use of KDE; compared with K-Means SMOTE, MAHAKIL and RUS.
SNOCC uses more seed samples and a new nearest-neighbour search so that samples leave the SMOTE line segments; compared with SMOTE and CBSO.
Time-Aware SMOTE partitions transactions by timestamp and then applies standard SMOTE, like partitioning then SMOTE; compared with conventional SMOTE.
Sodet oversamples inside each internal node of a decision tree with new distances, a new way of applying oversampling; compared only with CART and C5.0.
Refitted ADASYN places new samples by a Gaussian distribution closer to the minority centre, a changed ADASYN; compared with the original ADASYN.
OF-SSO-ABPSO wraps SMOTE-based oversampling with a new accelerated binary PSO sample-subspace filter, not an existing cleaner; compared with SMOTE variants and seven filtering-based oversamplers.
KM-GAN divides the minority with standard k-means and lets a GAN learn each cluster, with no change to the GAN stated (B2); the comparators of the comparative experiments are not named.
DOSS oversamples the majority with a standard conditional GAN and the minority with SMOTE, a chain holding a B2 generator; compared with other oversampling strategies.
A generation model that integrates a VAE with a conditional WGAN, read as a new hybrid architecture; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
SMOTE-GAN-VAE chains SMOTE, a standard GAN and a standard VAE with no stated change (B2); compared with each method alone and a beta-VAE filter.
SS_DEBOHID restricts the existing DEBOHID oversampler to a kNN-learned safe area, read as a DEBOHID variant, though it could be read as a chain of existing steps; compared with ten unnamed methods.
The generation-based oversampling module augments minority node embeddings, but the generator is neither described nor named; compared only with ML and GNN models.
SOMM generates diverse minority instances and updates them adaptively to neighbourhoods of both classes, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed existing methods.
Graphics-engine images are made realistic with existing image-to-image translation methods, with no stated change to the generators; compared with unaligned synthetic augmentation.

ACOR rebalances with an existing oversampler and then selects a near-optimal training subset by ant colony optimisation, a selection step of its own rather than an existing cleaner; compared with four popular oversamplers.
RGA oversamples selectively in regions found by rough-granular information granules with similarity-based editing, a new oversampler; compared with related methods not said to be resampling.

ABL-SMOTE is an advanced Borderline-SMOTE with improved sample placement plus INFFC noise filtering; the improvement is not described, so own by the improved-oversampler rule; compared with conventional sampling.
ACWO generates samples around an adaptive neighbourhood centre with distance-based weights, a new oversampler; compared with class imbalance learning algorithms not said to be resampling.
BootOS is a proposed bootstrap-based oversampling for active learning in word sense disambiguation; compared with ordinary oversampling and undersampling.
TAOS applies TextAttack text augmentation as oversampling with no stated change to the augmenter (B2 standard augmentation); compared only with standard classification techniques.

Noise factor encoding adds noise during autoencoder encoding to create altered fraud samples before SMOTE, read as a stated change to the generator, though it could be seen as a standard AE/VAE plus SMOTE; compared with SMOTE alone.
Masks non-event words and lets pre-trained RoBERTa fill them, a language model used as is (B2); the main contribution is knowledge fusion; compared only with current advances.
CA-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant that uses both classes to create diverse samples; compared with SMOTE and other modern techniques.
ADEO tunes DBSCAN with a DQN and generates samples inside constrained safe regions (hulls, ellipses, boxes), a new oversampler; compared with mainstream oversampling methods.
Random oversampling by sampling from probability models fitted to the minority, a standard fitted-distribution generator with no stated change (B2); compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
WRM-SMOTE weights several existing SMOTE variants by their performance and rank, a validation-based combination of existing samplers; compared with traditional oversampling methods.

Instance transfer of its own: topic-sentence features, information-gain common features and cosine similarity pick source reviews to add, with a SMOTE-based fix for feature inconsistency; compared with resampling and SMOTE.
A generative oversampling model (GANs in the keywords) is used but not described, so it cannot be told whether it is standard; only before versus after oversampling.
PRMOTE identifies genuine borderline samples without parameters and builds pure generation regions, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed baselines.

NR-Clustering SMOTE chains kNN noise removal, K-means clustering and SMOTE with Manhattan distance, standard parts with a standard metric swap; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-LOF, Radius-SMOTE and RN-SMOTE.
MaMiPot repositions majority and minority samples instead of generating new ones, a resampling scheme of its own; no comparison with another resampling method is clearly stated.
D_SMOTE is a new distributed SMOTE with two new expressions, paired with a modified BBO feature selector; compared with similar oversampling techniques.
A newly named neighbourhood-based adaptive heterogeneous oversampling ensemble is proposed with no detail of its oversampling; compared with benchmarking algorithms.

Clusters the data by spatial distribution and creates minority samples within each cluster, the standard cluster-then-oversample pattern with nothing stated as new; compared with state-of-the-art techniques.
CDSMOTE chains class decomposition (clustering the majority) with SMOTE oversampling, with no stated change to either; compared with common and state-of-the-art techniques.
An ensemble of three oversampling techniques plus a subsampling step that removes noisy negatives, none stated as new; compared with conventional oversampling techniques.

ESIO-GCN oversamples in a middle GNN embedding layer and explores different oversampling strategies, an existing sampler in a learned space; the strategy exploration is read as a resampling comparison.
SMOTE-D is a deterministic version of SMOTE and of other SMOTE-based methods; compared with the random originals.
SMOTE-kTLNN is SMOTE followed by an iterative-partitioning filter that uses kTLNN classifiers, existing parts; compared with unnamed methods.

ClusterDEBO generates samples by differential-evolution mutation and crossover inside silhouette-chosen K-means clusters, with a selective noise filter; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
SMOTE-PC is a purpose-built SMOTE variant using principal curves inside an incremental learning framework for defect prediction; only gains from SMOTE-PC itself are stated.
W-SMOTEs is a weighting framework that places each interpolated sample by the chaotic levels of seed and neighbour, a change to SMOTE variants; no explicit comparison is stated.

NG-SMOTE filters noise with an ensemble filter and interpolates between cluster centres and points on hyperspheres toward the nearest majority sample; compared with oversampling techniques including SMOTE-ENN and IW-SMOTE.
CDBH picks seeds and kept majority samples by density within k-means clusters through a roulette wheel, a new allocation by density; compared with other preprocessing (resampling) methods.

A proposed normal-distribution-based oversampler whose samples keep the minority mean and variance under stated conditions and widen class boundaries, not plain Gaussian sampling; compared with unnamed alternative methods.

Gradually adds synthetic minority examples drawn from attribute value ranges and removes those the stage classifier misclassifies, a resampling algorithm of its own; better than SMOTEBoost and DataBoost-IM.

parSMURF runs over- and undersampling inside a hyper-ensemble with Bayesian hyper-parameter tuning and parallel computing; the contribution is the parallel tool and no change to the samplers is stated; compared with the sequential version.
DTE-DSA applies SMOTE at differential sampling rates across an AdaBoost tree ensemble, a new allocation of oversampling; compared with a tree using plain SMOTE and other models.
A two-stage model synthesises minority image features with a standard GAN and oversampling, then stacks classifiers; no change to the GAN is stated (B2); compared only with existing approaches.
M-SMOTE interpolates between safe minority points and the minority centroid with DTW similarity for time series, a new SMOTE variant; compared only with models without it.
Applies 100% SMOTE in successive stages, doubling the minority each time, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with direct SMOTE and other balancing; rice yield is predicted as classes.

ADASYN synthesises unstable samples in the hidden space of an improved denoising autoencoder and decodes them, an existing sampler in a learned space, though the improved autoencoder could be read as a modified generator; compared with other imbalanced learning methods.
Diffusion and flow-based models learn the data distribution to synthesise fault samples, with no stated change (B2); compared with unnamed existing methods.
An improved ADASYN, whose change is not described, is developed inside a SPORF-based dynamic security assessment scheme; own by the improved-oversampler rule; comparisons are unnamed.
GSMOTE-NFM removes noise and groups minority instances by GMM densities, giving each group its own k for SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-based methods.
Convergent WGAN sets discriminator epochs dynamically from loss convergence, a stated training change; compared with WGAN.
NaNSMOTE uses natural neighbours for an adaptive k in SMOTE and removes outliers; compared with SMOTE and its extensions.
CdIGM generates new-class instances by shooting fixed-length direction vectors from the class centre in class-incremental learning; compared with SMOTE, OPCIL, OB and SDCIL.

A standard VAE models normal-to-leak spectrogram differences and generated differences are added to normal spectrograms; the VAE is unchanged, so B2, though the difference scheme could be read as new sampling; compared with existing oversampling methods.
A designed high-order augmented class-balancing (oversampling) module for heterogeneous graphs, own though its mechanism is not described; compared with models not said to be resampling.
AWSMOTE-NN is a proposed adaptive weighted SMOTE with natural neighbours inside a heart disease pipeline; compared only with prediction approaches.
KSMOTE is proposed to fix problems of oversampling before cross-validation in a smoke warning system, a new SMOTE variant or way of applying it; no resampling comparison.
Replaces rockburst clusters with synthetic instances from numerical models calibrated to cluster centroids, a generator of its own (physics simulation, coded statistical); no comparison is stated.
SDA-QEC uses a simplified lightweight diffusion augmentor, read as a stated change to a standard diffusion model, with a quantum-enhanced classifier; compared only with CNN baselines.

Iteratively moves selected unlabelled samples into the minority classes of a semi-supervised graph learner to balance the labels, a resampling approach of its own without synthetic generation; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

Proposes partial back translation, a stated variant of standard back-translation augmentation, to oversample fake news instead of duplication; could be read as standard augmentation (B2); compared with direct duplication.
ANCO combines location-based noise filtering and optimisation with nearest-neighbour interpolation, a new oversampler; compared with representative oversampling.

OHIT finds minority modes by density-ratio SNN clustering and draws Gaussian samples with shrinkage covariance per mode, an oversampler of its own rather than plain GMM sampling; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
DGM adds a KL-divergence term to a conditional GAN to learn the minority distribution, a stated change; compared with unnamed existing approaches.
AMOTRE is a novel oversampler that removes minority trappers resembling the majority and oversamples while shielding the majority border, inside the AnyThreat system; no comparison is stated.
Fi-Guide SMOTE generates samples guided by feature importance, a new SMOTE variant; compared with standard SMOTE.
GraphGAN builds kNN flow graphs and uses a GCN discriminator to generate minority samples, a new GAN architecture; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.

A tabular translation GAN with regularisation losses maps majority samples to synthetic minority samples near the boundary, plus a selection criterion; compared with re-weighting and oversampling techniques.
Adaptive semi-unsupervised weighted oversampling with a sparsity factor and noise removal, a changed ASUWO; compared with unnamed baseline techniques.
An improved SMOTE that spreads synthetic samples more widely is part of an ensemble with a PSO-tuned multi-kernel FCM classifier; compared with other relative models.
Restructures the representation of extremely sparse attack classes before standard SMOTE, a new way of applying SMOTE; the conditions include SMOTE on its own.
SMOTEBoostSVM is SMOTE inside AdaBoost with SVM weak learners, existing parts; compared with SMOTE, AdaBoost and SVM alone.
HENOS generates minority samples with the chaotic Henon map, a new oversampler; compared with existing oversampling methods.
CARE generates counterfactual minority samples from a structural causal model with exogenous variables inferred by a CVAE, a generator of its own; compared with unnamed existing methods.
CoBS-TGAN is a tabular GAN conditioned on biased samples (target labels and sensitive attributes), a new conditioning; compared with other synthetic augmentation techniques.
MS-SMOTE picks between SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE by data proportion, a choice among existing samplers, though it could be read as a multiclass scheme of its own; compared with unnamed algorithms.

A novel augmentation based on covariant SMOTE in a nonlinear low-dimensional embedding synthesises melanoma images; covariant SMOTE is read as a variant of its own, though it may be a standard sampler in a learned space; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
HD-Ensemble proposes margin-based undersampling and diversity-enhancing oversampling within an ensemble; compared with ten ensemble solutions not said to be resampling.
SOS-BUS pairs SMOTE with a novel undersampling technique of its own; compared with unnamed reference techniques.
Applies SMOTE inside each random-subspace iteration of a C4.5 ensemble, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; compared with unnamed approaches.
Presents RSMOTE as an improved, named random oversampler (change not described) and combines several RSMOTE runs with a Choquet fuzzy-integral ensemble; no comparison with other resampling is stated.

OsImp is a new named imputation-based sampling method for imbalanced data with missing values; the abstract names no generator kind and compares only with 'state-of-the-art methods for imbalanced data'.
An optimized SMOTE that generates minority samples from density-based clustering centres (a stated change to generation, not clustering then plain SMOTE); compared only with prediction models.
Adapts standard VAE, GAN and DDPM with ordinary label conditioning under new names (MALDIVAE, MALDIGAN, MALDIffusion) with no stated change; the generators are compared with each other.
Improved conditional WGAN-GP with Gaussian-mixture noise input and a new training strategy (stated changes); the comparative experiments are not said to involve other resampling methods.
PA-ACGAN enforces protocol constraints on generated traffic (constrained generation) before XGBoost; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Uses a standard DDIM to synthesize minority intrusion records, with only feature encodings explored and no change to the model; compared against a VAE-based approach.
Called a new oversampling technique based on GANs, but no change to the GAN and no new name are given, so a standard generator under B2; compared with SMOTE, ROS and ADASYN.
CAMIL modifies a conditional VAE with a class-aware KL weight, an adversarial imbalance constraint and feature-alignment loss; compared with state-of-the-art over-sampling methods.
SMOTE-ENN chain whose oversampling rate is adjusted dynamically from model error, a search for how much to oversample; compared only with unnamed baselines.
MASI is a new rebalancing method that relabels majority samples as minority based on the data distribution, generating no synthetic samples; compared with ROS, RUS, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
EMOTE is a newly named minority oversampling technique whose change is not described; compared with existing methods that the abstract says balance the data set.
The augmentation stage DA-CVAE is a conditional VAE conditioned on attack class with no stated change (the novelty is the cost-sensitive CVAE classifier); compared only with state-of-the-art methods.

Embeds SMOTE in an AdaBoost-SVM ensemble with a new weighting that puts more synthetic samples near new, difficult minority samples (new allocation); compared with the plain SMOTE-then-ensemble model.

MOGT oversamples from a parsimonious mixture of Gaussian trees structured for correlated time points, a named model of its own rather than plain GMM sampling; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.

Online continual-learning method whose pseudo-feature generator samples features from a per-class normal distribution estimated recursively, a standard fitted distribution in a learned feature space; compared with other methods, not resamplers.
3D-GAN uses three parallel discriminators (autoencoder, CNN, LSTM) with joint losses, a new architecture; compared only with the original imbalanced data.
GOS is a new oversampler that transforms overlapping minority samples with a matrix from the minority distribution (coded statistical as it is not interpolation); compared with 14 resampling methods.
MixBoost is a new named oversampler that selects instance pairs by boosting and mixes them (mixup-based); compared only with unspecified existing approaches.
Smart data augmentation is a named multiclass scheme whose equation combines sampling methods (own scheme, details not given); run alongside undersampling and oversampling strategies.

Proposes a novel form of synthetic oversampling based on a neural network architecture, with no name and no detail, so it cannot be told whether it is a standard generator; compared with state-of-the-art synthetic oversampling.
RB-CCR refines the CCR resampler with class potential to locate sub-regions for synthetic oversampling; compared with CCR and state-of-the-art resampling methods.
Chains repeated majority undersampling into subsets with ADASYN and a BiLSTM ensemble, all existing parts; compared only with traditional sentiment analysis methods.
Proposes a new Hellinger-distance-based oversampling method for multiclass data; compared only with classification on the imbalanced data.
SPAW-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant with space partitioning, adaptive allocation and a new generation step; compared with other existing oversampling techniques.
Runs the existing Radius-SMOTE on each bootstrap sub-sample of bagging, a SMOTE variant inside an existing ensemble under a new name; compared with previous oversampling methods.
QS-ENN is a new quantum SMOTE variant with fidelity-guided seed allocation, Fubini-Study geodesic synthesis and a protective quantum ENN; compared with Quantum-SMOTE, Quantum-SMOTEV2 and SMOTE-ENN.

TRIM-SBR is a newly named oversampler whose pruning step picks minority seeds for standard smoothed bootstrap (KDE-like) generation; the seed step is not shown to be standard but the generator is, so B2 may apply; compared with other oversampling techniques.
LLMOverTab uses large language models for tabular oversampling under a new name, with no stated change to the model or its conditioning; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
Proposes an improved SMOTE (change not described) ahead of BI-RADS co-clustering rules and AdaBoost; compared only with unnamed comparison methods.
New version of WECOI whose over-sampling generates from reference instances chosen in similarity-based clusters; compared with other data-stream learning algorithms, not resamplers.
Proposes wavelet-transform-based interclass fusion to create balancing ECG features, a non-standard augmentation of its own; compared only with known ECG classifiers.
Called an improved CTGAN, but the described change is only GMM clustering into subsets followed by standard CTGAN per class; compared with unnamed others.
SVM surrogate with an augmented SMOTE adapted to extreme imbalance (change not described) for offshore wind turbine reliability; no comparison is stated.
MLCSMOTE-FRST is a new multi-label oversampler using label-specific clustering and fuzzy rough sets; no comparison with other methods is stated.
BSGAN combines borderline-SMOTE with a GAN with no stated change to either, so the standard generator sets the kind under B2; compared with borderline-SMOTE and GAN-based oversampling.
WSMOTE-ensemble puts the existing weighted SMOTE inside bagging; competitors are unnamed and 'sampling methods outperform nonsampling algorithms' does not clearly say another resampler was compared.
Genetic Beta Oversampling is a new resampling algorithm that steers synthetic generation towards a user-set beta via a genetic algorithm; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-IPF.
Enhanced SMOTE that uses war strategy optimization for clustering, filtering and oversampling before a CAE-ELM detector; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
Sparse-SMOTE and SROT change SMOTE's neighbour step and generation through sparse representation; compared with SMOTE and other approaches.
Proposes two over-sampling algorithms that apply SMOTE to support vectors before a biased SVM, a new way of applying SMOTE; the comparison is not named.
EvoSampling generates instances by genetic programming with multi-task learning and undersamples with granular balls, a new hybrid sampler; compared with existing sampling methods.
DADO and DIWO generate minority instances by diversity optimisation, new oversamplers; compared with comparable synthetic over-sampling methods.
Churn model built on EMOTE, a named enhanced minority oversampling technique that adjusts misclassified instances by nearest neighbours; no comparison with resampling is stated.
TimeLT includes a personalized augmentation that tailors perturbations to tail samples (a stated change from uniform augmentation) with an encoder and regularizer; compared with unnamed baselines.

HSNF filters noise twice, removes boundary majority samples and applies different oversamplers to boundary and safe minority samples (a new allocation by region); compared with unnamed popular methods.
New bidirectional resampling for multilabel data that decouples concurrent labels and combines limited oversampling and undersampling; no comparison is stated.
EWMOTE is a new named oversampler that weights hard minority samples and generates them by EM-based imputation; compared with other oversampling baselines.
DAITD applies a standard GAN to learned behaviour representations to synthesize insider-threat samples, with no stated change; compared only with other detection algorithms.
Develops MKOS, a named multiple-kernel oversampler in the kernel space learned by a new l2,1 multi-kernel feature selection; no comparison is stated.
SMOTE-Cov is a modified SMOTE that uses the covariance matrix instead of k-nearest neighbours, in two variants; compared with 'the state-of-the-art approaches', among which the abstract counts SMOTE.

PPGO weights each minority sample by prior probability and purity to set how many samples to draw and the spread of its Gaussian sampling, a changed sampler; compared with unnamed conventional approaches.

Online algorithm that generates minority samples with an integrated adaptive weighted KDE plus a biasing mechanism; the KDE is not stated to be changed by the paper, so B2 may apply; compared with established oversampling methods.
Adaptive GAN that puts interpretability scores (SHAP, Grad-CAM) into its training objective, a stated change to the loss; compared only with a baseline.

DLRSD-SMOTE is a new deep generator (wavelet transform block, Seaformer encoder-decoder, auxiliary classifier, custom loss) with a multi-class filtering SMOTE block; compared with unnamed recent baselines.
Perturbation-based SMOTE picks boundary anchors from the global class distribution, perturbs synthetic examples with neighbours and filters noise; no named comparison.

New oversampler that starts from boundary minority samples in feature subspaces and optimizes a class-sensitive objective, with Bayesian reinforcement of subspaces; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.

A novel oversampling technology based on a probability distribution, with no name and no detail, so it cannot be told whether it is a standard fitted distribution; compared with unnamed traditional approaches.
Refines the output of a black-box oversampler with a refiner network trained by an adversarial loss, a new generator design rather than a filter; compared with the most common oversampling method.
MLBOTE is a new multi-label borderline oversampler with separate mechanisms for interior, self-borderline and cross-borderline seeds; compared with state-of-the-art multi-label resampling techniques.

Fuses the data sets oversampled by SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, SMOTE-ENN and ADASYN and applies balanced bagging, existing parts under a new name; the higher accuracy is only implied to be over the single oversamplers.
Couples a causal prototype attention classifier with the VAE-GAN encoder to shape the latent space during generation, a stated change to training; compared with SMOTE and other generative models.
Novel radial-based oversampling that uses the mutual class density distribution; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Trains standard text-GANs on minority URLs to generate synthetic URLs with no stated change; compared only before and after oversampling.
NanBDOS is a new parameter-free borderline oversampler using natural neighbours and dynamic seed weights; compared with unnamed baseline methods.
KernelADASYN samples from a kernel density estimate weighted by the difficulty of minority samples, a changed KDE sampler; no named comparison.
Over-sampling with a language model (named only in the title) with no stated change, inside a multi-task suggestion mining model; compared only with suggestion mining models.
SAGE-Net trains one generator against a discriminator ensemble with uncertainty-based active learning, a new architecture; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
AEKS is an adaptive enhanced K-Means SMOTE with dual noise filtering and adaptive clustering, used in a drift-aware dynamic ensemble; compared with unnamed baselines.

New raking-and-relabelling strategy that builds minority samples from majority attribute values without density estimation; compared with popular methods that the abstract identifies as under- and oversampling.
MIDS-GAN is a conditional GAN with trainable ACON activations and KL-divergence alignment, stated changes; results are reported only before and after.
GAN with a Transformer encoder block, a new architecture; compared with conventional and generative resampling strategies.
FocalGAN adds a focal hard-sample loss to generate boundary samples, a new loss; compared with deep generative and oversampling-based models.
CHRE removes negatively contributing majority samples and oversamples minority samples by a new contribution measure (GUDE); compared with imbalance algorithms not said to be resamplers.

AMOS samples absent minority points outside the empirical distribution with a normalizing flow and surrogate complement-set sampling, a changed sampling procedure; compared with absent minority oversampling methods.
BE-DeepSMOTE runs Borderline-SMOTE in the feature space of a deep encoder-decoder, an existing sampler in a learned space under a new name; no comparison with other resampling is stated.

SaVe-TAG prompts an unchanged LLM to interpolate minority texts and assigns edges by confidence; whether LLM interpolation counts as a new conditioning is not settled by the codebook; compared with numeric interpolation.
Chains K-means clustering, SVM-SMOTE and ENN cleaning, all existing steps; compared with seven other resampling methods.
Improved SMOTE with a symmetric generation strategy before a RepViT-transformer classifier; compared only with BiLSTM and transformer models.
AGNES-SMOTE clusters both classes hierarchically, chooses seeds by weight and restricts generation by a centroid rule, a changed SMOTE; the compared algorithms are not said to be resamplers.
QOSM uses quantum potential to choose cover centres in a constructive covering algorithm and oversamples minority covers, a new method; compared with existing oversampling methods.
A standard GAN generates malicious samples that are then oversampled with SMOTE, standard parts chained; compared with traditional sample generation methods.

SB-CPO is a new chunk-based progressive oversampling framework with severity-aware prioritization and localized diversity-preserving oversampling for streams; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
A conditional GAN with Wasserstein distance (standard parts, no further change) followed by a K-means and kNN noise and boundary filter; no named comparison.
A standard GAN generates samples in an autoencoder latent space after feature selection, with no stated change; compared only with other existing models.
CISO is a new interpolation oversampler with safety-guided seed selection, clearance-weighted partner choice and q-Gaussian placement; compared with SMOTE and ten other methods.

AMDO improves Mahalanobis distance-based oversampling with GSVD for mixed-type data, partial balancing and optimized synthesis along probability contours; compared with multi-class imbalanced learning methods not said to be resamplers.
Proposes a variant of SMOTE (change not described) for a smart-home prompting system; compared only with cost-sensitive learning.
DART is a newly named deep adaptive resampling technique whose working is not described; evaluated alongside established oversampling and undersampling techniques.
