Samples from a GMM adapted from the majority-class GMM by Bayesian adaptation to the minority data (a stated change to how the generator is fitted) with an assignment rule; compared with unnamed other methods.
Entropy-based over-, under- and hybrid sampling driven by a new entropy-based imbalance degree; no named comparison.
SMOTE with an improved Mahalanobis distance and a niche technique corrects imbalance inside a graph-embedding broad learning system; compared only with unnamed existing methods.
SVM-Guided GraphSMOTE restricts graph interpolation to minority support vectors, a new allocation of synthetic examples; compared only with methods reported in the literature.
Chains kRNN-based outlier removal in minority regions with SMOTE and random undersampling; compared against simple hybrid sampling.

Pipeline of unnamed oversampling and synthetic data generation followed by selection with a fidelity index, a quality screen over generators not stated to be changed; compared only with the original data.
IA-SUWO changes A-SUWO's weighting and synthesizes with k* information nearest neighbours; compared with ten oversampling algorithms.
ESMOTE oversamples boundary minority samples and SSLM removes instances beyond an F1-optimized margin, new methods; compared with unnamed advanced methods.

Generates neutral samples with an off-the-shelf LLM (Qwen2.5) and screens them with filters and audits, a standard generator plus filtering; compared only with a baseline and its own unfiltered variant.
AE-Multi-WGAN ensembles multiple generators and discriminators with an autoencoder, a new architecture; compared with unnamed baselines.
C-K-SMOTE clusters with Canopy then K-means and applies standard SMOTE, standard parts under a new name; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
Improves SMOTE with a feature-importance-weighted Euclidean distance for generating instances, used with textual features for fraud detection; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
SafeVAE-GAN combines a conditional beta-VAE and WGAN with dual safe-region constraints (constrained generation) plus boundary undersampling; compared with unnamed strong baselines.
Uses WGAN-div and mixup together with a novel nonlinear mixup and a minority-focused sampling strategy of its own; compared only with existing methods on the same data.
Optimizes the balancing ratio of SMOTE-family and interpolation oversamplers with PSO, WOA and Optuna, a search for how much to oversample; the six balancing methods are compared.
C-SMOTE ensembles classifiers trained at different SMOTE rates to find an optimal rate automatically, a search for how much to oversample; no named comparison.
Proposes cluster-based undersampling of the majority class by cluster variance, combined with standard SMOTE; the undersampling scheme is presented as new; no comparison is stated.
CSMOTE finds neighbours with both Euclidean and Mahalanobis distance, a changed SMOTE, before LSDA and LightGBM; compared only with imbalanced data and dimensionality reduction methods.
New methodology that creates synthetic minority instances with genetic algorithms; compared with unnamed other work.
A standard GAN generates fraud samples and SMOTE then reaches a target ratio, standard parts chained; compared only with a class-weighted baseline without oversampling.
Proposes a decision-surface undersampling strategy of its own and oversampling by standard KDE; only the undersampling is new, a mix the codebook does not settle; no named comparison.
Zero-complement estimator that extrapolates synthetic minority instances outward from the majority density fringe, a new generator; compared with Firth's regression and SMOTE.
SOS redesigns the score network of a score-based model for tabular data, with new generation options and fine-tuning; compared with other oversampling methods.
mixSMOTE synthesizes tail samples from head classes by mixup, with a gradient re-weighting module; no named comparison.
Clusters with a genetic K-means algorithm before the existing PCA-regression oversampling, a chain of existing parts; compared with SMOTE.
A new oversampling strategy that adds minority samples while keeping the majority misclassification rate low, generator not named; compared with SMOTE.

Enhanced SMOTE in a mutual-information sparse autoencoder space with natural-neighbour noise removal and different oversampling for borderline and centre samples; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.

IMOVNO+ partitions data into core, overlapping and noisy regions with a new cleaning algorithm and a multi-regularized oversampler, plus ensemble pruning; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
DBGS is a modified Gaussian oversampling algorithm (change not described) for load-curve classification in virtual power plants; compared only with traditional methods on clustering indices.
PABIO uses combined clustering and position-aware interpolation with a learned safe boundary, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed baselines.
Modified graph-based random walk oversampling that oversamples selected minority samples and removes low-density majority samples; compared with unnamed previous methods.
AE-SMOTE applies SMOTE interpolation in an autoencoder latent space, an existing sampler in a learned space; no comparison is stated.

SMOTE-CCU+ chains DBSCAN filtering, distance-weighted synthetic generation, adaptive centroid undersampling and Tomek links, with stated changes to generation and undersampling; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, ENN and CCU.
AC-GAN with added self-attention and spectral normalization, a stated architecture change; compared with oversampling and augmentation baselines.
Mentions a novel oversampling algorithm inside an astronomical classification pipeline with no name or detail; no comparison is stated.
SMOTIFIED-GAN feeds SMOTE samples to the GAN generator in place of random noise, a stated change to its input; compared only with unnamed traditional methods.
SMOTE-EKF refines SMOTE's synthetic samples with an extended Kalman filter, an improved oversampler with a stated change; compared with unnamed baselines.
ADASYN-N and ADASYN-KNN extend ADASYN to nominal data, new variants; compared with SMOTE-N.
I_SMOTE and I_ADASYN change candidate selection with a new similarity measure and roulette-wheel selection; compared with the original SMOTE and ADASYN.
Proposes three quantum-inspired QSMOTE variants (KNN, fidelity and margin based) used with PGM and KPGM classifiers; compared only with a random forest baseline.

GANHS oversamples with an existing dual-discriminator GAN, unchanged, then removes overlapping generated samples by neighbourhood undersampling, a filter on a standard generator; compared with unnamed peers.
Introduces K-CGAN as a new data augmentation model (change not described); compared with SMOTE, B-SMOTE and other augmentation methods.
Evidence-theory hybrid resampling that cleans uncertain majority samples and generates minority samples with a modified SMOTE; compared with popular re-sampling techniques.
Novel iterative oversampling that deletes values in minority samples and re-imputes them with EM or kNN imputation, plus random undersampling; no comparison is stated.
GPEA runs a standard conditional GAN in the latent space of a Bi-LSTM encoder before a boosting ensemble, with no stated change to the GAN; compared with oversampling baselines.
Conditional WGAN-GP with an added auxiliary classifier loss and a PacGAN discriminator, stated changes to loss and architecture; compared only with the original data.

New hybrid under- and oversampling inside bagging that selects the sampling rate by out-of-bag estimates, a search for how much to resample; compared with the counterpart bagging-based imbalance methods.
K-means clustering followed by the existing VCIR oversampler, existing parts; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, Kmeans-SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.
ECOGEN generates bird-song spectrograms with proven image generation techniques under a new name, with no stated change; compared with classic data augmentation.

CBReT balances each GMM cluster by synthesizing minority instances with a validity check, a newly named oversampler whose synthesizer is not shown to be standard; compared with imbalance learning approaches not said to be resamplers.
Class-incremental learning with replay that proposes a SMOTE based on global sample rationality to balance replayed samples; no comparison with other resampling.
Multiclass extension of the Optimum-Path Forest oversampler O2PF, a multiclass scheme of its own; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
ISMOTE creates new objects from the average of the minority objects nearest and farthest from the centroid, a changed SMOTE, alongside PSO feature selection; compared with unnamed methods.

Generates synthetic minority samples by artificial bee colony search with memetic refinement guided by feature importance, inside a fraud detection system; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art techniques.
FIDoS treats minority scarcity as missing instances and fills them by fuzzy information decomposition, a new oversampler; compared with sampling techniques.
Improved SMOTE based on density clustering, combined with multi-view features for amyloid prediction; compared with other over-sampling methods.
Gaussian Based-SMOTE places synthetic values using a Gaussian distribution, a new SMOTE variant; compared only with previously published results.
Augmentation pipeline of ConceptNet semantic perturbations and LLM-generated samples, standard parts with no stated change; compared only with prior sexism detection results.
Generates minority data at the same Mahalanobis distance from the majority class as known minority instances, a new oversampler; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
SCOU-LDCB combines a new cluster-overlap undersampler with local-density boundary oversampling; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.

Samples RoBERTa embeddings from Gaussian models with Ledoit-Wolf, Lasso or Elastic Net covariance estimates, standard fitted distributions in a learned space; compared only with prior reported results.
WBDSS improves SMOTE with Wasserstein distance and a dual safety mechanism, before a fine-tuned TabPFN; compared with traditional sampling algorithms.
SOMO generates within- and between-cluster samples on a self-organizing map representation, a new oversampler; compared with various oversampling methods.

HySMOTE removes outliers and generates with SMOTE in safe regions and by counterfactual generation in borderline and disjunct regions, a new allocation by region; compared with other oversampling methods.

OFD generates synthetic nodes and edges by 'applying oversampling techniques' that the abstract neither names nor describes, so own or standard cannot be told; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.

LOF removes outliers and the existing HCAB-SMOTE then oversamples the purified data; the claimed coupling amounts to a cleaner before an existing oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and HCAB-SMOTE.
Introduces Borderline-SMOTE1 and Borderline-SMOTE2, which oversample only minority examples near the borderline; compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
Adapts SMOTE to the string space by iteratively creating artificial strings between two samples, a new variant; no comparison is stated.
Adds a soft nearest neighbour loss to WGAN, CWGAN and WGAN-GP, a new loss; compared with the same GANs without it.
ISSBM is an improved model-based synthetic sampling that uses fitted models of feature relationships to generate data; compared with five unnamed methods.
New over-sampling algorithm built on a preliminary classification and reclassification of predicted minority cases, generator not described; compared with SMOTE and undersampling.
Hybrid ADASYN-GAN oversampling with FCM clustering undersampling, standard parts with no stated change, before an adaptive-weight Bi-LSTM; compared only with XGBoost and random forest.
New boosting-style ensemble that undersamples the majority and generates synthetic examples from hard majority examples each round, generator not named; compared with unnamed known algorithms.

Combines the authors' Learn++.NSE ensemble with standard SMOTE (or a minority subensemble) for drifting imbalanced streams; the novelty is in the ensemble voting weights; compared with unnamed approaches.
UCLSO clusters the data and generates label-specific synthetic minority points only within clusters, a multi-label scheme of its own; compared with unnamed competing algorithms.
A standard Cycle-GAN translates images of normal system-call data into anomalous ones, with no stated change; compared with SMOTE.
FC-TABGAN is a new name over standard parts (fully connected GAN, class-conditional generation, Wasserstein critic with gradient penalty); compared with CTGAN and WGAN.
New multi-armed-bandit protocol that removes synthetic minority points adding overlap, refining the output of existing oversamplers; compared with two competing refinement methods.
Curriculum meta-learning framework whose augmentation prompts multimodal LLMs with gold labels to generate tail samples, a standard generator used as is; compared only with previous methods.
NP-SMOTE clusters minority data with FINCH and synthesizes boundary and central points differently, a parameter-free SMOTE variant; compared with unnamed commonly used algorithms.
SPECGAN is a GAN with temporal-domain feature pyramid fusion and residual attention, a new architecture; compared only before and after augmentation.
AdaOUBoost uses its own clustering-based undersampling and borderline-SMOTE at several sizes fused by accuracy, adapting the degree of resampling; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

Samples local Gaussian candidates around selected anchors in a supervised autoencoder latent space and keeps those passing support checks, a standard sampler in a learned space plus filters; compared with other augmentation settings and SMOTENC.
Mean-shift clustering then SMOTE on selected clusters, existing parts; compared with literature algorithms that the abstract describes as generating samples, a borderline compared call.
GAMC creates offspring samples by genetic crossover and mutation and accepts them by Monte Carlo acceptance-rejection, a new oversampler; compared with two classical oversampling methods.

DatRel relocates oversampled points towards class cover catch digraph dominant points, a new way of applying SMOTE-family oversamplers; compared with Tomek links, ENN, NEATER and NearMiss after SMOTE.
TLS-WGAN-GP puts an encoder-decoder-encoder three-layer subnet in the WGAN-GP generator, a new architecture; compared with typical oversampling and plain WGAN-GP.

SCUT is a multi-class hybrid sampling scheme that SMOTEs minority classes and undersamples majority classes by clustering to handle within- and between-class imbalance; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
SA-CGAN trains attribute-wise conditional GANs and filters new instances with an attribute-based minimax filter, a new generator design; compared with GAN, CGAN and multiclass oversamplers.
Hybrid sampling that removes high mass-ratio-variance majority instances and synthesizes from high-variance minority instances, a new selection scheme; compared only with plain classifiers.
MOPSO-SMOTE optimizes SMOTE's synthetic samples by multi-objective particle swarm optimization; compared with five baseline resampling techniques.
Distributed Spark SMOTE that finds neighbours by locality-sensitive hashing, a changed neighbour step (could also be read as an implementation of SMOTE); no comparison is stated.
Gamma Sampling is a named oversampler based on the Gamma distribution whose working is not described; no comparison is stated.
Proposes G-SMOTE, a SMOTE hybridized with a genetic algorithm, inside an IoT water-quality incremental learning framework; compared with no other resampling.
A new balancing method based on learning and sampling probability distributions, with no further detail, so a standard fitted distribution cannot be ruled out; compared with SMOTE.
DAI is a new multi-label re-sampling algorithm that over- and undersamples at once to shift label proportions; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art results.
MC-SMOTE is a newly named multi-cluster SMOTE whose change is not described; compared with RUS, ROS and SMOTE.
Generates minority points along fitted dose-response curves, a new model-based balancing method; compared with SMOTE and the raw data.
SDDSMOTE is a new SMOTE variant based on sample density distribution; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling algorithms.
BBO combines binarization with boosting and oversampling, existing parts with no stated new resampling step; compared only with traditional binarization.
Combines 'an undersampling technique' and 'an oversampling technique' with an SVM without naming or describing them, so own or standard cannot be told; no comparison is stated.
Proposes a manifold-based synthetic oversampling framework whose generative bias follows the data manifold instead of SMOTE's; its superiority is shown against SMOTE-style oversampling.
TDBCL includes DDTSS, a new time-series resampling algorithm with a novel DDTW-Tomek link undersampling and Self-SMOTE; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Combines SMOTE with one-versus-all decomposition and deep learning or ensemble classifiers, all existing parts; compared with unnamed other methods.

FincGAN creates node samples with a GAN not stated to be changed and links them with deep learning edge generators; whether the edge step makes the generator its own is not settled; compared with baseline models.
Chains Kalman filter smoothing, a standard conditional GAN and one-vs-one decomposition; compared with unnamed competitors.
Cyclic exponential averaging creates points between consecutive minority pairs with exponential weights, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, SVM-SMOTE and KMeans-SMOTE.

Novel multiclass hybrid scheme: one-vs-one decomposition, the paper's own density-aware undersampling and Borderline-SMOTE; coded own as a multiclass scheme of its own, though it could be read as a chain of existing parts.
New oversampler with manifold reduction, grid clustering, entropy-based allocation and Beta-distribution SMOTE; stated changes, so own.
SRBO splits minority points into safe, dangerous and noise and allocates synthetic counts before radial-based oversampling; a new allocation, so own.
HEOMGA generates minority samples with a genetic algorithm whose fitness uses HEOM; a new oversampler compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and others.
Proposes modified SMOTE variants D-SMOTE and BP-SMOTE, compared with basic SMOTE, before a stacking classifier; named SMOTE changes, so own.
CS-SMOTE uses a center offset factor and three-point interpolation; new SMOTE variant; competitors are not said to be resampling methods.
New attention-guided prototype mixing that cuts and pastes instances across whole slide images to diversify the minority; own method compared with oversampling and augmentation methods.

SMOTE whose k is chosen by an improved multi-objective wolf pack search, presented as a novel element; coded own as a search over how SMOTE is applied, borderline with plain tuning; compared only with existing models.
K-means clustering chained with standard CTGAN; the 'improvement' in the title is the clustering step, not a stated change to CTGAN, so existing-parts.
WOTBoost adjusts its oversampling at each boosting round through a weighted distribution; a new allocation inside boosting, compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and SMOTEBoost.
AOLM filters overlap by local density, builds hyperspheres and allocates random oversampling adaptively; new oversampler compared with mainstream oversamplers.
Cluster-based oversampling built from K-means and SMOTE after HEOM imputation; standard parts; compared with baselines without clustering and/or oversampling, read as including SMOTE alone.
Minority samples are made with the existing counterfactual tool DiCE, used as is, in place of SMOTE; DiCE is not on the B2 list and its kind is not covered, coded classical as nearest.
CARBO generates samples by threshold-based geometric rotation with majority-influenced clustering; new oversampler; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
FLEX-SMOTE picks the region to oversample from a density function of the minority class; new SMOTE variant; no comparison stated.
Improved ADASYN with complexity-based neighbour choice and iterated greedy refinement of synthetic patterns; compared with four oversamplers.
GAMO: a new three-player adversarial game with a convex generator; new generative model; no comparison with resampling stated.
Newly named CAS-NR (Clustered Adaptive SMOTE with Noise Reduction) whose change is not described, so own; title presents it as the novelty; no resampling comparison.
Retinopathy grading model 'strengthened by a new hybrid oversampling method' with no name, parts or detail; cannot tell, so unclear.
Dynamic balanced sampling that adaptively sets SMOTE's neighbour count, with random undersampling, inside an improved random forest; coded own as a new way of applying SMOTE.
AGSS: newly named DBSCAN-based adaptive oversampler that synthesises in dense minority clusters; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
The paper's own 3D-engine rendering pipeline with class-targeted balancing synthesises minority damage images; rendering is not a codebook kind, coded augmentation; compared only with reweighting.
MixBoost iteratively selects and mixes majority and minority instances; a new mixup-based oversampler; compared only with unnamed existing approaches.
Standard beta-VAE generates minority samples by latent manipulation for a triplet network; no stated change to the generator, so existing-parts.
Cluster oversampling with an improved kernel FCM then SMOTE, before SVM and PIBoost; the stated improved clustering step is coded own, but the abstract is vague.

RBStack draws a random minority size, oversamples with SVM-SMOTE and randomly undersamples inside a new stacking ensemble; the resampling parts are standard and the novelty is the ensemble, so existing-parts; compared only with classifiers.
FG-SMOTE removes subgroup information from node embeddings, samples synthetic nodes from them and adds edges with a fair link predictor; new graph oversampler; only unnamed baselines.

CERTIFIES develops its own pre-learning resampling in which assistant classifiers screen critical samples after an unnamed oversampler; coded own for the new screening step, borderline with oversampling plus a filter.

GL-GAN integrates SMOTE in a learned latent space with adversarial training to capture global structure; coded own as a new generative architecture, though it could be read as latent SMOTE chained with a standard GAN.
MSBNRT, a modified Borderline-SMOTE with noise reduction whose change is not described, so own; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and NRAS.
ESA-GCN uses SMOTE-ENN on nodes with a new attention mechanism for generating the synthetic nodes' edges; coded own for the changed graph oversampling step; no comparison stated.
Enhanced support-vector-based oversampler whose change is not described, so own; compared with the studied oversampling techniques.
New oversampler based on convex combinations of minority samples; results claim better performance without naming what it was compared with.
Constraint-aware genetic algorithm with anatomical rules in its fitness evolves synthetic landmark samples; own generator compared with standard augmentation.

MOEF designs a multi-oversampling strategy giving several balanced sets fused by a Dempster-Shafer discounting rule; coded own as a new way of applying oversampling; compared only with unnamed related methods.
Novel granule-based selective oversampling with three modes and a rough-set filter of generated samples; own; compared only with unnamed other techniques.
SMOTE with an adaptive choice of k for multiclass startup data; coded own as a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with other imbalance-handling methods.
MSYN: new margin-guided synthetic oversampling; no comparison stated.
NaNDS removes overlapping majority samples via density-based hyperspheres and oversamples with natural-neighbour weights; new hybrid sampler; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
Newly named composite oversampler TampC-CL-SMOTE proposed alongside an attribute reduction algorithm, so own; the comparison algorithm is not named.
K-medoids-based SMOTE with LPP features and AdaBoost.M2; no stated change to SMOTE, read like K-means then SMOTE, so existing-parts; compared with traditional oversampling.
AWSMOTE adds two SVM-based weights to SMOTE; new variant compared with SMOTE and its improved versions.
SMOTE improved with an anticosine function, K-means++ and TLR before an MSFO-tuned SVM; improved oversampler, so own; compared only before against after balancing.
NOTE chains a stacked autoencoder for latent features with a standard cWGAN for oversampling; no stated change to the generator, so existing-parts.
Univariate and dual-channel SMOTE extensions feed a multi-path CNN; coded own for the SMOTE extensions, but the abstract does not say whether they are new; compared only with a CNN baseline.
Enhances GraphSMOTE with network-specific constraints to generate synthetic nodes in a heterogeneous graph; changed oversampler; no comparison stated.
Enhanced WGAN-GP with attention, layer normalization and skip connections in the discriminator; stated architecture change, so own; compared only with IDS methods.
FFA-GAN tunes GAN hyperparameters dynamically with the firefly algorithm; coded own as a stated change to training, borderline with tuning a plain GAN; task is speech recognition.
Proposes WCDSMOTE (SMOTE with weighted cosine distance) plus weighted ENN; new SMOTE variant; compared only with sORF prediction methods.
AHE sets the oversampling amount from within-class imbalance, uses an improved SMOTE and hardness-histogram undersampling in a boosting-like ensemble; own; only unnamed baselines.

Augmentation chains K-Shape clustering with sliding windows and DTW-SMOTE per region for a CT fault-diagnosis network; no part is stated as new, so existing-parts, coded augmentation for the sliding-window step.
Decision Boundary Computation-based Oversampling generates samples in the computed minority part of the decision boundary; new method; only unnamed state-of-the-art methods compared.
MLFS oversampling synthesises minority samples in a new quasi-linear-kernel feature space computed through the kernel matrix; a new method of its own; no comparison stated.
SOTB: semi-supervised oversampling on Mahalanobis-based triangles and their barycenters; new oversampler compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
REEL develops a double-level oversampling (change not described) with an improved random forest; newly named oversampler, so own; compared only with unnamed algorithms.
An oscillator factor decides per subset between undersampling and multiple-imputation oversampling for data with missing values; a new way of applying resampling, so own.
Standard GMM sampling of a cluster-structured positive class combined with a weighted SVM that down-weights synthetic samples; the generator is unchanged, so existing-parts.
New two-step interpolation (toward the positive centre, then toward negative neighbours) with undersampled balanced subsets for an ELM ensemble; own; compared only with ensemble algorithms.

Hybrid sampler that generates from high-density minority instances within k-means clusters and removes boundary majority instances by density; own selection rules; compared with unnamed established techniques.
GAN-based oversampling of faulty modules with no stated change to the GAN; standard generator, so existing-parts; compared with class imbalance techniques.
Oversampling with a conditional WGAN-GP whose described features (Wasserstein loss, gradient penalty, label conditioning) are the standard ones; plain standard model, so existing-parts.
NASOTECH allocates synthetic samples per minority sample by noise ratio; a new allocation compared with three oversamplers.
Oversampling guided by each module's fault content; a new way of applying oversampling compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
Bidirectional sampling with a designed sampling ratio and correlation-based under- and oversampling before an SSD model; new method of its own; comparison target not stated.
SyMProD-IF adds Isolation-Forest-based adaptive weighting and a simplified design to SyMProD; changed oversampler compared with the original method and G-SMOTE.

ADASYN adapted to a multi-label learning framework for data balance inside a PET feature-selection method; coded own for the stated adaptation, though its detail is not given and the contribution lies in feature selection.
Visualization and silhouette scores guide the choice among existing oversampling techniques; a choice among existing samplers, so existing-parts; assessed only before against after.
SPY, a newly named resampling method whose working is not described, so own; compared with SMOTE and its variants.
HOVER removes heterophilic edges by heuristic criteria, then oversamples minority nodes in the learned embedding without edge synthesis; coded own as a new graph oversampling method.

Improved K-means clustering then Borderline-SMOTE on boundary minority samples per cluster; coded own because the clustering step is stated as improved; compared only with unnamed traditional methods.
Statistical theory of synthetic augmentation with Validation-Tuned Synthetic Size, a search for how much to oversample, so own; the generator is generic.
MCSMOTE generates samples through a transition-matrix Monte Carlo mechanism; new oversampler compared with ROS, SMOTE, ADASYN and others.
ISBA extends swarm optimisation of SMOTE parameters to incremental decision trees; a search over how SMOTE is applied, so own; compared with SBA.
Wiener process oversampling perturbs samples within the normal distribution and is integrated into WPOBoost; new oversampler; compared with unnamed imbalance learning solutions.
P2PK-SMOTE re-balances locally by synthetic generation and shares a fraction of synthetic minority data across peers; a new way of applying SMOTE; no named comparison.
Cluster-based undersampling with ROSE pseudo-oversampling; both parts standard, so existing-parts; ROSE's smoothed bootstrap is KDE sampling, so coded statistical; compared with SBC, KMUS and OBU.
GANsemble picks an augmentation strategy automatically, trains a cGAN (MPcGAN, presented as a baseline) with it and filters the output; no stated change to the cGAN, so existing-parts.
SDG-GAN is a GAN-based generator whose only named part is a GAN and whose change is not stated; read as a standard generator under a new name, so existing-parts.
Improved random balance sampling with random class weights fusing over- and undersampling for multiclass data; improved resampler, so own; compared with traditional resampling.
Two novel feature-space oversamplers, M2mf and M2mu, derived from the network-guided M2m translation; own; compared with the original M2m and baselines.
EDAOS synthesises instances by RPCL clustering then sampling from estimation-of-distribution models; both parts are existing and unchanged, so existing-parts with a fitted-distribution generator.
Contrastive learning on a KNN graph that expands minority representations in the embedding space; the abstract does not say how or name a generator, so unclear.
Two stages: heuristic-enhanced SMOTE with searched sampling rates, then a GAN whose generator embeds an autoencoder; stated changes, so own.
Distance features pick safe, low-imbalance seeds for SMOTE in multiclass data; a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with MultiRandBal random oversampling.
New oversampler based on a stratification of Pascal's triangle; own; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, G-SMOTE and Gaussian oversampling.

New probabilistic WordNet synonym augmentation weighted by synonym similarity to oversample minority clinical notes; stated change from plain synonym replacement, so own; compared with existing augmentation.
New fuzzy-based hybrid data-level resampling technique with little detail; coded own as a method of the paper's own; compared with unnamed approaches.
Sets the oversampling size from classification complexity instead of full balance; a search for how much to oversample, so own; compared with full balancing.
NADOS gates interpolation seeds by a reliability score and allocates synthesis by a difficulty score; new allocation compared with nine oversamplers.
DeepSMOTE with BSRBF-KAN layers replacing its MLP layers; stated architecture change, so own; compared with the MLP-based DeepSMOTE.
US-PONR removes duplicate version samples by undersampling, then oversamples via propensity score matching; new method; compared with unnamed dataset processing methods.
BCGAN, a borderline-conditional GAN that generates minority data along the class border; new conditioning, so own; no comparison stated.
Adapts the existing MultiBoost ensemble with unnamed resampling; no new resampling stated, so existing-parts; compared only with simple and ensemble techniques.
Uses SMOTE, ADASYN and a ResNet-based Deep-CTGAN, with a fix to how the target variable is generated, before TabNet; read as existing generators used as is, so existing-parts.
Ensemble-SMOTE pools the datasets produced by several SMOTE variants; a combination of existing samplers, so existing-parts; compared with other treatment methods and sampling ratios.
MM-WGAN-GP uses multiple critics with complementary perspectives; stated architecture change, so own; compared only with an IDS.
MPP-SMOTE removes noise, splits minority samples by predicted probability and uses separate selection and generation schemes; new variant compared with other oversamplers.
SAC, a named technique that generates synthetic data per class subset and recombines; generator not named; coded own as a newly named oversampler; compared with ROSE and SMOTE.
New oversampling for CNNs that adversarially changes oversampled instances during training; own; no named comparison.
Hybrid resampling whose class sizes are set by logarithmic interpolation (SMOTE for minorities, RUS for majorities); a new allocation, so own.
HD-GNNS adds an SE-block encoder and a cross-layer, low-rank structure to the GAN, with natural-neighbour noise removal and adaptive undersampling; stated changes, so own.
Retracted paper; designs a novel oversampler based on the three-way-decision boundary region before attribute reduction; own; compared only with attribute reduction algorithms.

EyeDiff is a standard latent diffusion model trained on ophthalmic data to generate images from text prompts; no stated change to the generator, so existing-parts; compared with traditional oversampling.

SEO pools five existing oversamplers and adds its own strategies (such as Cluster Uncentered) for selecting the generated samples; coded own for the selection strategies; compared with single oversamplers.
WGAN conditioned on feature-relationship graphs and steered by LLM-defined constraints; new conditioning and constraints, so own; compared with SMOTE.
DML-SMOTE replaces SMOTE's Euclidean distance with a learned metric; changed SMOTE compared with standard SMOTE.
CIRKNN balances data with centroid and KNN concepts instead of SMOTE's random seeds; new oversampler compared with SMOTE.
SOVA applies SMOTE inside a one-versus-all LightGBM ensemble after DCT feature extraction; standard parts, so existing-parts; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes SMUTE (interpolation-based undersampling) and CSMOUTE combining it with SMOTE; new method; no named comparison.
A named 'dominant SMOTE' whose change is not described, so own; compared with SMOTE, an outlier SMOTE and ADASYN.
Conditional residual diffusion constrained by defect masks, with output filtering and balanced sampling, for anomaly detection and localization; constrained generation, so own.

Adaptive DBSCAN, whose parameters follow density, clusters the minority before SMOTE, plus cost-sensitive learning; coded own for the stated adaptive clustering step, borderline with clustering then SMOTE.
A standard conditional VAE generates distilBERT report vectors with security labels; no stated change to the generator, so existing-parts.
SGSF contributes its own rough-set-based noise removal (SGNR) and positive-region-oriented oversampling (PROO); new methods; no named comparison.
DTE-SBD applies SMOTE with differentiated sampling rates across bagging iterations; coded own as a new allocation of synthetic examples; compared with SMOTE and other resampled tree models.
Extracts defect templates against similar normal images, augments them and merges them into other normal images; own generation method compared with oversampling and augmentation.

Converts binary features to numerical ones by feature extraction before standard oversampling; the contribution is the feature step, so existing-parts with presented no; compared with oversampling on raw features.
HCFF-SMOTE applies SMOTE in the feature space of a new skip-connected encoder-decoder with attention fusion; new architecture, so own; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
A standard conditional GAN used as an oversampler; no stated change, so existing-parts; compared with standard oversamplers.
MeanShift-guided oversampling with random vectors, a cut-off mechanism and self-adaptive sizes; new oversampler and allocation; compared with unnamed methods.
CGAN with a progressive decoupling generator, patch discriminator, perceptual loss and SMOTE between real and generated samples; stated changes, so own.
Score-based hybrid sampling that interpolates between sparse minority samples and removes dense majority samples via sharing and tournament selection; own; compared with other preprocessing methods.
SMOTE on topic vectors followed by an autoencoder that reconstructs the balanced data; read as SMOTE with an autoencoder cleaner, so existing-parts; no named comparison.
CAF-Net applies an unspecified data augmentation to learned sequence features before fine-tuning; the abstract does not say what the augmentation is, so unclear.
A 'deep oversampling technique' for acne grading with no name, parts or detail; cannot tell, so unclear.
Uses a large language model as is to generate minority traffic samples; a standard generator of the B2 list, so existing-parts; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and TVAE.
Data split into MapReduce blocks, each balanced with a 'hybrid SMOTE' that is not described and fed to decision trees; read as partitioning then SMOTE, so existing-parts; no resampling comparison.
PFIE designs a physics-based augmentation from fault frequencies and synthesises samples with a physical-feature optimisation function; own constrained generator; compared with unnamed approaches.
BEDCOE generates synthetic samples from adaptively kept class-wise disjunct clusters, with borderline-enhanced training, for online multiclass streams; own; no named comparison.
A modified local adaptive SMOTE (LA-SMOTE) before a GRU detector; modified SMOTE, so own; compared only with IDS models.
SP-SMOTE oversamples within a new density-adaptive space partition (Dannoy); new variant compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, K-means SMOTE and others.
LncSTPred proposes 'a new oversampling method' with no name or detail alongside an improved AdaBoost; cannot tell, so unclear.
draGAN, a new GAN architecture that generates minority and majority samples to optimise classifier performance; own; compared with SMOTE-family and GAN methods.
Replaces SMOTE with Jacobian Data Augmentation, enhanced to handle categorical features; stated change, so own; generator kind coded augmentation; no explicit resampling comparison.
CopulaSMOTE samples from truncated vine copulas fitted to the minority class; a standard copula used as is, so existing-parts; compared with other resampling strategies.
SMOTE applied unchanged to meta-level features inside a stacking ensemble with TabTransformer; the contribution is the ensemble; compared only with and without SMOTE.
FL-SMOTE computes SMOTE across federated clients under partially and fully homomorphic encryption; a new way of applying SMOTE, so own; no named comparison.
AWH-SMOTE adds attribute weighting and kNN-hub-based selective sampling to SMOTE; changed variant compared with other oversamplers.
Proposes five new named samplers (SMOTERandRep and lax random over- and undersampling variants) built on RO, RU and SMOTE; newly named, so own; compared with SMOTE, RO and RU.
ProWRAS combines LoRAS and ProWSyn with variance control, proximity-weighted clustering and four schemes; stated new design, so own; compared with five oversamplers.
DDPM-LGFormer: a diffusion model with a new local-global transformer module; new architecture, so own; compared with GAN-based generators.
Power-GNN adds high-similarity edges to low-degree synthesised nodes, using the power law in reverse; new graph oversampling; only unnamed baselines.
Standard VAE-based minority augmentation inside a hybrid encoder and ensemble pipeline; no stated change to the VAE, so existing-parts; benchmarked against SMOTE and ADASYN.
BI-BMCSMOTE: BIRCH clustering, probabilistic boundary marking, density-based weights and midpoint composite sampling; new variant; no named comparison.
Dissertation on mouse brain segmentation; mix-ratio sampling sets different oversampling ratios per minority class, a new allocation, so own; compared with simple oversampling.

A hybrid mixup strategy derived from an analysis of existing mixed-sample augmentations, with a two-head network and balanced softmax; read as a combination of standard augmentations, so existing-parts.
STANDER generates Feature Envy samples from multidimensional code-entity similarity; new oversampler compared with baseline oversamplers.
MSMOTEBoost adds safety and multi-class-neighbour weights to SMOTE and fuses it with AdaBoost.M2; stated changes, so own; no named comparison.
TimeWeightedSMOTE restricts neighbour selection by temporal proximity with a decay mechanism; changed SMOTE compared with seven sampling methods.
W-SMOTE uses DTW neighbours, a safe-level interpolation proportion and interpolation along the DTW path; new variant; no named comparison.
ASCB_DmSMOTE uses swarm optimisation to set SMOTE parameters and over- and undersampling per clustered sub-dataset; a search over how SMOTE is applied, so own; compared with other SMOTE versions.
Gaussian noise injection into minority samples, a standard augmentation, offered as an alternative to SMOTE and ADASYN; no stated change, so existing-parts.
SA-CTGAN adds self-attention to the CTGAN generator; stated architecture change, so own; compared with SMOTE and CTGAN.

SBoost adds synthetic minority instances at each boosting round and deletes those misclassified, with a threshold-based weight update; coded own as a new way of applying oversampling in boosting; generator unnamed.
CURE-SMOTE combines CURE clustering with SMOTE without a stated change to either, so existing-parts; compared with random sampling and several SMOTE variants.
EDKS oversamples in SVM kernel space guided by entropy difference and sparse regions; new variant; only unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
MKLMO generates synthetic instances in a multiple-kernel feature space jointly with classifier training; new method; only unnamed baselines.
Statistically informed generation constrained to the distribution of real kinematics to keep movements physiologically plausible; constrained generation, so own.
C-SASO synthesises new instances by a safe metric of selected instances after clustering and adaptive sizes; own generation rule; no named comparison.
GradGAN feeds the minority data gradually through a GAN until balance; coded own for the stated gradual procedure, borderline with a plain GAN; compared only with no oversampling.
Empirical study of distance in SMOTE-based techniques that also improves SMOTUNED (faster, same accuracy); improved oversampler, so own; compared with the original SMOTUNED.
DSMOTE and ESMOTE synthesise near easily misclassified samples; new variants compared with SMOTE.
DDMSE estimates minority sub-regions by direction distribution and synthesises within them; new method compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
SDP-CycleGAN trains CycleGAN on siamese data pairs to synthesise balancing data; coded own for the stated pair structure, borderline with a standard CycleGAN; compared with SMOTE.
Genetic-algorithm oversampler that generates diverse minority samples by a distribution measure; own; compared with SMOTE, BSMOTE, ADASYN, ROS and MAHAKIL.
BiGAN with an improved training architecture that adds encoder feedback to the generator; stated training change, so own; compared with the original GAN-based method.
Carsite_AGan pairs a new attention-based undersampler with a GAN oversampler that has no stated change; the generator is standard, so existing-parts under B2, though the undersampler is new.
VGAN generalises MSE GAN and WGAN-GP with a V-matrix criterion and an early-stopping-like strategy; new loss and training, so own; compared with GANs and SMOTE.
IFSDS, a newly named stream algorithm with its own over- and undersampling (not described), so own; compared only with C4.5 and Hoeffding tree.
Modified ODBOT that uses Mahalanobis instead of Euclidean distance; changed oversampler compared with Euclidean ODBOT and SMOTE.
Adaptive oversampler for between- and within-class imbalance that accounts for data spread; new method compared with existing oversamplers.
Two new noise filters for borderline majority instances combined with SMOTE and thresholding; coded own for the new filters, a case the codebook leaves open; compared with class-imbalance techniques.
SL-D merges Safe-Level-SMOTE with DEBOHID in three variants with an adaptive crossover rate; stated new design, so own; compared with nine oversamplers.
Fuzzy K-Prototypes clustering then SMOTE-NC within clusters, SVM and a weighted ensemble; existing parts without a stated change, so existing-parts; compared only with plain SVM.
Separates core and boundary samples, oversampling the boundary and reducing the core; new method; no named comparison.
HABC computes an adaptive sampling rate from data characteristics and applies density-based under- and oversampling before bagging; a new allocation, so own; only unnamed algorithms compared.
Extends NI-MWMOTE by widening its hyperparameter range and correcting its noise function, then uses it with LS-SVM; stated changes, so own; compared with unnamed algorithms.
KSMOTE filters SMOTE output with a Kalman filter used as a cleaner; existing parts, so existing-parts; comparison read as including the SMOTE-Tomek and SMOTE-ENN named in the study.
SMOTE-RUS-NC chains neighbourhood cleaning, random undersampling and SMOTE, also inside a balanced random forest; existing parts, presented and compared with other sampling techniques.
RTS learns noise-tolerant representations, then oversamples time series from purified samples; coded own for the named purified oversampling step, though the oversampler is not described.
G-SOMO uses self-organising maps to choose areas and Geometric SMOTE to generate; parts named as standard, so existing-parts; compared with common oversamplers.
Integrates SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek using quantified noise and overlap; a chain of existing methods, presented and compared with conventional methods for noise and overlap.
HDBA-MTD seeds unnamed deep generative models with interpolation-based samples for mixed tabular data; no stated change to the deep generator, so existing-parts.
RBKWOT extracts rough-allowance borderline samples, forms K-mode clusters, weights them and generates by per-cluster rules; new oversampler; only unnamed techniques compared.
KMS_SMOTE selects SMOTE seeds near K-means centroids of the minority class to avoid marginal samples; stated change to seed selection, so own; compared with SMOTE.
GAT-RWOS interpolates along random walks guided by graph attention; new oversampler compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
A 3D grid of virtual points with inverse-distance-weighted interpolation of ion concentrations oversamples rare water samples; own generator; compared only before against after.
GAN with an auxiliary evidential classifier that guides training toward borderline minority samples; new architecture, so own; compared with unnamed popular methods.
SZ-SMOTE generates with a concentration mechanism in a hypersphere around selected minority instances; changed SMOTE compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and B-SMOTE.
An 'improved' conditional GAN whose change is not described rebalances data for a random forest; improved generator, so own; no named comparison.

Adds a kNN filter that removes synthetic points surrounded by majority neighbours to the existing NR-Clustering-SMOTE; existing method plus an ENN-like cleaner, so existing-parts; compared with NR-Clustering-SMOTE.
M-VAEGAN replaces the generator's Gaussian prior with a jointly trained mixture of Gaussians; modified generative model, so own; compared with other augmentation methods and GAN baselines.
KCPIA synthesises in a binary encoding space via Kolmogorov-complexity neighbours, crossover and mutation with a Mahalanobis constraint; new oversampler compared with other oversamplers.
EHS removes low-information majority instances in the overlap and generates informative minority instances near the border; new hybrid sampler; only unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
SEDG, a search-based generator in an embedding space; own method compared with traditional resampling methods.
OBMI oversamples only minority instances found in Tomek links, then cleans with Tomek links; a stated change to SMOTE's seed choice, so own; compared only with unnamed baselines.
Novel oversampler that builds new minority sentence vectors by adding two same-class sentence vectors; a generator of its own, compared only with the dataset's state-of-the-art score.

K-SMOTE generates minority points directly in the SVM kernel feature space by augmenting the Gram matrix; a new SMOTE variant rather than plain SMOTE in a learned space; no named resampling comparison.
RADAR uses pseudo-labels from a dual decoder to guide adaptive node oversampling, a new way of oversampling beyond GraphSMOTE; results only against unnamed prior methods.
SWIM is a new synthetic oversampling framework that uses majority-class density (Mahalanobis, RBF) to guide generation; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
Proposes an improved SMOTE (change not described) as the preprocessing stage of an IIoT intrusion detection model, which the codebook counts as own; compared only with detection methods.
CoCo-GAN uses a standard conditional GAN to make minority samples inside a defect-prediction framework, with no stated change to the generator; compared only with SDP models.
RE-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant with radius-estimated generation for safe samples and WENN/density cleaning; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Hybrid re-sampling applies SMOTE (with NCR per keywords) after Isomap dimension reduction, an existing sampler in a learned space; reported superior to plain re-sampling.
GDG clusters minority data with GMM, allocates synthetic samples by boundary complexity and generates them by GA search in superspheres; a new oversampler; baselines not named as resamplers.
GBSS couples a conditional GAN with semi-supervised learners in a triple network optimising a newly defined objective, a new architecture and loss; compared only with semi-supervised learners.

WGAN-VDE adds density-aware targeted generation and sample refinement to a WGAN, read as a changed sampling; it could instead be a plain WGAN plus a density filter; compared with 11 rebalancing techniques.

Two-stage text-conditioned video diffusion combining 2D latent diffusion with added temporal attention layers and rejection sampling, a new architecture; evaluated only with and without synthetic videos.
A conditional GAN applied in an ISOMAP-reduced space with no stated change to the GAN; standard generator in a learned space; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
ENSY is a newly named probability-distribution-based synthesizer whose parts the abstract does not show to be standard; compared with ROS, SMOTE-NC and CTGAN.
Introduces its own spatio-temporal statistics-driven time-frequency augmentation module for minority sleep stages inside a staging network; compared only with SOTA staging models.
Applies standard SMOTE to the training and DSEL sets of the existing DES-KNN ensemble, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Proposes four new SMOTE extensions (distance, Dirichlet, feature-correlation/perturbation, BGMM) for time series; compared with standard SMOTE and baselines.
AD-GSMOTE is a new graph SMOTE with an adaptive topology-aware node generator and triadic edge generator; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
MCDO-BR is a new multiclass cluster-based diversity oversampler with boundary refinement; better than unnamed alternative methods.
New adaptive oversampler that generates within hyperplanes under a Gaussian prior with multi-objective error-bound optimisation; evaluated only by classifier improvement.
Fuzzy-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant that generates more samples in the fuzzy region; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
CCO is a new cluster-core oversampler that generates within convex hulls of minority clusters; compared with unnamed cutting-edge algorithms.
Searches optimal per-class SMOTE ratios with an SVR model, a search for how much to oversample; compared only with previous approaches.
Proposes DI-SDG, perturbation-based generation within physics-derived feature-specific limits (range-constrained); evaluated alongside SMOTE.
KA-Ensemble combines random undersampling and existing Kernel-ADASYN inside the EasyEnsemble framework, a new name over standard parts; compared with state-of-the-art sampling methods.

SMOTE-VAR, a newly named oversampler that uses Gaussian-process variance to judge the uncertainty of generated minority samples (a new criterion, not an existing cleaner); better than existing oversampling approaches.
New minority oversampler for mixed numeric/nominal features with its own distance measures and coordinate calculation for synthetic samples; discusses diverse oversampling methods.
Title names a Confidence SMOTE that uses a per-minority-point confidence score with SMOTE, read as a newly named SMOTE variant; it may only be filtering plus standard SMOTE in an FSVM pipeline.
ConvGeN, a new deep generative model that learns convex-combination coefficients of minority samples; compared with deep generative models and LoRAS/ProWRAS.
Study that oversamples specific example types within each class independently, a new multiclass allocation of synthetic examples; compared with standard multi-class preprocessing.
NKI generates synthetic samples in hyper-spheres around selected minority instances as part of IM-NKA, a new oversampler; compared with four oversampling methods.
New genetic-algorithm-based synthetic data generator with designed fitness and initialisation; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, GAN and VAE.
MACO, a new manifold-guided oversampler with adaptive class-wise weights and neighbourhood-guided interpolation; outperforms traditional and state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
GAN conditioned on genuine transactions and trained with poisoning-inspired losses to make boundary frauds, a new conditioning and loss; no comparison stated.
CycleGAN-M adds a multi-scale attention mechanism to CycleGAN to make minority disease images, a modified generator; comparisons only between YOLO-type detectors.
Syn_Gen_Min, a new oversampler for raw categorical data using greedy neighbours under several categorical similarity measures; compares similarity measures, not other resamplers.

A new oversampler assembled from key steps of existing methods and fitted to each dataset by optimisation, presented as a new sampler rather than a choice among samplers; compared with well-known samplers.
InCuBAtE, a new iterative classifier-based oversampling algorithm for ordinal imbalanced data; balancing techniques and earlier work are compared.
SMOTE-OB uses a new sketched version of SMOTE within online bagging for drifting streams, a changed SMOTE; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art.
GA-SDA generates minority examples with a genetic algorithm whose fitness joins F1 and distributional similarity, a new generator; compared with SMOTE.
MLSIN, a new multi-label synthetic oversampler using label imbalance rates and neighbourhood distribution; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Image SMOTE only adds Gaussian noise to minority images, standard augmentation under a new name; compared with synthetic feature vectors; survival-group prediction.
Oversamples the minority class in Gaussian-kernel space and maps synthetic points back by pre-image computation, a new kernel-space sampling method; no resampling comparison.
NBG combines BALO feature selection with NPSMOTE, a novel SMOTE variant; compared with unnamed existing algorithms.
Potential Anchoring positions synthetic and retained points by optimising a new RBF-based potential resemblance loss; outperforms state-of-the-art resampling algorithms.

RFMSE sets the M-SMOTE oversampling rate from the random forest misclassification rate and iterates with an MCC stop before ENN, a search for how much to oversample; compared with unnamed traditional algorithms.
D-Self-SMOTE joins self-training, SMOTE and a density-based noise filter, parts that read as standard under a new name; compared methods are not named as resamplers.
CIR, a novel class imbalance reduction algorithm based on distribution properties; compared with SMOTE and K-Means SMOTE.
GDRS selects anchors by weighted Chebyshev distance and samples Gaussians around them, then random undersampling, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed imbalanced learning methods.
Weighted SMOTE adds random-forest feature weighting to the Euclidean distance in SMOTE, a changed SMOTE; compared with standard SMOTE.
CI-ASMOTE1/2 synthesise only within connected minority sub-clusters near the boundary, with a diversity extension; new SMOTE variants compared with SMOTE and its extensions.
New oversampler with kNN-distance noise detection, boundary-risk weight allocation and a neighbour class-sensitive coefficient; outperforms well-known oversampling approaches.
PL-SMOTE sets multiclass resampling amounts from a power-law prevalence model with a modulating factor, a new multiclass allocation; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Three hybrid strategies each combine two existing samplers (SMOTE+Random_SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek+MSMOTE, CBSO+ProWSyn); compared with their constituent methods.
ASCPF, a newly named balancing method that changes how samples are created and retained by class proportion (details vague); compared with SMOTE and NearMiss.

Novel hierarchical VAE with diffusion architecture that uses the majority (healthy) distribution to learn the damaged class, a new generative model; compared with conventional and recent oversampling.
Distributed SMOTE built from scalable k-means++ partitioning and M-tree neighbour search around standard SMOTE, an implementation of existing parts; compared with the Python SMOTE.
Replaces the agglomerative clustering inside MWMOTE with BIRCH and adds random undersampling, a stated change to an existing oversampler; compared with the original method.
SIM-GEN, a new simulation-based generative oversampler producing abnormal-operation data from dynamic process models with HAZOP pseudo-labels; outperforms conventional resampling techniques.
New borderline oversampling performed in the SVM feature space; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and borderline over-sampling.

Oversampling followed by a new iterative partitioning filter built on new interval-valued (intuitionistic) fuzzy KNN classifiers and voting rule, a cleaner of its own; compared with SMOTE and its generalisations.
Proposes an improved G-MSMOTE geometric oversampler for multiple minority classes within an encrypted classification framework; evaluated only before vs after.
Rel-MOSS adds a relation-guided minority synthesizer on relation-gated GNN representations, a new oversampler; compared with RDL methods and unnamed classic imbalance methods.
Synthetic-MixUp is described as mixing document vectors, yet the results report only ROS and SMOTE with Naive Bayes; cannot tell whether the generator is new, mixup or standard oversampling.
BOS locates borderline minority instances with new K generalised Tomek links and generates adaptively, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed typical methods.
GANified-SMOTE with latent factors, a newly named GAN-SMOTE hybrid whose mechanism is not described, read as own; could be a plain GAN+SMOTE chain; only classifiers compared.
UCPMOT, a newly named safe-level oversampler with its own lowest-versus-highest multiclass scheme on MapReduce; benchmarking techniques not named as resamplers.

A new HMM generator sampling constrained synthetic data from per-score Gaussian emissions feeds one ensemble member; read as own, though it is close to plain class-wise Gaussian sampling; compared with SMOTE.
YOGA-GAN adapts the discriminator to also predict injury risk while generating rare postures, a stated architecture change; compared only with deep learning models.

Class- and regime-wise GMM sampling followed by physics-constrained distance-based quality control, read as a standard generator plus a filter; borderline with physics-constrained generation; compared with SMOTE+XGBoost.
REPEAT trains the oversampling autoencoder recursively with a dynamically weighted loss, a modified generative model; no comparison with other resampling stated.
MPDA combines oversampling-strategy selection, a GAN with no stated change and fuzzy-sampling strategy selection, a choice among existing samplers plus a standard generator; only before vs after.
CRmix is a new Mixup variant that restricts patch location and restores minority labels for patch-mixed samples; compared with Mixup, Remix and CutMix.
Plain KDE sampling of the minority class with no stated change, a standard generator of the B2 list; compared with SMOTE.
LNE chooses over- and undersampling intensities per neighbourhood type by evolutionary optimisation, a new allocation of resampling; compared with SOTA resampling strategies.
Proposes federated SMOTE synchronization across institutions as one part of an FL framework, read as a new way of applying SMOTE though undescribed; compared only with FL frameworks.
Modifies GAMO by adding an attention mechanism (with fuzzy C-means) to oversample IoT intrusion data, a modified generative model; compared only with state-of-the-art NIDS.
MOKAS generates synthetic instances from kernel adaptive-subspace SOMs and reconstructs their pre-images, a new oversampler; outperforms state-of-the-art oversampling algorithms.
AGGAN recasts GAN training as an evolutionary process with simulated-annealing acceptance, a new training scheme; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Chains a standard class-conditional VAE with ADASYN, with no stated change to either; standard generator of the B2 list; evaluated only by improvement.
RMCSID finds a condensed set by cooperative coevolution and uses it for over- and undersampling, a new resampling method; compared with classical resampling methods.
Standard SMOTE applied in the second stage of a hierarchical 1D-CNN, which needs less synthetic data; contribution is the classifier framework; compared only with SVM and RF.
EMSMOTE uses standard SMOTE to make several synthetic datasets for an ensemble, a new name over standard parts; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Boost-BFKO generates minority samples with an adaptive Balanced Feature Knockout procedure inside boosting, read as a newly named generator; no comparison stated.
BO-SCAO guides neighbour selection and generation by a Bayesian-optimised semantic/complexity distance, a new oversampler; baselines (incl. LTRUS) not described as resamplers.
Stacks models trained on existing sampling strategies, existing samplers inside an ensemble; experiments analyse the individual sampling techniques, read as a comparison.
RABot interpolates minority embeddings within local subgraphs, read as a new neighbourhood-aware graph oversampler; could be plain SMOTE in a learned space; baselines unnamed.
SCOS generates samples inside searchlight structures stopped by the majority area, a new oversampler; outperforms state-of-the-art over-sampling methods.
Vibration SMOTE synthesises in a frequency-domain hyperspace after CF-VMD and statistical filtering, a new SMOTE variant; only class-separability gains reported.
CE-SMOTE selects cluster-boundary minority samples by a cluster-ensemble consistency index before oversampling, a new SMOTE variant; no comparison stated.
PC-SMOTE pairs SMOTE with a new percolation clustering algorithm of its own, not an existing clustering; compared with K-means and DBSCAN combined with SMOTE.
SDCGAN feeds the CGAN generator strengthened distribution information from curated and augmented minority samples, a new conditioning; surpasses 13 resampling techniques.
OHIT finds minority modes by density-ratio SNN clustering and samples Gaussians with shrinkage covariance, a new structure-preserving oversampler rather than plain GMM sampling; no comparison stated.
MeanFlow-IDS, a newly named lightweight flow-matching variant with one-hot projection and stabilisers, read as own; could be a standard flow model plus filters; compared with SMOTE.
Proposes a modified SMOTE-ENC (change not described) within a deep ensemble architecture; compared with ROS, RUS, Tomek links and SMOTE.
Improved SMOTE generating minority activities by Euclidean-distance neighbourhood placement instead of linear interpolation; outperforms traditional SMOTE.
AHOBENN builds hyperspheres around borderline minority points with gravitation-based weights and DE relocation of noise, a new oversampler; compared with nine oversampling methods.
Proposes an improved LR-SMOTE using multiple samples and random smoothing means within a domain-adaptive IDS; no resampling comparison stated.
Novel oversampling technique for binary-feature malware data combined with fuzzy and dynamic class weighting; competing methods unnamed.
Quantum-SMOTE generates synthetic points by swap tests and quantum rotation instead of kNN interpolation, a new SMOTE variant; only classifiers and synthetic proportions varied.
Oversampling with restricted Boltzmann machines, a standard neural generator with no stated change; compared only with unnamed commonly used techniques.
EEGAug composes new minority samples from frequency bands of several minority samples, a new augmentation method; compared with other data augmentation methods.
Evaluates five mixup-style embedding augmentations and introduces conditioned versions that keep the vulnerable section unchanged, a stated change; compared with random oversampling.
NC-SMOTE synthesises within a safe sector near the minority centre, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE.
Reinforcement-learning oversampler that produces samples targeted to the downstream classifier and metric, a new generator; no named comparison.
Designs ML-SMOTE, a new SMOTE for imbalanced multi-label data, used in the MLAMP classifier; no resampling comparison stated.
EXOT synthesises positives around originals using extreme and negative anomalous scores, a new parameter-free oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and Safe-level SMOTE.
Improved AC-WGAN-GP with class-aware sampling, label embedding and modified generator, discriminator and classifier, a modified generative model; no comparison stated.
CTGAN augmentation with relaxed feature bounds for some training points and silhouette filtering, read as a standard generator plus data tweaks and a filter, inside a prediction and XAI framework.
Applies standard SMOTE after PCA or convolutional-autoencoder feature extraction, an existing sampler in a learned space; CAE+SMOTE compared with PCA+SMOTE.
New noise-robust oversampler for mixed-type multiclass data with in-cluster noise removal, adaptive embedding and a safe boundary; no comparison stated.
WGAN-GP with threshold optimisation added in the generator, a stated change; compared with SMOTE and five GAN-based models.
New embedding-space oversampler driven by instance hardness and adversarial-neighbourhood variance control; compared with unnamed similar approaches.
IFE-SMOTE generates near three strategic points per triangulated element, an improved FE-SMOTE; compared with FE-SMOTE and other oversampling algorithms.
New oversampler with position-based noise filtering, relative-density weighting and nearest-neighbour area control; compared with state-of-the-art sampling methods.
Adversarial-guided oversampling steered by decision trees and neural networks, read as a newly named generator; details are vague and it may be a GAN plus validation; only before vs after.
RIOT selects hard minority instances by region impurity and generates until regions balance, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE extensions.
Selects minority seeds from examples misclassified by a bagged ensemble and oversamples them with a SMOTE variant, a new allocation; compared with SMOTE.
ASMOTE-ENN chains adaptive SMOTE with ENN cleaning before a hybrid ensemble, existing parts; compared only before vs after and with unnamed fault diagnosis techniques.
DEAHS uses MDP-guided adaptive undersampling and entropy-based weighted oversampling in overlap regions inside boosting, a new resampling scheme; no resampling comparison stated.
GAME extends the sampling margin in generative and adversarial phases by tuning a local linear model toward the majority class, a new generator; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

RE-SMOTEBoost adds roulette-wheel generation in overlap regions, an entropy filter and a double regularisation penalty to SMOTEBoost, a changed SMOTE method; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
STESO applies standard SMOTE to sentence-transformer embeddings of tabular data, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with oversampling alone.
SANSA, a new synthetic average neighbourhood sampler with a tunable placement parameter; tested against seven existing sampling methods.
ICSPMH partitions the space into balanced subspaces with its own metaheuristic (SPMH) so SMOTE is needed little or not at all, a new allocation of oversampling; compared with unnamed approaches.
Fits a plain GMM to the minority complaints and samples from it, a standard generator of the B2 list with no stated change; contrasted with SMOTE.
Decoupled latent diffusion for mask and image generation with a novel proportion-aware loss on generated masks, a new loss; comparisons only across segmentation models.
Proposes restrained WGAN structures (IWGAN, MWGAN, SWGAN) guided by a new SRC indicator, new architectures; compared with SMOTE and other GANs.
OSDD, a newly named oversampler using diversified distributions whose change is barely described; compared with an unnamed approach.
MIX-NOISE GAN feeds the generator a mixture of GMM-derived and random noise against mode collapse, a stated change to the generator input; compared with six classical sampling methods.
ACo-MO picks hard examples by boosting and adapts the interpolation range with the minority global distribution, a new multiclass oversampler; compared with unnamed imbalanced classification methods.
Diffusion fine-tuning with an explicit class constraint plus classifier-likelihood filtering of fundus images, read as a stated training change; only before vs after reported.
CWOS-Ord clusters minority classes and oversamples by distance and ordinal relations with complexity-based sizes, a new oversampler for ordinal classes; compared with unnamed methods.
D-SMOTE interpolates uniformly inside a closed area of three nearest abnormal samples, a new SMOTE variant; comparisons only across machine learning methods.
Pattern_Syn generates minority patterns by overlap pattern synthesis, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE.
DG-GCN balances the graph by plain interpolation of minority nodes in latent space, an existing sampler in a learned space; contribution is the GCN; compared with unnamed methods.
EHSEL uses information entropy to choose majority samples in undersampling and limits oversampling to subset size within an ensemble, a new hybrid sampling method; no comparison stated.
AMD-GAN decouples the architecture per class and adapts optimisation to class cardinality, a new architecture and training; compared with ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
SD-CSMOTE clusters minority data by SNN-DPC, allocates samples by KDE density and generates at three-sample centroids, a new SMOTE variant; compared with 10 sampling methods.
Feature-guided LLM text augmentation with no stated change to the language model, a standard generator of the B2 list; compared only with imbalanced baselines.
MeanRadius-SMOTE, a new SMOTE variant that avoids useless and noise samples; compared with SMOTE and LR-SMOTE.
E-SMOTE uses entropy to choose boundary minority seeds and oversamples only that subset, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE.
OALDPC adds a new local density peaks clustering, noise filter, sampling weight and interpolation, a new oversampler; outperforms 8 oversampling techniques.

Contextual augmentation applied to tweets chosen by a new non-random relevance criterion, read as a new way of building synthetic threads; could be standard augmentation plus selection; compared with random selection.
Modified real-value negative selection detectors with supervision and crowding-density weights for multiclass oversampling, a new oversampler; compared with seven oversampling algorithms.
Optimised version of the authors' rough-granular oversampler that generates in difficulty-aware areas with ambiguity filtering; compared with SMOTE.
EmDT, a diffusion model with UMAP-clustered conditioning and a Transformer denoiser with positional embeddings, a new architecture; compared with oversampling and generative methods.
Combines standard SMOTE with decision thresholding and removal of misclassified borderline majority instances, read as existing parts; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Develops AnnSMOTE, a new SMOTE with adaptive nearest neighbours for drifting streams, inside dynamic ensemble selection; compared with unnamed methods.
GAN whose generative process is optimised by the shuffled frog leaping algorithm and adapted toward misclassified samples, a stated training change; compared with unnamed algorithms.
Conditional DDPM generates vibration data with no stated change to the diffusion model (novelty is the improved CNN); compared with seven augmentation methods; B2 applies.
New resampling that over- and undersamples with synthetic prototypes from class-specific subclustering; better than classical random resampling.
A strategy of majority reduction and synthetic minority generation with no detail in the abstract (keywords hint at Weibull sampling); cannot tell whether it is new; compared with unnamed methods.
Metaheuristics (Bat, PSO) search the Random-SMOTE rebalancing parameters jointly with feature selection, a search for how much to oversample; compared with unnamed conventional methods.
Designs a new extrapolation Borderline-SMOTE used in bagged SVMs (BEBS); no named comparison.
Weighted-Distance SMOTE with an improved interpolation strategy for line-graph NIDS data, a new SMOTE variant; compared with an unnamed baseline.
RUROForest/SROForest combine random undersampling or SMOTE with rotation forest, existing samplers inside an ensemble; compared with unnamed ensemble methods.
SEMRes-DDPM uses a new SEMST-ResNet denoising network for tabular diffusion, a new architecture; compared with TabDDPM, CWGAN-GP and SOTA oversamplers.
CutMix with a new balanced sampling strategy and minority-biased label assignment, a changed augmentation; compared with unnamed imbalance strategies.
Adaptive geometric SMOTE with attention levels and adaptive generation areas, a new SMOTE variant; compared with unnamed traditional methods.
IA-KNNR, a new multi-label resampling framework with distance-weighted KNN, label similarity and co-occurrence weighting; compared with unnamed approaches.
Develops NMOTe, a newly named oversampler (change not described), for a CNN-GRU fraud detector; compared only with deep learning classifiers.
IFSMOTE, a fractal-based oversampler presented as the paper's own for image annotation; compared with SMOTE and FSMOTE.
ASE-Bagging integrates standard SMOTE with bagging, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble under a new name; no comparison stated.
SMOTE combined with a new intuitionistic fuzzy rough instance selection that cleans both classes, a cleaner of its own; no comparison with other resampling stated.
3D-GIGAMO embeds a guided implicit neural representation in adversarial learning with a bounded-score objective and class-consistency loss, a new generator; compared with unnamed methods.
Applies SMOTE to high-confidence pseudo-labels and adds data with class-adaptive sampling rates, read as a new allocation for black-box domain adaptation; only before vs after.

On-the-fly image oversampling with an instance-based generator seeded by uncertain boundary samples, read as a new method; generator may be standard with seed selection; compared with unnamed approaches.
TarDiff embeds influence-function gradients into reverse diffusion, a new guided sampling; compared with unnamed existing methods.
Two-stage schedule of image-space oversampling then feature-space undersampling for fine-tuning, a chain of existing resampling steps; no comparison stated.
CT-TabGAN redesigns the generator with TabNet-aware structuring and an improved conditional sampling module, a modified generator; outperforms traditional oversampling.
imDEF uses the OREMG generator plus error-aware and margin-aware self-paced sampling ensembles of its own, read as own resampling schemes; no comparison stated.
ECO-Ensemble uses a novel cluster-based generation method with evolutionary parameter optimisation, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed ensemble algorithms.
Improves SMOTE to oversample in Hilbert space with PSO-set adaptive rates (Border-Kernel-SMOTE), a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.
Each ensemble member uses random undersampling and SMOTE toward a random target class size, existing samplers inside an ensemble; baselines unnamed.

ADBoost pairs an unchanged Adversarial Random Forest generator with its own Double-Random-Forest leaf-removal undersampling inside reweighted boosting, read as a hybrid scheme of its own; compared with boosting methods.
New oversampler that recasts minority data as a time series and samples from a fitted ARIMA model, not a standard tabular generator; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
DSMOTE uses an optimised DBSCAN to split minority samples into core, borderline and noise with separate oversampling strategies, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
ASN-SMOTE filters noise and adaptively selects qualified neighbours inside the majority boundary, a new SMOTE variant; compared with nine oversampling algorithms.
