Spatial-SMOTE upsamples spatial time series while retaining location information, a new SMOTE variant; no comparison with other resampling stated.
CUSS pairs SMOTE with a newly designed cluster-based undersampler and a new rule for the expected instance number; compared with five popular resampling methods.
Feature-guided, prompt-engineered LLM text augmentation with no stated change to the language model, a standard generator of the B2 list; compared with oversampling.
Proposes a part-synthetic oversampling (PSOS) strategy (change not described) with ROS/RUS ensemble members; outperforms traditional data balancing approaches.
TRPS-DER interpolates in triangular regions and filters noise by differential evolution resampling, a new oversampler; outperforms SMOTE-based oversampling methods.
Clusters the data into regions, applies standard oversampling and trains random forests, clustering then standard SMOTE; only simulation effectiveness reported.
ReMAHA, an innovative weighted-Mahalanobis oversampler with Relief-F weights and a genetic algorithm, a new oversampler; outperforms other oversampling algorithms.
Two hard-constraint modules select GAN-type synthetic samples by medical semantics and informativeness, a standard generator followed by filters; only before vs after.
V-GAN trains the GAN on virtual big data made by concatenating instances, a stated training change; compared with standard GANs and traditional oversampling.
Standard SMOTE (or any generator) followed by density-based penalty weights for synthetic samples in AdaBoost; the novelty is the boosting weight scheme; no comparison stated.
KSMOTE splits data by k-means and applies over- and undersampling per cluster with random forests, k-means then standard SMOTE; compared with SMOTE.
TDMO filters noise by XGBoost confidence and combines multiple samples in multi-dimensional space, a new oversampler; outperforms comparative oversampling methods.
CFAMG creates minority samples by counterfactual swapping of disentangled causal factors and a minority decoder, a new generative method; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
SMOTE followed by a newly named OSBNR noise-reduction module for overlapping majority instances, a cleaner of its own; surpasses state-of-the-art sampling methods.
Adaptive optimal-transport image mixing for minority classes, a new mixup variant; no comparison with other augmentation stated.
Proposes specific over-sampling techniques that exploit the partial-order class structure in melanoma staging; compared only with classifiers.
Filter extension of SMOTE using an optimised SVM kernel trick to control generation in overlap, a changed SMOTE; outperforms SMOTE and RC-SMOTE.
MOSS is a new oversampler that picks candidates by sensitivity to imbalance and interpolates; compared with seven oversampling methods.
Proposes an unnamed novel oversampling technique for mineral prospect mapping with no detail on how samples are generated, so the method cannot be judged.
Clustering-based oversampler that sets how many points to generate per minority sample from its distance to the cluster centroid (new allocation); compared with other synthetic resampling techniques.
AH-CGAN modifies a conditional GAN with an adaptive gradient-penalty schedule and a feature-matching loss; results are reported only as before against after augmentation.

A denoising autoencoder algorithm that oversamples through misclassification cost and then denoises; the abstract does not say whether the oversampling step is standard or new; compared with a DAE using an oversampling process.
Kernel-based SMOTE runs standard SMOTE in the kernel feature space and maps the samples back by pre-images, i.e. an existing sampler applied in a transformed space; compared with SMOTE.
New oversampler that fits a majority-aware support vector domain description to the minority class and samples from it; the abstract names no comparison with other resampling.
GAMCGSA uses a genetic algorithm to search the optimal SMOTE sampling rate (a search for how much to oversample); comparisons are only with models such as TabNet and RF.
Borderline-PC SMOTE restricts synthetic records to prescribed process bounds (range-constrained generation) as part of the framework; compared only with conventional BP without resampling.
EMA-GAN is a new GAN architecture with multi-scale attention, a frequency-domain loss and adaptive training balance; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and random oversampling.
WISEST is a new locality-aware weighted-interpolation SMOTE variant with thresholds; the abstract reports it against other samplers and alternatives.
NOSTE is a new oversampler (noise removal, density and distance weights, averaging of two minority instances); compared with four popular oversampling methods.
MLSOL and MLUL are new multi-label over- and undersampling methods based on a new local label imbalance measure; the abstract names no comparison with other sampling methods.
Proposes and compares several strategies for choosing seed samples when applying SMOTE to multi-label data, a new way of applying SMOTE; the strategies are compared with each other.
Novel adversarial framework (feature extractor, generator, discriminator) trained on normal data that generates unseen fault classes by changing the generator condition; no comparison is named.
EB-Smote is a new borderline SMOTE variant that oversamples both classes between selected minority and majority samples; compared with eight oversampling methods.

An improved (modified) CWGAN-GP is part of the proposed diagnostic method; the change is not described but the codebook counts an improved generator as own; no comparison with other resampling is named.
FCM-CSMOTE is a new SMOTE variant generating samples within fuzzy c-means clusters using the cluster centre; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
Modified GAN whose generator takes KPCA and SMOTE pattern vectors instead of noise, with self-attention and a data filter; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
The latent space sampling stage applies standard SMOTE to learned IndoBERT embeddings (existing sampler in a latent space); results are compared only with standard fine-tuning baselines.
NCGAN is a new GAN that calibrates synthetic positive samples against negative samples; compared only with an unnamed traditional method.
C-SMOTE ensembles classifiers trained at different SMOTE rates to find the optimal rate automatically (a search for how much to oversample); no comparison with other resampling is named.
ARS-sampling is a newly named adaptive neighbourhood-based oversampler presented as one component of the IDS framework; only comparative and ablation studies of the framework are mentioned.
AceNet applies standard SMOTE to learned features before classifier refinement (existing sampler in a learned space); compared only with unnamed existing approaches.
A-SUWO is a new clustering-based weighted oversampler with adaptive per-cluster sizes; compared with other sampling methods.
RA-SMOTE is a newly named region adaptive SMOTE variant; it is tested with three classifiers but no other resampling method is named as a comparison.
OUPS is a newly named oversampler using propensity scores, not shown to be a mere chain of PSM and SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and PSM.
T5C paraphrases minority sentences with an unchanged T5 language model plus WordNet and POS tagging, a standard generator in a chain (B2); compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.

K-IPO is a generator-agnostic generate-then-select filter that keeps candidates only if a Kendall tau constraint holds, so the generator is unchanged and unnamed; best or tied-best results imply comparison with existing oversampling methods.
A GAN aided by Gaussian discriminant analysis, a newly named GAN variant whose change is not detailed; compared with a common oversampling method and the basic GAN.
IMWMOTE is an improved MWMOTE oversampler for heterogeneous fault data; the abstract names no comparison with other resampling methods.
Oversampling with a plain VAE with no stated change (B2); compared with oversampling and undersampling methods.
An improved oversampling algorithm combining dependent wild bootstrap with a modified SMOTE for unfixed-length time series; no comparison with other resampling is named.
DAMO guides multiple over-sampling with a distribution-inconsistency constraint and fuses calibrated results; compared only with unnamed related methods.
The GAN generator is fed ADASYN samples instead of random noise, a stated change to its input like a new conditioning; comparisons are only with classifiers such as SVM, MLP, KNN and LGBM.
KNNOR is a new k-nearest-neighbour oversampler that considers the data distribution; it is reported against state-of-the-art augmentation algorithms.
MOOST is a new majority-oriented oversampler that generates out-of-distribution anomalous samples guided by normal data inside a deep network; no comparison with other resampling is named.
Proposes a new Peak-clustering undersampler and a new boosting algorithm combining it with SMOTE and unequal weights; only improved minority performance is reported, with no named comparison.
RAMGANH combines association-rule undersampling with a modified tabular GAN (stated as modified); compared only with an unnamed state-of-the-art method.
ANMWS is a new weighted SMOTE using expert attribute priority levels; compared with standard SMOTE.

Multi-generator GAN with independent generators specialised per failure subtype, presented as a new architecture though it may be standard GANs per subtype; compared with SMOTE, undersampling, cost-sensitive learning and a single GAN.

AdaBoost-SVM-OBFS chains ReliefF feature selection, boosting with an unnamed standard over-sampling technique and SVM retraining, a new name over standard parts; compared only with AdaBoost-SVM without resampling.
SPEAR is a multiclass scheme balancing to the average class size with k-means downsampling and Sparse PCA based upsampling not shown to be a standard sampler; compared with eight resampling methods.
SISMOTE is a new selective interpolation SMOTE variant proposed for speech emotion data; compared only with state-of-the-art recognition works.
SACTGAN adds self-attention to CTGAN (an architecture change) combined with EasyEnsemble; reported against traditional methods for handling the imbalance.
CE-LSWGAN is a new causal-constrained WGAN in VAE latent space with class-weighted resampling; generated-data similarity is compared with six state-of-the-art generation baselines.
LMCMO is a new oversampler that estimates minority spaces before generating synthetic points; compared with four competing methods not called resampling methods.
A SMOTE modification using inter-cluster centroid distances to place synthetic points; compared with previous studies that used standard oversampling methods.
HDBA-MTD combines interpolation-based oversampling with GANs with no stated change to the GAN, a chain holding a standard generator (B2); compared with other synthetic data generation techniques.
SLEO is a new oversampler with semi-supervised clustering, entropy-decay cleaning and entropy-weighted hypersphere generation; compared with 13 sampling techniques.

HypoGAN builds minority mode discovery and boundary information into latent-noise candidate generation (stated changes beyond its post-generation filter); compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
RWO-Sampling is a new oversampler creating synthetic samples by random walks from real data that keep the mean and standard deviation; compared only with unnamed alternative methods.
DSMOTE changes SMOTE with a ten-sampling split rule and a quadratic rule for the number of neighbours; compared with SMOTE.
Presents a normal distribution-based SMOTE that changes how synthetic points are placed; compared with the original SMOTE.

SVDDDPCO cleans overlap with an SVDD boundary, clusters minority data with DPC and allocates synthetic samples adaptively per sub-cluster (new allocation); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
VIRTUAL is a new adaptive oversampler that generates synthetic examples during SVM training with active learning; compared with competitive oversampling techniques.
TGT is a newly named adversarially guided oversampler that keeps synthetic samples in minority regions; how samples are generated is not stated and no resampling comparison is named.

The novel anti-imbalance scheme pairs pseudo-label generation with a weighted feature-level oversampling technique that is neither named nor described, so new or standard cannot be told; compared only with a state-of-the-art method.
AKS is a new kNN-based oversampler with adaptive neighbourhood selection and non-linearity checks; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-ENN and Borderline-SMOTE.
GAN oversampler with a novel generator training loss; compared with existing oversampling methods.

CGGReaT generates synthetic tabular data with a pre-trained DistilGPT-2 language model and no stated change, a standard generator under a new name (B2); compared only with classifiers trained on the imbalanced data.
GMM-SMOTE clusters with a Gaussian mixture and applies standard SMOTE in minority-rich clusters, a chain of existing parts; compared with KMeans-SMOTE, KMeans-ADASYN, GMM-ADASYN, SMOTE and ADASYN.
NGDSO is a new oversampler using a noise-free gradient distribution, a new neighbour concept and new sample distribution strategies; no comparison with other resampling is named.
ClustSyn combines clustering with its own Mahalanobis-distance based synthetic generation not shown to be a standard sampler; compared with RUSBoost and SMOTEBoost among others.
An adaptive SMOTE strategy that sets per-class oversampling by attack severity and rarity, a new allocation of synthetic examples; no comparison with other resampling is named.

Introduces the newly named Prompt Adaptive Oversampling (PAO) alongside LLM-prompted augmentation; PAO is not described so it counts as own by name; no resampling comparison is named and answer scores are classified.
ODBOT is a new multiclass oversampler generating samples with regard to outliers found by clustering the minority classes; it outperforms other common and state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.

Existing oversampling techniques are used to diversify base learners of a new ensemble belief rule base classifier, whose contribution lies in the classifier; compared with EBRB systems and imbalanced classifiers.

Generates node samples in the embedding space with random variables controlling the distance to target samples; the abstract does not say whether this is a standard sampler in a latent space or a new one; no comparison is named.
AEGAN-SMOTE-PSO chains an autoencoder GAN with SMOTE-PSO with no stated change to either, so the generator kind is coded (B2); compared with three oversampling techniques.
MC-NCLWO is a new multiclass oversampler with cooling-law noise cleaning, difficulty-weighted generation and class sampling priority; compared with 10 unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
The paper proposes SMOTE-TS, a newly named SMOTE for time series, as its imbalance module; results are compared only with related research accuracy.
KSMOTE is k-means clustering coupled with standard SMOTE, a chain of existing parts presented as the contribution; compared with no sampling and SMOTE.
New oversampler weighting minority line segments by the reciprocal robust Mahalanobis distance of their midpoints; compared with unnamed baseline techniques.
CSRBoost combines cluster-based undersampling, SMOTE and AdaBoost with no clearly stated change to the parts, a new name over standard parts; no comparison with other methods is named.
Distributional Random Oversampling is a new text oversampler that generates random minority documents from the distributional properties of terms; results are discussed without a named comparison.
New kernel-space synthesis rule that builds each sample from three real samples under constraints, with a stopping criterion; no comparison with other resampling is named.
G1Nos adds silhouette-based instance selection with an imbalance-degree threshold before SMOTE-like generation; it beats the other two state-of-the-art oversampling methodologies.
The ADASYN-FLS-SMOTEBoost strategy names standard parts (ADASYN, focal loss-softmax weighting, SMOTEBoost) without a clear change to how samples are made; compared only with ML and DL baselines.
wADASMO is a new weighted oversampler built on SMOTE and ADASYN with a weight adjustment to target minority areas; compared with other oversampling methods.

AutoSMOTE learns with hierarchical reinforcement learning how many synthetic samples to make and where within the SMOTE space (search and allocation); compared with state-of-the-art resampling algorithms.
Global-IC is a new oversampler that uses an artificial immune network to generate immune centroids as synthetic examples; compared with multi-class resampling methods.
Changes Safe-Level SMOTE by relocating synthetic instances away from majority instances and handling minority outcasts with 1-NN; the abstract reports F-measure gains without naming the comparison.
SMOTE followed by a stacked sparse autoencoder used to denoise the synthetic samples and a Fuzzy ARTMAP classifier, i.e. SMOTE with an autoencoder cleaner; compared with other SMOTE methods.
A GAN generates incident MI cases and a novel GAN feature-enhanced (GFE) loss is proposed, read as a new GAN loss, though it may be the predictor's loss; only the gain from the GFE loss is reported.
Proposes soft-label SMOTE and a new margin-aware Mixup, a stated change to standard mixup; the study compares SMOTE, soft SMOTE and Mixup.
FedAgriGAN is a new federated GAN with one generator and three discriminators; compared with InfoGAN, DCGAN, ViTGAN and WGAN.
SGEOM is a new oversampler using sample gradient entropy for neighbour choice and barycentric Lagrange weights for synthesis; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.

A dynamic multiclass over-sampling procedure inside a memetic algorithm that generates patterns for the minimum-sensitivity class during evolution; compared with methods using other over-sampling procedures.
A standard VAE trained on PCA-compressed acoustic features generates synthetic samples with no stated change (B2); results are before against after augmentation.
HOOST is a new oversampler combining interpolation with hyperplane-guided extrapolation to make out-of-distribution fault samples; no comparison with other resampling is named.
IS-SMOTE is a modified SMOTE with distance-based instance importance and non-fixed oversampling rates; compared with standard SMOTE.
A novel SMOTE combined with fuzzy logic using fuzzy c-means membership degrees and gap statistics, more than partitioning before standard SMOTE; no comparison is named.
Borderline Shifting is a new resampling method that selectively enhances significant borderline instances; compared with seven resampling techniques including SMOTE and NearMiss.
SCOTE is a new multiclass oversampler with binary decomposition, kNN noise filtering, LS-SVM importance ranking and k*inn synthesis; compared with 8 oversampling algorithms.

A deep forest with undersampling-based ensemble learners and an instance hardness-based oversampling technique in each layer; the abstract does not say whether that oversampler is new or standard; no comparison is named.
A hierarchical over-sampling bagging method that uses a grey wolf optimizer with SMOTE plus a new temporal sampling technique for sequences; compared only with unnamed baseline algorithms.

A multiclass framework with two approaches of its own for balancing among minority classes combined with decomposition methods, though the approaches are not described; compared with unnamed existing methods.
MRS-GNN uses a MeanRadius-SMOTE variant in the GNN embedding space plus a specialised edge generator; compared with SMOTE, oversampling and reweighting.
An improved SMOTE that generates samples inside a super-geometry of minority neighbours and narrows it near majority samples; no comparison is named.

A standard Quantum Circuit Born Machine trained by KL divergence after PCA, with no stated change to the generator (treated as a standard generator under B2); compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, KMeansSMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.
A new persistence-guided interpolation resampling that weights interpolation between minority neighbours by their structural persistence; compared only with detection methods.
B2BGAN has a new backbone-to-branches generator and a prototype-guided loss; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art models.
An adaptive kernel-SMOTE step, not claimed as new, feeds a new fuzzy twin SVM classifier inside AdaBoost; the contribution lies in the classifier and comparisons are with TSVM and fuzzy models.
GSDC is Gaussian SMOTE after density clustering, a new name over parts its name shows to be standard, used with a selective ensemble; no comparison with other resampling is named.
Hybrid augmentation chaining a furthest-neighbour SMOTE, not claimed as new, with a standard TimeGAN (B2); compared only with collision detection approaches.
A new local resampling that sets the resampling rate and number of neighbours per local region (new allocation); compared with classical resampling approaches.
New oversampler with majority hyperspheres, roulette-wheel seed selection and an overlap shift of synthetic samples; compared with well-established oversampling methods.
SMOTE-BD is a newly named exact, partition-independent distributed SMOTE for big data, a change in how SMOTE is carried out rather than in the samples; no comparison is named.
SMOTE-ICS-Bagging runs standard SMOTE in each iteration of a new classifier-selection bagging ensemble whose contribution is ensemble generation; compared with SMOTEBagging.
New oversampler choosing neighbours by manifold distance with an adaptive density-based number of new samples; no named comparison.
A new resampling approach that changes ADASYN with decision-tree boundaries to focus on rare complex cases; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
SC-GAN is a conditional GAN conditioned on key blockchain transaction features, read as a new conditioning though it may be a plain cGAN; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
GraphSMOTE synthesises nodes in a learned embedding space and adds a jointly trained edge generator for the new nodes, more than a sampler in latent space; compared with unnamed baselines.
MSMOTE is an improved SMOTE using Mahalanobis distance, part of the fault diagnosis method; the comparison is not named.
AWTDO assigns synthetic sample counts per k-means cluster via three-way decision on cluster imbalance ratios (new allocation); compared with nine oversampling methods.
NR-Clustering SMOTE is kNN noise filtering, k-means clustering and standard SMOTE per cluster, a new name over standard parts; compared only with the original imbalanced data.
WGAN-GP-BM adds a memory module of discriminator features to guide generation plus Bayesian tuning; compared with SMOTE, CGAN and WGAN.
The dissertation introduces HOVER, a newly named graph oversampling approach via edge removal, whose generation is not described; no resampling comparison is named.
CVAE_SeTred is a new CVAE architecture with two encoders and a domain classifier transferring knowledge from majority to minority; compared with unnamed comparative methods.
Hybrid GRSOM oversampling and bootstrap undersampling whose stated contribution is deciding how much to grow and reduce (a search for how much to oversample); no named comparison.
GTGAN is a new game-theoretic GAN with parallel training and ensemble voting; compared with traditional oversampling including SMOTE variants.
Heron-Centroid SMOTE synthesises at triangle centroids with Heron-based density and noise mitigation; compared with SMOTE.
EE-SMOTE selects homogeneous minority seeds for SMOTE with a new eigen-entropy metric; no comparison is named.
MSTabVAE is a new TabNet-based CVAE with multi-step latent mapping and per-step class conditioning; compared with generative and traditional oversampling baselines.
The STCAE framework includes a newly designed piecewise SMOTE (PSMOTE) for rebalancing; comparisons are with unnamed existing methods and ablations.
VAE latent points are chosen by PSO guided by the SVM margin with a diversity penalty, a stated change to how the generator samples; compared only with an unnamed baseline.
AdaptiveSMOTEGD is a new SMOTE with density-based sparsity detection, tunable Gaussian noise and constraint preservation; set against SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE, SVMSMOTE and KMeans-SMOTE.
GBCloud is a new granular-ball cloud model fitted per granular ball and used as an oversampler; compared with unnamed popular or state-of-the-art algorithms.
A novel contingency-based adaptive synthetic data generation method whose mechanism is not described; compared with ADASYN and SMOTE.

A sampling strategy that over- and undersamples according to instances misclassified by a spectral-clustering AdaBoost-SVM ensemble, read as a new allocation though the samplers are unnamed; compared with unnamed previous algorithms.

Ensemble-based SMOTE integrated into existing pixel-pair feature augmentation with no stated change; the chain holds a standard augmentation, so its kind is coded (B2); compared with CNN with K-means SMOTE among others.
A standard VAE oversamples minority nodes from GAT embeddings, a standard generator in a learned space (B2); compared with conventional oversampling techniques.
Generative oversampling of BERT embeddings with f-VAEGAN-D2 whose discriminator the authors state they adapted to text embeddings, read as a stated change though slight; no comparison is named.
Improved hybrid sampling with physically constrained synthetic oversampling and anomaly-detection-based undersampling (physics-constrained generation); results are before against after sampling.
Fed-DynamicSMOTE is a newly designed federated dynamic sampling algorithm built on K-means SMOTE whose dynamic part is not described; compared only with centralized and federated methods.
A new crossover-based oversampler generating minority text samples for genetic programming; compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
FRIPS is a new fuzzy-rough prototype selection with a wrapper threshold that cleans noise before SMOTE (a new cleaner, not an existing one); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
AWLT-GAN embeds an adaptive wavelet-like transform layer in the generator and uses dual discriminators (new architecture); no comparison with other resampling is named.
T-SMOTE is a new temporal SMOTE that generates border samples and weighted synthetic samples for time series; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
A new class-dependent resampling that over- and undersamples by taking different numbers of vertical spectrogram slices per class; compared with random undersampling.
DBSCAN-based noise removal followed by a CGAN with an adaptively modified Wasserstein loss (new loss); compared with five classical oversampling methods.
MRS-GNN integrates the newly named MeanRadius-SMOTE into a GNN to synthesise node representations; compared only with unnamed traditional and popular methods.
A plain DCGAN generates minority fault data with no stated change (B2); compared with multiple resampling algorithms.
Explores an unsupervised GAN and a semi-supervised modality-synthesis GAN for oversampling with no stated change to either; compared with classic data augmentation.
GMF-SMOTE groups data by an EM Gaussian mixture, filters noisy and boundary samples and designs two dynamic oversampling ratios (new allocation); compared with traditional oversampling algorithms.
A multiclass big-data framework that embeds instance-level difficulty into resampling plus a novel distributed SMOTE version; shown to improve on resampling without instance-level information.
A standard Gaussian process regressor generates artificial failure sequences with no stated change (B2); results are before against after adding samples.
A novel noise filter over-sampling approach with AdaBoost whose filter and oversampler are not named or described; compared with RUSBoost and SMOTEBoost.
MK-SMOTE and M-SMOTE are new oversamplers, the latter creating instances iteratively by calculated probabilities; compared with K-Means SMOTE.

CorLabelNet proposes an oversampling approach that uses learned label correlations to pick crucial seed samples (a new way of applying oversampling); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
WSSMOTE is a new watershed-transformation based SMOTE; the abstract contrasts it with existing oversampling methods that fail to raise PPV.

A new framework that generates samples on a learned manifold (PCA or autoencoder) chosen by manifold conformance estimation; the in-manifold sampler is not named, so it might be read as an existing sampler in a learned space; no named comparison.
EMOTE is a new oversampler that oversamples the nearest neighbours of misclassified minority instances; compared with SMOTE and other over- and undersampling methods.
Ad-RuLer adapts the RuLer rule-learning algorithm into a new rule-driven data synthesis oversampler; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Tomek links, Borderline-SMOTE and KMeansSMOTE.
CHDS is a new oversampler generating with a Dirichlet strategy inside safe Delaunay triangles of boundary convex hulls; compared with 15 resampling methods.
Proposes a KD-tree classifier together with a variation of SMOTE for Spark, a changed SMOTE presented as a contribution; no named comparison.
e-SMOTE extends SMOTE with the move-split-merge elastic distance for time series; compared with generic and time-series rebalancing strategies.
Four enhanced SMOTE variants with kNN attribute weights from mutual information and entropies; compared only with unnamed previous methods.
New oversampler that learns a constraint-based causal network and perturbs causal features to synthesise minority samples, with a selection estimator; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
PacketCGAN is a standard conditional GAN conditioned on application type under a new name (B2); compared with ROS, SMOTE and vanilla GAN.
A new oversampling technique that extracts extra minority patches from homogeneous regions of stitched whole-slide images within a CAD system; compared only with existing models.
ESMOTE4Graph has its own node generator with added randomness, feature and neighbour selection and an edge generator; compared with unnamed models.
IA-SUWO improves A-SUWO with a sparsity factor for sub-cluster sample counts; compared with baseline oversampling techniques.
New hybrid resampling with similarity-biased synthesis and variation-coefficient boundary undersampling; compared with unnamed algorithms.
SSMNFOS adds a new stochastic-sensitivity noise filter (neural network ensemble) before oversampling; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

ITS-JiT maps signals to an interpretable space, samples there with a minimalist JiT-based conditional backbone and decodes interpretably (a new generator design); compared with conventional augmentation.
CSS oversamples with Gaussian noise around support vectors and undersamples by improved density-peak clustering with stratified sampling; compared with state-of-the-art sampling methods.

WOA-Oversampling runs an existing oversampler and then picks the best training subset with the whale optimization algorithm, a separate selection on standard output; compared with four oversampling methods.
An improved adaptive synthetic over-sampling model with variance-distance closeness and neighbour pairs, paired with a fuzzy neighbourhood feature selection; compared with unnamed related algorithms.
Uses a contrastive VAE that draws on majority and minority data for oversampling with no stated change to the model; no comparison is named.
A new oversampling approach that creates minority samples per data chunk by imputation methods, with a firefly-optimised ensemble for drifting streams; compared only with unnamed existing methods.

A large quantum restricted Boltzmann machine embedded on D-Wave hardware generates attack samples; the novelty is the hardware embedding, not a change to the generator (B2); compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
Evaluates standard VAE, AE, GAN and a hybrid AE-GAN with no stated change for fraud oversampling (B2); compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
Proposes the Histogram Augmentation Technique (HAT) as a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE-XGBoost.
OTASMM is a newly proposed adaptive multiclass oversampler for vibration signals feeding a transfer-learning CNN; results are before against after oversampling.

The SAEO module of the fraud-detection GNN interpolates between neighbours in the positive-class embedding space, a standard interpolation in a learned space under a new name; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
LAD-SMOTE is a new SMOTE based on a locally adaptive distance that also oversamples non-borderline informative samples; compared with unnamed existing ones.
WOA-IA is a new image augmentation combining images with WOA-optimised edge maps placed by an angular model, not a standard augmentation; compared with standard edge-based augmentation.
An improved SMOTE preprocessing, change not described, used with a new IIBK classifier; compared only with classifiers J48, IBK and SVM.
Proposes three surrounding-neighbourhood variants of SMOTE that account for proximity and spatial distribution; compared with SMOTE.
R-GDORUS picks anchor samples by density and distance and generates new samples from a Gaussian distribution, with random undersampling; compared with five mainstream imbalance-handling methods.
A new approach that oversamples with genetic mutation and crossover operators and then cleans both classes by clustering; no comparison is named.
A new two-stage iterative ensemble balancing method for multiclass data whose working is not described; compared with two widely used oversampling techniques.
An improved WGAN-GP with residual connections in the generator (architecture change); no comparison with other resampling is named.
Studies chains of standard SMOTE and a standard GAN, including the proposed GANified-SMOTE, with no stated change to either part (B2); compared with SMOTE and GAN.
Feature-weighted adaptive boundary oversampling that sets per-sample synthetic factors (new allocation); compared with seven sampling methods.
Proposes a hypervector oversampling technique in hyperdimensional federated learning, not described further; compared only with HD computing frameworks.
No abstract; the title names PROSTENN, a proxipair-based oversampler with stacked noise removal, which suggests a new method.
AICGAN adds an auxiliary discrimination layer to the CGAN discriminator and mixes interpolation with generator samples; no comparison is named.
A standard VAE sampled in the crash region of its latent space with no stated change (B2); compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and a GAN.
New graph-based ordinal over-sampling for ordinal regression; compared only with a cost-sensitive ordinal SVM, not another resampler.
SVMSMOTE-ENC modifies SMOTE-ENC encoding and selects seeds near an SVM boundary; compared with SMOTE-NC and two oversampling methods.
Sort-Augment-Combine splits data by class, generates synthetic data per group with an unnamed generator and recombines, so new or standard cannot be told; compared with SMOTE, GAN-DA and ROSE.
EDOS uses a new entropy-difference metric to measure imbalance and keep only synthetic samples with retention capability, with its own unnamed generation step; no named comparison.
New LVQ-based fuzzy-rule oversampler computing samples per rule; compared with five other sampling techniques.

RUBRIC is a new generator-agnostic algorithm that ranks and selects synthetic candidates by a realism-utility score; coded own as a new algorithm of the paper, though the codebook's generator-plus-filter case could point to existing-parts; no comparison with other resampling stated.

Designs its own hybrid sampling: an interference negative-sample deletion strategy, a hard positive sample generation strategy and a self-paced balance factor in oversampling; only superiority on six datasets is claimed, no resampling comparison named.
TWHGBS proposes new granular-ball generation plus its own undersampling and adaptive oversampling inside granular balls, compared with GBU, SMOTE-Tomek and SMOTE-ENN.

TSHSA is a new name over standard parts (Tomek links, Euclidean-distance noise removal, k-means, SMOTE per cluster by density, close to k-means SMOTE); presented as part of the contribution but only AUC gains are reported, no other resampler compared.

A novel mixed sampling algorithm that uses a neighborhood three-way decision model to split data into density regions and applies undersampling, SMOTE or oversampling per region, a new allocation scheme; compared only with unnamed 'others'.

SPSO is the authors' own oversampler that creates synthetic protein sequences from the class distributions in data space; it is evaluated combined with cost/threshold adjustment, with no other resampler compared.

AIMEN is an explainable prediction framework that uses standard CTGAN for augmentation with relaxed feature bounds and silhouette-score filtering of the output; the generator is unchanged and comparisons are with classifiers only.
CeC-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant using k-means and centroid-based generation with noise filtering, compared with established oversampling techniques.
A novel cluster-based oversampling technique guided by an information-entropy evaluation of ambiguous areas, compared with existing oversampling techniques.
Own data-balancing algorithm that places synthetic samples near minority neighborhoods toward maximum class posterior ratio; compared only with unnamed 'experimental methods'.
APNOMO anomaly-prediction framework includes a proposed neighbor over-sampling (a newly named oversampler, change not detailed); compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art designs.
DSPOTE is a new oversampler with Chebyshev-distance noise filtering and density-based selection probabilities for borderline samples; compared with 'eight methods' not stated to be resamplers.
META_GAN adds two penalty terms to the GAN losses with meta-learned coefficients (a modified generative model), compared with alternative oversampling methods.
Standard SMOTE applied to deep features inside a network (an existing sampler in a learned space), presented as the solution but with no comparison against another resampling method.
Hybrid resampling with an 'improved' SMOTE whose change is not described, followed by clustering to delete redundant or noisy samples; no comparison with other resamplers stated.
New grouping scheme for minority samples and a new kernel-space oversampling method built on it; compared with seventeen benchmark algorithms not stated to be resamplers.
New fair oversampling technique using heterogeneous clusters with a new interpolation method; the abstract names no comparison with other resamplers.
OverNaN extends synthetic oversampling methods to work on incomplete vectors with explicit NaN strategies (a changed oversampler); demonstrated on examples without comparison.
New oversampling approach that generates minority examples with a trained autoencoder combined with particle swarm optimisation, compared with SMOTE and DBSMOTE.
AND determines the SMOTE neighborhood size k for each minority object (a changed SMOTE), compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
Uses a standard SeqGAN without stated change to create synthetic minority user profiles for text, compared with SMOTE; a standard generator under B2.
actGAN adds an activation-specific output layer to the generator (a new architecture) for mixed-type oversampling, compared with SMOTE-NC.
COSTE is a new oversampler pairing defective instances of similar complexity, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, MWMOTE and MAHAKIL.
Proposes a PSO-based dynamic multi-objective rebalancing algorithm and two hybrids with over- and under-sampling, compared with classic resampling methods.
Standard SMOTE on sliding-window data combined with domain-adaptive transfer learning to suppress oversampling noise; presented as the framework and compared with common oversampling methods.
PT-Trans-WGAN-GP puts pre-trained Transformer layers into the discriminator and auxiliary classifier of a WGAN-GP (a new architecture) to generate minority fault samples; no other resampler compared.

Guided Deep Interpolation is a new augmentation method: an autoencoder with a self-expressive layer and composite loss plus a semantic-variability pair sampling for latent interpolation, compared with traditional and generative augmentation.

GraphVCM is a new mixing scheme that synthesizes minority nodes by mixing them with spectral-clustering virtual centers, plus a distance-aware regulation; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
CR-SMOTE is an enhanced SMOTE that interpolates new minority instances near the class center, used with ELM; compared only with classifiers.
Proposes a new data balancing technique that grows synthetic data with a growing ring self-organizing map (a neural generator of its own), compared with SMOTE and random undersampling.

VAST-KD-SMOTE changes resampling with variance-based KD-tree undersampling and SMOTE neighbors taken from KD-tree leaves; it is part of an IDS framework compared only with other feature-selection optimizers.

MPLDO is a newly named oversampler doing locality-constrained interpolation in a correlation-projected latent subspace with classifier-guided pruning, not shown to be standard SMOTE; no resampling comparison stated.
A new weighted oversampling method built on a redefined intuitionistic fuzzy C-means with symmetric relative entropy, compared with various sampling methods.

New image oversampling method using influence functions and weights, SMOTE on features from a modified pre-trained CNN and a DCGAN generator fed with those features; experiments name no other resampler.
Proposes setting SMOTE's k with the Natural Neighbor algorithm (a new way of applying SMOTE-family methods), compared with the same SMOTE variants at default k.
A sequential SMOTE strategy that generates virtual samples from principal-curve class models and prunes them online, compared with SMOTE-based OS-ELM.
Federated ABC-GMM changes how the GMM is trained (approximate Bayesian computation across institutions) to oversample the minority class; no other resampler compared.
The SC-ECCE multi-label method includes a proposed dynamic sample-specific oversampling algorithm (DSSO), a newly named oversampler whose change is not described; compared only with MLC baselines.

Integrates an MLP-based undersampling (MLPUS, called 'a new approach') with MWMOTE; the abstract does not let one tell whether MLPUS is the paper's own or an existing method, and no comparison is stated.
DIR-SMOTE filters minority instances by density and interpolates while perturbing only top SHAP features, compared with nine standard resampling methods.

FCM-KSMOTE is a newly named oversampler with density-based fuzzy clustering, iterative region partitioning, in-cluster oversampling and noise detection; the compared methods are not said to be resamplers.
GBRF optimizes with a genetic algorithm two probability mass functions that allocate generation and removal across instance groups (a new resampling allocation), compared with SMOTE-IPF and ProWSyn.
Divide-Augment-Combine groups instances and trains a generative adversarial model per group with no stated change to the GAN; reports gains over no augmentation only.
Proposes ITerative Sampling, which iteratively modifies class priors and then cleans overlap, as an alternative to RUS, ROS and SMOTE used in the same phase; the abstract names no generator for ITS.
A wrapper that searches the amount of undersampling and SMOTE generation (a search for how much to oversample); compared only with published cost results.
ACWGAN adds an independent auxiliary classifier to a Wasserstein GAN (a changed architecture) for multiclass oversampling, compared with popular oversampling approaches.
C-SMOTE clusters the minority class and applies SMOTE with the groups as units, which reads as clustering then standard SMOTE with no stated allocation rule; no comparison stated.
GAA-BD introduces its own graph adversarial augmentation that strategically generates synthetic samples for bot detection, not described further; compared only with existing baselines.

New cluster-based oversampling via a deep instance envelope network of multilayer fuzzy C-means with a minimum interlayer discrepancy mechanism; compared with representative algorithms not said to be resamplers.
A GA-SVM search for SMOTE's k and over/under-sampling percentages (a search for how much to oversample), compared with SMOTE at default settings.

KB-SMOTE clusters minority boundary samples and uses centroid-guided within-cluster interpolation (a changed Borderline-SMOTE) inside a NILM model; compared only with DAE, Seq2point and Bi-LSTM models.

Builds an adversarial attack-based oversampling strategy for an SBERT multi-label model; the abstract does not say whether this is a new method or standard adversarial text augmentation, and compares only with conventional models.
MASV-weighted SMOTE uses mean absolute SHAP values to weight features during synthetic generation (a changed SMOTE); compared with baseline models and with no oversampling only.
Data balancing with an improved SMOTE (clustering and natural neighbours) and a GAN with label information and an optimised training loss (a stated change); no other resampler compared.
COAL active learning framework chains clustering-based uncertainty sampling with an unnamed standard oversampling method, no stated change; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
SMOTE-FraudGAN is a domain-adaptive generative model that enforces joint distribution alignment (a stated change to training) as stage one of a fraud framework; compared only with baseline models.
WGAN-GP trained on SVM-weighted overlap samples with MAML incorporated into training (a modified generative model), compared with advanced oversampling methods.
THPIA is a new positive-instance augmentation that hybridizes (mixes up) majority and minority features with a distance constraint, compared with CDSMOTE, SMOTE-LOF and others.
CluAD-EdiDO is a multiclass scheme of its own: clustering-based adaptive decomposition with editing-based diversified oversampling per cluster; no named comparison.
A gradient-improved deep GAN with a gradient penalty and deep feature matching in the losses plus a data evaluator, presented as an improved GAN; compared only with a diagnosis method.
NDANKA builds a time-series SMOTE with a numerical-differential artificial natural killer cell method (an own SMOTE variant) for earthquake prediction; compared only with prediction approaches.
AE-ELM-SynMin creates minority samples by crossover, mutation and filtering of AE-ELM hidden outputs and decoding them, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, Random-SMOTE and SMOTE-IPF.
A newly named RL-controlled subspace ensemble sampling algorithm with a dynamic ensemble module mixing under- and over-sampling, details not given; compared with unnamed traditional approaches.
A modified Borderline-SMOTE (NRBSID) hybridizing noise reduction with borderline-only oversampling, parts not shown to be standard; compared with random oversampling.

Standard GAN whose discriminator screens the generated samples before use; coded as a standard generator with quality screening of its output, though it could be read as a change to sampling; compared with other oversampling solutions.

CFS-SMOTE uses k-means, kNN-based removal of both classes in selected clusters and adaptive SMOTE that oversamples both classes by class size, a newly named variant; compared with state-of-the-art sampling algorithms.
GAN-LSTM IDS uses an LSTM-based GAN to synthesize attack patterns with no stated change to the generator (the novelty is anomaly scoring); compared with MAD-GAN, an anomaly detector, not a resampler.

Suggests SMOTE with cluster filtering (SMOTE-CF) and a weighted ENN with a distance-weighted disagreement score, both presented as its own changed steps; compared with traditional preprocessing methods not said to be resamplers.
HDHS is a new hybrid sampler using a heat decay model to expand sampling regions, remove majority samples and weight oversampling; compared with 10 state-of-the-art methods not said to be resamplers.
BRFE-PBKS-SVM improves SMOTE to oversample in Hilbert space with a PSO-adapted over-sampling rate, alongside imbalance-aware SVM-RFE; no comparison stated.
WECOI is a rotation-based ensemble for imbalanced data streams that forms chunks with standard over-sampling and instance selection; the contribution is the ensemble and no comparison is stated.
wRACOG is a new Gibbs-sampling oversampler that selects Markov-chain samples most likely to be misclassified, compared with three well-known resampling methods.
SMOTERoF applies standard SMOTE for each tree of an existing Rotation Forest ensemble, presented as the method and compared with RUS, ROS, SMOTE and UnderRoF.
SMOTE-RD adds a relative-density noise filter and density-based sparsity and boundary weights to SMOTE, compared with 7 popular oversampling methods.
LOF-KNN-CSENN is a new name over standard parts (LOF noise filtering, KNN boundary preservation, SMOTE and ENN) used before a stacking ensemble; compared only with single models.
GICaPS proposes an angle-based informative undersampling and a class-prioritized geometric oversampler that generates in 'no man's land', compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
QCL-MixNet includes its own kNN-guided, sample-aware dynamic mixup (a changed augmentation) as one of three innovations; compared only with ML, DL and GNN baselines.
A new over-sampling technique that generates minority samples by manifold distance instead of Euclidean distance; no named comparison.
Alongside the RAF-DB database, puts forward VFSG, a new face-aimed oversampling method whose generator is not described, and reports it performing well among over-sampling methods.
HCADE-SMOTE uses hypersphere coverage and adaptive differential evolution to move error-prone samples, then weighted SMOTE, compared with seven SMOTE-based methods.
Random-SMOTE is a new oversampler generating examples randomly in the minority sample space, compared with other random sampling approaches.

NEATER is a new game-theoretic algorithm that filters synthetic data from any over-sampling technique; coded own as a new selection algorithm, though the codebook's generator-plus-filter case could point to existing-parts; no named comparison.

A neighborhood-based adaptive heterogeneous oversampling ensemble that 'adopts an oversampling approach' not described, so one cannot tell whether the oversampler is new; compared with popular oversampling algorithms.
Balances multiclass data by applying standard SMOTE repeatedly, one class at a time, with no stated change; evaluated only by classifier performance.
GraphSAGE+ adds its own pattern-based oversampling module that generates synthetic laundering transactions, not further described; compared only with GNN models such as PNA.
Integrates standard SMOTE into the existing Learn++.NSE incremental ensemble for non-stationary imbalanced data; preliminary results with no comparison stated.
ADDPC-SMOTE uses adaptive density-difference peak clustering and spatial distribution entropy to set sampling probabilities, compared with SMOTE, K-means-SMOTE, BS-SMOTE, ADASYN and DPC-SMOTE.
GAMCGSA uses a genetic algorithm to find the optimal SMOTE sampling rate (a search for how much to oversample) for multi-class landslide deformation warning; compared only with traditional ML models.

Deep instance envelope network with multilayer fuzzy C-means and a minimum interlayer discrepancy mechanism, a new cluster-based oversampler; compared with representative algorithms not said to be resamplers.
DP-SMOTE combines adaptive density clustering, Bayesian confidence screening of candidates and directionally constrained interpolation, compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-ENN.
SyMProD is a new oversampler that selects minority seeds by the probability distribution of both classes, compared with seven conventional oversampling algorithms.
PSC-Net proposes an 'enhanced' augmentation based on SMOTE-Tomek whose change is not described, as one component of a signal classifier; no resampling comparison.
HD-SMOTE weights natural-neighbour density and boundary entropy density for adaptive oversampling; compared with 'four other classical algorithms' not said to be resamplers.
Optimized SMOTE with an adaptive boundary adjustment and a weight allocation by feature relevance and class distribution, compared with random over-sampling and under-sampling.
Regional SMOTE applies standard SMOTE separately within rural and urban subsets (a partition then standard SMOTE); compared only with no SMOTE.
DA-SMOTE-ED learns interpolation factors with an attention module in an encoder-decoder feature space and decodes the samples (a new method), compared with SMOTE-ENN, TimeGAN and AugmentTS.
BBO is a one-versus-all classification framework that uses boosting and an unnamed standard oversampling; the contribution is the classifier framework and counterparts are not said to be resamplers.
Adaptive TreeHive proposes its own selection of informative majority and minority instances to drive over- and under-sampling before tree ensembles, compared with under-sampling and over-sampling.
H-SMOTE allocates synthetic samples per histogram bin to equalize bins (a new allocation), with fuzzy ARTMAP, compared with SMOTE variants and GAN oversamplers.
MC-SMOTE clusters the minority class and interpolates between adjacent clusters (a changed SMOTE), compared with classical SMOTE.
Multi-scale convolutional GAN with an attention-guided statistical loss (new architecture and loss) for minority attack traffic, compared with baseline and state-of-the-art GAN schemes.
AFS-O is a newly named feature-weighted oversampler that uses attention feature selection weights before synthesis, compared with other synthetic oversampling algorithms.
Hybrid sampling chains k-means with SMOTE in safe clusters and instance-hardness-based undersampling, standard parts without stated change; compared with SMOTE-kNN, SMOTE-Tomek, SMOTE and DBSMOTE.

A dynamic over-sampling procedure that oversamples the minimum-sensitivity class during evolutionary MLP training (a new allocation of synthetic examples), compared with static preprocessing oversampling; classes are binned efficiency scores.

GDEO generates minority samples by a Gini-guided discriminatively constrained optimization instead of interpolation (a new oversampler); compared with 10 state-of-the-art methods not said to be resamplers.
A two-phase framework of its own: head-class undersampling with knowledge distillation and tail-class oversampling by visually aware augmentation; compared with long-tailed classification methods.
A new sampling strategy that builds balanced samples by raking and relabeling majority attribute values for the minority class; compared with the popular under- and oversampling methods it names.

ML-RUSMOTE is a novel multi-label undersampling plus SMOTE algorithm targeting imbalance within minority samples (a multi-label scheme of its own), compared with traditional methods for handling multi-label imbalance.
GAT-ADASYN replaces ADASYN heuristics with graph-attention weights for synthesis quotas and neighbour choice (a changed oversampler); baselines are not said to be resamplers.
WSUN spam detector includes a graph-based over-sampling method devised by the paper, not further described; compared with state-of-the-art detectors only.
Proposes a multi-label minority oversampling method driven by imbalance ratio per label and mean imbalance ratio; evaluated only with two classifiers.
RAC-GAN jointly trains a GAN oversampler and an RL ranker for undersampling that learn when, where and how much to resample (a new method); baselines are not said to be resamplers.
FC-SMOTE is a fairness-constrained oversampling module that preserves intra-group demographic balance, one of EFADL's novel components; no resampling comparison named.
RM-SMOTE down-weights atypical minority observations by robust Mahalanobis distance in seed selection, compared with other balancing techniques.

Perturb-and-Restore synthesizes abnormal chromosomes by perturbing normal banding patterns with a restoration diffusion network and energy-guided sample selection (a new generation framework); compared with unnamed existing methods.
A new Monte Carlo oversampler that draws from a density interpolated from the bootstrap empirical distribution of the minority class; compared with past algorithms not said to be resamplers.
A new multi-generator GAN blending TMG-GAN and R3GAN with class-specific generators, a dual-branch discriminator-classifier and decoupling, compared with hybrid sampling, SNGAN and TMG-GAN.
SMOTE-ENC encodes nominal features by their association with the minority class (a new SMOTE variant), compared with SMOTE-NC.
An SA-PSO hyperparameter search for SMOTE's oversampling ratio and k with an AdaRBFNN fitness (a search for how much to oversample); no comparison named.

Standard ADASYN followed by MCA-based pruning of the synthetic instances and bootstrapping before a CNN; coded as an existing sampler plus an existing analysis used as cleaner; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Improves SMOTE only by adding k-means (k-means partitioning then SMOTE) inside an RF model for coal origin identification; compared only with SVM and RF.
Introduces a newly named PCA-based cluster-driven synthetic sample filtering framework whose generator and steps are not described; compared only across classifiers.
ISMOTE computes SMOTE neighbours with both Euclidean and cosine distance (a changed SMOTE) before LSDA and AdaBoost; compared with feature extraction methods only.
OS-GAN feeds selected majority samples instead of noise to the GAN and adds a central regularization (a modified generative model), compared with 14 resampling techniques.
Q-SYNTH is a newly named synthetic oversampling and augmentation technique for code comments whose generator is not described; only gain over the base classifier is reported.

OD-GAN changes a cGAN so its discriminator is trained as an outlier detector across majority and minority distributions and removes outliers (a modified generative model), compared with other oversampling methods.

Adaptive Swarm Balancing uses PSO and bat algorithms segment by segment to optimize SMOTE's key parameters (a search for how much to oversample), compared with whole-dataset swarm SMOTE and brute-force tuning.
An enhanced SMOTE with entropy-based neighborhood calibration is one of three innovations of an IoT intrusion framework; compared only with state-of-the-art approaches.

A deterministic per-attack supplementation coefficient and generation from local medians and extreme values of neighbours without random interpolation (a new allocation and generator); compared with unnamed basic approaches.
RACOG and wRACOG are new probabilistic oversamplers using a joint distribution and Gibbs sampling with lag or misclassification-based selection, compared with three existing resampling techniques.

AdaCluCSL applies SMOTE with cluster-specific weights after adaptive k-means plus cost-sensitive learning, read as k-means SMOTE-like standard parts (same call as R05498); compared only with traditional methods.
A local PCA approach that generates new churn samples (an own generator), compared with linear regression and standard PCA data generation techniques.

Hierarchical ensemble whose third level oversamples from multivariate Gaussians fitted on clusters and kNN neighbourhoods with a developed distance-based sample optimization (a changed Gaussian oversampler); no comparison named.
Proposes SMOTE combined with a genetic algorithm to synthesize new active compounds, the GA's role not described; compared only with traditional virtual screening.
A-SMOTE eliminates SMOTE samples that lie closer to the majority than the minority class (a changed SMOTE with its own rule), compared with ten widely used sampling methods.

Traso treats synthetic over-samples as a transfer source and TrasoBoost reweights them separately in boosting (a new way of applying synthetic oversampling); compared with unnamed class-imbalance methods.

OAGAN makes CTGAN generation take ADASYN difficulty weights into account, coded as a stated change to the generator's sampling, though it could be read as ADASYN chained with a standard CTGAN; compared with three standard oversamplers.
Interpolation oversampling applied in an autoencoder latent space and mapped back (an existing sampler in a learned space); compared with existing synthetic-data methods.
ALIS alternates its own important undersampling of majority instances and generation of informative minority instances, each informing the other; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
GAN-AE is a new recurrent GAN architecture with an autoencoder component for sequence data, compared with SMOTE, autoencoders and GAN-based generators.

EO-WGAN chains SMOTE with a WGAN and claims an undescribed optimized sampling strategy, coded own as a newly named enhanced generator, though the parts may be standard; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
Introduces a new oversampling algorithm EKSMOTE (not described) inside a cost-sensitive stacking classifier; compared with a traditional algorithm.
GA-SMOTE uses a GA-chosen noise scheme, boundary weights and intra-cluster triangular sampling (a new oversampler); compared with five methods not said to be resamplers.
KM-MSMOTE filters k-means clusters by class dominance and partitions them into safe, overlapping and noisy regions by membership to control generation, compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
UCLSO is a multi-label scheme of its own that generates label-specific synthetic minority points within unsupervised clusters; compared with unnamed competing algorithms.
FCSMI is a label-wise multi-label scheme that constructs distance-to-minority features before SMOTE, compared with state-of-the-art multi-label sampling methods.
Safe Level OUPS is a newly named pre-processing oversampler not described in detail, compared with other popular techniques and their combinations.
Develops an improved SMOTE (change not described) as the second contribution of a mammographic density CAD system; no resampling comparison stated.
iHHO-SMOTe is a newly named hybrid of an improved Harris hawks optimizer with SMOTE after RF feature selection and DBSCAN outlier removal; only scores are reported.
SMOTE-BWO adaptively picks SMOTE or ROS and then refines the synthetic samples by black widow optimization, compared with widely used oversampling techniques.
A new mutation-based augmentation that applies mutation operators to non-defective code to create defective instances, compared with other data augmentation methods.
Improves SMOTE by combining k-means SMOTE with an RBF network, an FCM resampling link and RUS (RUS FCM K-RBFNN SMOTE), compared with K-means SMOTE and FCM SMOTE.
MLSMOTE is a new synthetic instance generation algorithm for multilabel data, compared with other multilabel oversampling methods.
A novel multiclass preprocessing that oversamples minority classes by normalized probability before a stacking ensemble; compared with representative approaches not said to be resamplers.
An 'improved' algorithm that builds pseudo samples from SMOTE with a multi-dimensional Gaussian density hypothesis, the combination not described; compared only with SVM and RF.
DBSCAN noise removal and kNN safe/dangerous typing, then synthesis with GANs and bootstrapping by neighbourhood type, with no stated change to the GAN (B2); compared with unnamed approaches.
Uses a standard SeqGAN without stated change as the oversampler for text, compared with four other oversampling methods.
Designs a balancing step combining a standard WGAN and ADASYN without stated change, alongside a DenseNet1D and Bi-SRU detector; no resampling comparison.
NR-Modified SMOTE filters minority noise by KNN and uses a modified Manhattan distance in SMOTE (a changed SMOTE), compared with NR-SMOTE.

CrossACL, an analytic class-incremental HSI classifier, introduces 'a simple but effective oversampling strategy' with no detail, so one cannot tell whether it is new; compared only with continual learning methods.
AC-CTGAN chains ENN, an improved k-means with density-based cluster weights, a standard CTGAN and Tomek links; the generator itself is unchanged (B2); compared with SMOTE, its variants and CTGAN.
SMOTEiS (SMOTE in stages) is a newly named oversampler whose change is not described, compared with SMOTE and ensemble methods.
A storm nowcasting network uses 'cell-based oversampling' with no detail, so one cannot tell whether it is new; the contribution is the model and comparisons are with extrapolation methods.
COM is a multiclass clustering-based oversampler that weights clusters inversely to density and oversamples within them, parts not shown to be standard; no named comparison.
Introduces newly proposed a priori based re-sampling methods, not described; robustness shown without a named comparison.
SGO uses an SVM to locate the boundary and a genetic algorithm to generate minority samples along it (a new oversampler); compared with unnamed traditional methods.
A diffusion model with a CBAM-enhanced U-net and a new minimal noise scheduling (new architecture and training) to augment fault data; no other resampler compared.
BGDSO is a new synthetic oversampler balancing global and fine-grained bilateral gradient distributions; no named comparison.
MOSIG is a new oversampler that synthesizes defective instances weighted by an instance-gravity similarity; evaluated against the classifiers without resampling only.
ADOMS is a new oversampler generating along the first principal component of local data; compared with 'other relative methods' not said to be resamplers.

CCAS uses complexity-guided agglomerative clusters, percentile-based probability filtering and proportional allocation of synthetic samples (a new oversampler); compared with unnamed benchmark methods.
Hybrid oversampling chains Information Gain and PCA, DBSCAN clustering and a standard WGAN-div generator with no stated change, compared with SMOTE.
SOMM generates diverse minority instances and updates them adaptively using both classes' neighbourhoods (a new oversampler); compared with 'existing methods'.

An ECG system applies an unnamed standard oversampling to each binary subproblem after decomposition; the contribution is the autoencoder and classifier system, compared with state-of-the-art methods.
A new rebalancing algorithm that uses GMM-EM densities and a mu-sigma probability graph to set safety-based generation weights; compared with unnamed existing methods.
AHRS is a new adaptive hybrid resampling that iteratively mixes over- and undersampling by imbalance ratio and feature importance, compared with SMOTE, ROS and Tomek links.
EA-GAN adds an adaptive attention mechanism and progressive feature refinement module to the GAN (a new architecture) for class-specific lesion images; compared only with unnamed baselines.
Replaces the GAN noise input with improved k-means SMOTE output (a changed generator input), presented as an improved network; no named comparison.
FAST-DN is a newly named transformer-guided diffusion generator with fidelity gating and residual correction, stage one of FRACTAL; compared with leading baselines not said to be resamplers.
BADGAN adds a boundary sample classifier and a dual-discriminator distance constraint to the GAN (new architecture and loss), compared with peer methods for addressing class imbalance.
NLKF-SMOTE is a two-stage SMOTE with Gaussian and linear interpolation, adaptive neighbour selection and GNN anomaly filtering; no named comparison.
FSOTE finds minority clusters in feature space and fills synthetic samples uniformly in their interiors (a new generation rule); compared with unnamed previous methods.
An enhanced SMOTE-RUS scheme that preserves appliance-level periodicity in synthetic attacks, part of an FDIA detection framework; compared only with baseline detectors.
MNHS is a new hybrid sampler with density-KNN undersampling, majority auxiliary instances constraining oversampling and cleaning; compared with various algorithms not said to be resamplers.
EvoSampling generates instances by multi-task genetic programming and undersamples with granular balls (a new hybrid sampler), compared with existing sampling methods.
DSF-Unet is a diffusion model with a new dual-stream U-net using Bi-Mamba and multi-scale attention modules to synthesize minority wafer maps; no other resampler compared.
Proposes three new variants of GAN and BOSME (Bayesian-network oversampling) augmentation, compared with the original techniques analysed.
SMOTE-IF combines a SMOTE-based multiclass strategy with a proposed isolation-forest variant for overlap and noise, compared with state-of-the-art resampling methods.
DPDO is a new Poisson-disk oversampler with dynamic region expansion within minority clusters, compared with eleven oversampling baselines.

Asymmetric SMOTE-ENN sets its own per-class targets (benign and attack caps, minimum synthetic counts), coded as a new allocation, though it may be read as SMOTE-ENN with chosen settings; no resampling comparison stated.
Presents SyMProD, a new oversampler with z-score noise removal and probability-based reference selection, in a liver cancer model; compared with 'other techniques' not said to be resamplers.
CSUP is a multiclass up-sampling scheme that allocates synthetic counts by centroid distance weights, compared with SMOTE and Adaboost.

Augments toxic samples with an LLM prompted by extracted semantic elements, an unchanged language model under B2 unless element-guided prompting counts as new conditioning; compared only with GPT-4 zero-shot.
Adds synthetic 'ghost points' in distance space for time series where SMOTE cannot apply (a new oversampler); compared only with no augmentation.
A selective preprocessing that oversamples identified outliers of any class before SMOTE (a new way of applying SMOTE), compared with plain SMOTE.
GOS-IL is a newly named over-sampling based online imbalanced learning framework with deferred, error-triggered updates; the oversampling itself is not described and no comparison is named.
Dazzle is presented as an optimized cWGAN-GP whose architecture hyperparameters are searched by Bayesian optimization, read as a stated change to the generator; compared with SMOTE.

DOS samples in-class-neighbour synthetic embedding targets in CNN feature space and uses them to drive iterative representation learning, a new framework rather than an existing sampler simply run in latent space; comparison only with 'the existing method'.

Adaptive over- and under-sampling that sets the degree of resampling and cost ratio adaptively within an ensemble, a new way of applying resampling; comparison only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
RBSP-Boosting removes noise and undersamples by Shapley value and weights minority oversampling by Shapley value, a new resampling scheme; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.
HSAB uses BIRCH clustering to set adaptive SMOTE weights per sparse minority region (a new allocation) plus GMM-based majority reduction; no comparison named.
MWMOTE is a new weighted, cluster-based minority oversampler; compared with other existing methods framed in the abstract as oversampling methods.
SMOTE followed by a novel weighted ENN cleaner (WENN), so the chain contains a new part of the paper's own; compared with three resampling methods.
CCR is a novel resampling algorithm combining decision-border cleaning with guided synthetic oversampling (generator kind not named); outperforms conventional oversampling approaches.
Conditional WGAN for mixed tabular data extended with an auxiliary classifier loss (a stated loss change, 'our extensions'); compared with standard oversampling regimes.
A modification of radial-based oversampling with an added constraint and a recursion mechanism, a changed oversampler; no comparison named.

PENH mixes each positive with fuzzy KNN negative neighbours via Mixup and screens outputs by one-class SVM; the pairing rule is read as a stated change to mixup, though it could be seen as standard mixup plus a filter; baselines unnamed.

Local CGANs trained federatedly with validation-guided weighted aggregation of discriminator updates, read as a stated change to GAN training, though it could be read as a plain CGAN inside an FL pipeline; no comparison named.
ADVO is a new oversampling strategy built on an innovative regression-based fraud-sequence generator (plus an adapted TimeGAN); compared with traditional oversampling algorithms.
Proposes a newly named Graph-based Over-sampling Technique (GOT) for graph data whose mechanism is not described, so own; no comparison stated.

LEL partitions data by a KNN Sample Type and applies unnamed tailored imbalance strategies per subset in an ensemble; the abstract does not say what resampling is used or whether the parts are standard; compared with SMOTE and NOGAN.
A modified SMOTE that removes outliers left after SMOTE generation (not an existing named cleaner); compared with SMOTE, SMOTE+ENN and SMOTE+Tomek.
TSCBU-SMOTE-ENN adds an anchor-driven two-stage clustering undersampling stage before SMOTE and ENN, read as own for that new stage though its steps are close to standard; baselines unnamed.
CIHR adaptively applies over- and undersampling guided by a relative class-impurity measure, a new hybrid resampling scheme; no resampling comparison named.
CRN-SMOTE adds a novel cluster-based noise reduction step to SMOTE; compared with RN-SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek and SMOTE-ENN.
New oversampler whose neighbour selection for producing synthetic instances is done by the firefly algorithm; no comparison named.
New generative architecture (domain-constraint autoencoder prior for a generator trained against a discriminator and classifier); compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
RIGAN combines natural-neighbour denoising, an improved GAN and a PPO-trained sample filter; compared with GAN oversamplers, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
New supervised kernel-thinning sample-reduction methods (SKT, CKT, JKT) with SMOTE-based variants, compared with each other and with plain kernel thinning.
MBS generates synthetic data with regression models that capture feature relationships, a new oversampler; compared with 10 methods not said to be resampling methods.
ABUSVM uses a newly named adaptive borderline-SMOTE (change not described) with under-sampling SVM, so own; no resampling comparison.
CMSS steers synthetic samples from unnamed oversamplers by SHAP-selected directional perturbations tuned with PSO, a new way of applying oversampling; evaluated only before against after.
New oversampler: density-peaks clustering of the minority, weights by sub-cluster size and interpolation between cluster cores and members; comparison partners not named.
OT-SMOTE replaces k-NN with an optimal-transport plan and uses Beta-distributed interpolation, a changed SMOTE; compared with SMOTE.
MAO builds multiple adaptively oversampled balanced sets fused by evidential reasoning with inconsistency-based weights, a newly named oversampling scheme; compared with unnamed related approaches.
Clustering-based reduction of the majority class (with an unspecified encoding) followed by standard SMOTE, a chain of existing steps with no stated change; evaluated only before against after.
Balances mineral prospectivity data with a conditional VAE described with no stated change to the model, a standard generator used as is; compared with SMOTE and class weighting.
ABC-GAN adds an attention mechanism to the generator and a DTW term to its loss; compared with standard oversampling and a vanilla cGAN.

Block-based dynamic ensemble for drifting streams that uses an enhanced-PSO oversampler (enhancement not described, so own); unclear whether the oversampler is the paper's or prior work; compared with unnamed existing techniques.
BLT is a new augmentation that creates tail-class images by gradient-ascent adversarial perturbation; compared with oversampling tail-class images.
Spectral SMOTE, called a modified oversampler, clusters the data spectrally and applies SMOTE only in sparse areas (an allocation rule); compared with SMOTE and its variants.
TaGN includes a density-based WGAN that penalizes synthetic samples close to legitimate transactions, a stated change to the GAN loss; compared with unnamed peers.
Compares informed pre-processing methods and modifies the oversampling ratio of a SMOTE-related method from local neighbourhood types, a new way of applying SMOTE.
Feature-level SMOTE runs standard SMOTE in a feature space learned by a Siamese self-attention network, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with the oversamplers OUPS, A-SUWO and NRAS.

Membership-density-based oversampling groups samples into safe, overlapping and noisy areas by membership degree and selects seeds by density ratio, a new SMOTE-based scheme for multiclass data; compared with unnamed test methods.

Novel synthetic oversampling for binary malware features that preserves app functionality (mechanism not given); outperforms existing techniques, which the abstract frames as imbalance methods such as SMOTE.
CFGAN is a new GAN combining an autoencoder with ACGAN, interpolating learned categorical features and using Wasserstein distance; compared with existing data generation methods.
Replay-guided SMOTE seeds synthesis from a drift-aware episodic memory buffer across time, a new way of applying SMOTE in continual learning; compared only with classifiers and replay baselines.

Novel oversampling in a kernel space built from RNN generative models of sequences; the sampler used in that space is not named, so it could be an existing sampler in a learned space; no comparison named.
GPCR classification using the authors' new synthetic protein sequence oversampling (SPSO) algorithm, a newly named oversampler whose mechanism is not described; no comparison.
PSSTO is a newly named oversampler that synthesizes and prunes minority series in path-signature space; compared with conventional resampling and time-series oversamplers.
DPG-da enforces decision predicates extracted from trained models as constraints during sample generation, a constrained oversampler of its own; compared with traditional over-sampling methods.
Bi-SMOTE restricts interpolation to class-aware bounded regions, a changed SMOTE; compared with seventeen resampling methods.
IB-GAN generates from randomly masked real vectors by imputation instead of noise and trains jointly with the classifier, a new GAN design; compared with parametric augmentation and GAN baselines.
ImbGAN embeds a classifier in the GAN and generates minority samples resembling misclassified ones, a new architecture and training; outperforms well-known synthetic sampling methods.
STR-DES introduces STW-SMOTE, which weights historical neighbours by spatial proximity and temporal recency, a new SMOTE variant for streams; compared with nine unnamed baselines.
