Improved SMOTE that combines over- and undersampling with targeted neighbour choice and varied synthesis strategies, an improved oversampler; evaluated without a resampling comparison.
CS-SMOTE selects seed points by a symmetrical cube scoring rule and interpolates repeatedly, a new SMOTE variant; compared with other oversampling methods.

Proposes a denoising ADASYN with purposeful target selection inside an outage prediction model, a changed oversampler; compared with unnamed benchmarking algorithms; predicts the category of the outage count.
TailBoost's SPMix mixes tail- and head-class images under saliency-map guidance, a stated change to mixup; compared with long-tailed learning methods not said to be resampling.
Introduces a novel oversampling technique called fuzzy sampling (within the GHOST pipeline) whose mechanism is not described; compared only with prior deep-learning defect predictors.
TPH-SMOTE runs SMOTE, selects seeds for a second round with the whale optimization algorithm and applies SMOTE again, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with 11 oversampling algorithms.
SMOTE-FRST-2T cleans synthetic minority and real majority instances by fuzzy-rough instance selection with two thresholds, a new cleaning stage; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
OOSI is a new oversampler with adaptive spatial partitioning, per-cluster allocation, noise suppression and oriented generation paths; compared with 11 oversampling algorithms.
LEO-CVAE adds a local-entropy-weighted loss and entropy-guided sampling to a CVAE, stated changes to loss and sampling; compared with traditional oversampling and generative baselines.

Synthesizes samples for hard attributes with a semi-supervised GAN extended by deactivating outputs for synthetic samples (Deact), a stated training change; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes a new Enhanced Geometric SMOTE (EG-SMOTE) for IoT edge streams; compared with SMOTE and G-SMOTE.
Safe-Level-SMOTE weights interpolation along the SMOTE line by a safe level, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
SMOTE followed by an editing technique based on fuzzy rough set theory that the abstract does not describe as new, a chain of existing steps; compared with state-of-the-art resampling methods.
MuDIOT is a newly named multiclass oversampling technique whose mechanism the abstract does not describe, so own; no comparison.
GraphCKSA proposes a new CENN undersampler and KCQ-SMOTE with Q-learning to choose the number of clusters for intra-cluster SMOTE; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art models.

MEDA_LUDE evolves latent feature distributions with an improved estimation-of-distribution algorithm jointly with a DNN (L-GM loss, diversity fitness) to generate images, a new method; no comparison named.
NMCCO cleans boundary majority samples with KNN and constructive covering and constrains synthesis by coverage radius, a modified oversampler; no comparison named.
Chains standard SMOTE with a standard conditional GAN with no stated change; ablation compares with SMOTE-only and CGAN-only; 3D seismic segmentation.
An enhancement to SMOTE that places synthetic instances as solutions of attraction-repulsion Weber problems; no comparison named.
OMOS clusters by mean shift, keeps safe samples, generates from autoencoder-learned distributions and sets per-cluster sampling rates by a novel rule; compared with six SMOTE-based oversamplers.
FSDR-SMOTE removes noise by Tukey's rule, labels boundary and safe samples by feature standard deviation and generates from sub-cluster centres, an improved Random-SMOTE; no comparison named.
Genetic-algorithm generation of synthetic minority text patterns with an overfitting-based stopping criterion deciding how much to generate, a new oversampler; no comparison.
Incremental synthetic data generation that adjusts SMOTE variants to the data distribution over iterations, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with the original SMOTE variants and autoencoders.

FreMGP evolves sets of synthetic minority series by multi-tree genetic programming guided by a contrastive frequency-domain representation, a new oversampler; compared with existing oversampling methods.
Class-specific GANs generate samples in a convolutional-autoencoder latent space with no stated change to the GAN, a standard generator used as is; compared only with CNN and transformer classifiers.

Adaptive SV-Borderline SMOTE-SVM labels positive support vectors as concave or convex in kernel space and generates with two adaptive interpolation rules via a designed Gram matrix, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed approaches.

CIPNN applies standard SMOTE and a nearest-neighbour critical-area subset, then bootstraps an ensemble of polynomial networks; the resampling itself has no stated change and no resampling comparison is named.
Oversampling framework of a trivial autoencoder plus modified GANs (modification named, not detailed), so own; compared with data oversampled by other techniques.

Padding-aware GAN that synthesizes windows of consecutive sessions rather than isolated records, read as a stated change to the generator, though it could be a standard GAN on a new data unit; compared with ROS and SMOTE.
AE-CGAN oversamples rare classes with a standard conditional GAN in an autoencoder's reduced feature space, standard parts under a new name; compared only with RF and AE-RF without resampling.

Two-tier iterative ensemble with a 'hybrid oversampling technique used at different levels' for multiclass rare samples; the abstract names no parts, so own versus existing parts cannot be told; no comparison.
EHSBoost extends evolutionary undersampling in boosting (EUSBoost) to evolutionary hybrid under- and oversampling, a changed resampling method; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art counterparts.
SG-CGAN trains a CGAN on GraphSAGE hidden vectors to generate minority subgraphs, a new conditioning and output for graph oversampling; compared only with no synthetic data.
Proposes a confident over- and under-sampling process built on principal curves and granulation of fault data for an online ELM, a new resampling method; compared with unnamed algorithms.
Two new Borderline-SMOTE-based methods that also synthesize on the majority side and undersample particular majority samples; compared with ROS, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
SMOTE-RkNN removes noise by RkNN-based probability density after SMOTE, a new cleaning rule rather than an existing cleaner; compared with SMOTE hybrid variants.
CWMAGAN-GP adds Gumbel-softmax categorical outputs, a discriminator embedding layer and multi-head attention to a WGAN-GP, a new architecture; no resampling comparison named.
New oversampling framework that perturbs majority samples under a counterfactual objective to create minority samples near the boundary; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

CSKGO chooses clusters by a compactness-separateness K-means and allocates per-cluster Gaussian sampling by compactness, a new allocation over a Gaussian generator; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
RAMOBoost ranks minority instances by an adaptive sampling distribution for synthetic generation inside boosting, a new oversampling method; no comparison named.

AGO-FT partitions space with a complete random forest, detects noise and guides SMOTE synthesis with confusion-based weights in a trusted neighbourhood, a new oversampler; compared with 8 oversampling algorithms.
MMOTE is a new Mahalanobis-metric-based oversampler (generation details not given); outperformed alternative oversampling techniques.
EREC develops an affinity-propagation-based oversampling method to balance training sets for an evidential-reasoning ensemble; compared with ensembles built on other oversampling methods.
DFGAN translates digital-twin data to measured data with an improved SE U-Net generator and a spectral correlation loss, a new GAN; no resampling comparison.
EdgeCutMix is a new augmentation combining Canny edge detection with selective mixing; compared with MixUp, CutOut, CutMix and Mosaic.
OpTunedSMOTE tunes SMOTE hyperparameters with TPE in Optuna, read as a search over how SMOTE is applied, though it could be seen as standard SMOTE with tuning; compared only with SDP classifiers.

HS-Gen generates in an adaptively shrinking hypersphere instead of on a line, a new generation mechanism embedded in SMOTE methods; compared with the original SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and others.
CDCMOM is a newly named cluster-aware resampling doing localized under- and oversampling within clusters to reduce overlap (samplers not named); compared with SMOTE, NearMiss and SMOTE-Tomek.
A reinforcement-learning agent sets sampling ratios and synthetic generation parameters for ensemble members, a search for how much to resample; no comparison named.
TAC-ACGAN adds triple-attention fusion to the generator, a center-loss term and spectral normalization, a new GAN; compared with unnamed existing approaches.
Dynamic resampling with an attenuation rate of oversampling that changes class sizes during training, a new way of applying existing resamplers; compared with unnamed existing methods.

Synthesizes minority data with standard Latin hypercube sampling followed by a selection step, read as a standard statistical sampler used as is plus a filter, though it could be seen as a new oversampler; evaluated only before against after.
CBSMOTE removes noise by distance to the minority-class centre before SMOTE, an improved SMOTE with its own filter rule; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
Generative learning (GL) fits a Gaussian mixture model and samples new minority and majority data, standard GMM sampling under a new name; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-ENN and other SMOTE variants.
Novel oversampler that weights hard minority seeds locally and generates samples by EM-based imputation from the minority distribution; compared with baseline sampling techniques.
GenSample uses a genetic algorithm to set per-example oversampling rates and stops when performance drops, a search for how much to oversample; compared with unnamed existing methodologies.
RCSMOTE categorizes minority samples and generates within a calculated safe range per dimension, an improved SMOTE; experiments show it overcomes SMOTE's problems.
Boosting-based SMOTE with a per-sample oversampling rate tailored by local covariance matrices, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with six unnamed benchmark techniques.

MetaBoost combines SMOTE, ADASYN and CTGAN outputs by tuned weighted averaging, a mix of existing samplers including a standard generator with no stated change; compared with ROS, SMOTE, ADASYN and CTGAN.
CRISP augments the minority class with native counterfactuals inside a causally informed mortality model, an augmentation method of its own; compared with interpolation-based oversampling.
Improved VAE-GAN with self-attention and WGAN-GP plus filters on generated samples, stated changes to the generative model; no comparison named.
Easy-SMT combines SMOTE-based oversampling with EasyEnsemble with no stated change, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; compared only with baseline classifiers.

Teacher-guided conditional diffusion generates risky nodes and a new temporally constrained structural completion links them into the graph, read as own constrained generation, though the diffusion step may be standard with filters; compared with graph augmentation baselines.
POM shifts fuzzy-identified overlapping majority samples into the positive region by a transformation matrix, a new oversampler; compared with 15 unnamed methods.
LN-SMOTE uses local neighbourhood information including majority neighbours, a new SMOTE generalization; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and Safe-Level-SMOTE.

Active learning combined with a proposed semantic oversampling for dialect NER whose mechanism and parts are not described, so own versus existing cannot be told; compared only with and without oversampling.
Multi-label borderline oversampling guided by label correlations with two critical boundary regions and distance weights, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
Biased-SVM finds support vectors, standard SMOTE oversamples them, and Biased-SVM classifies, a selection then standard SMOTE with no stated change; no comparison named.

Proposes over- and under-sampling triggered when imbalance passes a threshold during active learning for person re-identification; the samplers are not described, so own versus existing cannot be told; compared only with and without.
Redesigns SMOTE and Safe-Level SMOTE so new instances always fall between two minority instances, changed SMOTE variants; compared with the original algorithms.

Model-based clustering per class then oversampling each sub-cluster to remove between- and within-class imbalance, read as a new allocation per region, though it resembles clustering then standard oversampling; compared with unnamed methods.

GenEEG uses a dual-conditioned VAE with latent diffusion conditioned on clinical states and neurophysiological features, a new conditioning, in a continual learning framework; compared with traditional oversampling baselines.
Clustering then standard SMOTE in clusters above an imbalance threshold, a step in a GBDT2NN credit model whose contribution lies elsewhere; compared only with other credit algorithms.
SMOTE-Complex selects synthetic samples by optimizing training-set complexity (plus outer-sample and clustering variants), a new way of applying SMOTE; no resampling comparison stated.
NKB-SMOTE chains K-means, SMOTE in the boundary cluster, Tomek links and NearMiss-2, standard parts under a new name; compared with traditional SMOTE.

MEDA_LUDE learns Gaussian-mixture latent distributions with a new L-GM loss, a four-phase training strategy and an improved EDA that evolves latent features, a new generative framework; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

INGB models the data with entropy-optimized granular balls and oversamples nonlinearly from isotropic Gaussians inside them, a new oversampling framework; compared with linear sampling frameworks and algorithms.
CGMOS adds points by certainty change with a guarantee over SMOTE, a new SMOTE extension; compared with existing algorithms the abstract frames as SMOTE and its extensions.

New sampling strategy that builds balanced samples by raking and relabeling, imputing majority attribute values into the minority class; compared with popular existing over- and undersampling methods.
DVAAN combines a discriminative VAE with a class-conditioned two-component latent mixture and a GAN to generate near-boundary samples, a new generative model; comparisons not named.
Proposes an oversampling algorithm MRF-SMOTE (change not described) alongside feature selection and a Dueling DQN classifier, so own; compared only with classifiers.
Augments minority fake-news classes with synthetic texts produced by prompting a language model, a standard generator used as is (prompting is not a change to the model); no resampling comparison.
NaN-DEBOHID splits minority samples by natural neighbours, synthesizes with differential evolution and removes noise, a changed DEBOHID; comparison partners not named.
SOI-C and SOI-CJ are two new cluster-based oversamplers generating inside minority clusters in proportion to cluster size; compared with other oversampling methods.
MOODS guides synthetic oversampling and majority undersampling by multi-objective bilevel optimization with a new diversity metric, a new way of applying resampling; no resampling comparison stated.
BSGAN combines Borderline-SMOTE with a GAN without describing any change to either, a chain with a standard generator; compared with existing oversampling techniques.

Scalable Spark pipeline that transforms data with fractional norms and then applies SMOTE, an existing sampler in a transformed space; outperforms the traditional Euclidean data-level approach, read as a resampling comparison.
MCI screening system that develops a novel extended over-sampling method SNEOM (mechanism not described), so own; compared only with a clinical expert.
FAEM proposes hybrid sampling with cross-validation-based undersampling and sensitive-attribute-based oversampling, a new way of applying resampling for fairness; compared with benchmark models.
ADKEN combines adaptive denoising with density- and complexity-weighted KNN oversampling, a new oversampler; comparison partners not named.
ESMOTE overproduces with a new interpolation mechanism and selects synthetic examples by evolutionary instance selection; compared with SMOTE and its variants.
GMOTE samples from a Gaussian mixture with tail probabilities adapted by Mahalanobis distance for local outliers, a stated change to GMM sampling; compared with SMOTE.
CS-WGAN-PSO optimizes a conditional WGAN-GP with particle swarm optimization, read as a stated change to training (like Dazzle); compared with WGAN-GP and IWAE.
CBLoRAS selects boundary minority samples, applies standard LoRAS and filters with reverse-kNN, a chain of existing steps; compared with LoRAS.
Introduces a novel K-CGAN for fraud data whose change from CGAN is not described, so own as a newly named generator; compared with other oversampling approaches.
GraphMV-SVAE generates minority subgraphs with a subgraph VAE using quantum-inspired reparameterization and class-mean constraints, a new generative model; compared with unnamed baselines.
RTAEI encodes tabular data with robust VAEs and generates by SMOTE in the latent space, existing parts including a B2 generator with no stated change; no comparison named.
Novel approach where both oversampling and undersampling use synthetic cases generated by class-specific subclustering; compared with random resampling methods.
Improved SMOTE with hierarchical noise filtering, minority selection and dynamic distribution density; compared with SMOTE and its improved algorithms.
IGAN-IDS uses an improved GAN (improvement not described) to generate attack samples, so own; compared with GAN, MLP-GAN, SMOTE and ADASYN.

k-INOS is a new wrapper that undersamples noisy minority examples by neighbourhood of influence before any oversampler, a new way of applying oversampling; compared with 8 oversampling methods without it.
Introduces a standard DDPM, class-conditioned on flare intensity, to synthesize rare solar flare images, with no stated change to the model; evaluated only with and without synthetic images.

A deep autoencoder trained on attack traffic produces pseudo-normal samples selected by low reconstruction error to balance data, read as a new reverse-autoencoder generation scheme, though it could be seen as a plain AE with a filter; compared only with Isolation Forest.
Random undersampling of the majority followed by SMOTE on minority boundary instances, a chain of existing steps; compared with other sampling algorithms.
ASCFNO introduces a new density-peak clustering with noise filter, adaptive per-sub-cluster oversampling sizes and probability-guided interpolation; no comparison named.
Improved CGAN conditioned on a modified Gaussian-kernel density-peak clustering and trained with WGAN-GP, a new conditioning; compared with three common oversampling algorithms.
Generates minority instances by standard kernel density estimation sampling with no stated change, a B2 generator used as is; compared with other sampling techniques.
Cluster+Boost puts an undescribed cluster-based oversampling inside boosting; the abstract does not say whether the oversampler is new or standard; compared with RUSBoost and SMOTEBoost.

PA-CDiT is a conditional diffusion transformer with new temporal embedding, interval-aware attention and adaptive modulation on a protocol-aware representation, a new architecture; compared with a DDPM baseline.

Conditional GANs conditioned on cluster assignments of VGG16 features rather than labels, read as a new conditioning, though the three GANs are otherwise standard; evaluated with and without generated images.
A new cosine-similarity-based sampling method for imbalanced thruster data (mechanism not detailed); outperforms SMOTE and ADASYN.
Introduces a newly named augmentation algorithm cPAen whose mechanism is not described, so own; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and cWGAN-GP.
The original SMOTE paper presents the synthetic minority oversampling method; compared with majority undersampling alone and with loss-ratio or prior adjustment.

CropGAN is called a re-engineered class-conditional GAN for mixed tabular data, read as a modified generator, though the only stated mechanism (class conditioning) is standard; compared with SMOTE and VAE.
MSMOTE changes SMOTE's distance to Mahalanobis (own part) and a standard GAN then expands the balanced data; compared with Bootstrap and tableGAN.
Improves the generator part of a VAEGAN for fraud oversampling, a stated change; compared with GAN, VAE and SMOTE oversampling.

MNDO samples bivariate normals over the most correlated attribute pairs and univariate normals for weakly correlated ones, a designed statistical oversampler rather than plain fitted sampling; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek.
Progressive decay Mixup mixes instance-based and class-based samples with a decaying mixing weight, a stated change to mixup; compared with other Mixup-based techniques.

Applies SMOTE-based oversamplers in a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding built with unlabeled test data, an existing sampler in a learned space; the abstract states an aim to improve SMOTE-based methods but names no comparison.
Runs a synthetic oversampler in the empirical feature space of a kernel, an existing sampler in a transformed space; compared with the same oversampler in the input space.
Improved triangle oversampling that synthesizes along the triangle median line with a variance regulator, a new interpolation rule; no comparison named.

Trains a regularized autoencoder with a joint linear classifier so latent convex combinations preserve class, oversampling built into the representation's training rather than an existing sampler simply run in latent space; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
ClusIM combines k-means with unnamed oversampling techniques through an undescribed switching step, so own versus standard parts cannot be told; compared with unnamed methods.
Borderline-SMOTE with new safety criteria and a reassigned weight-coefficient threshold, a changed SMOTE variant; comparison partners not named.
TRACOS generates along adaptive spline trajectories with logistic chaotic maps, a new oversampler; compared with seven oversampling techniques.

GAN generator built as a reinforcement-learning Counterfeiter that turns normal into fraud samples under a multi-objective reward, jointly trained with the classifier, a new generative model; compared with unnamed baselines.
GNOT generates minority samples with a genetic-algorithm scheme screened by novelty detection, a new oversampler; no comparison named.
Applies standard SMOTE-ENN on decision-tree leaf features before XGBoost, an existing sampler in a transformed space with no stated change; compared only with a baseline model.
Introduces a modified SMOTE that produces interval series closer to the original distribution; compared with SMOTE and smoothed bootstrap.
Sampling method built from fuzzy C-means clustering and SMOTE with no stated change to either, clustering then standard SMOTE; compared only with an unnamed base paper.
Refined SMOTE with in-line and off-line interpolation plus a refined ENN that keeps selected boundary data, changed SMOTE and cleaner; compared with classical SMOTE.

Main contribution is the Ghost Rate diagnostic; it also offers ContraSMOTE, an exploratory oversampler with contrastive-encoder neighbour selection, so own but not the main contribution; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
Proposes a newly named SCORE-SVM-SMOTE (based on SVM-SMOTE, change not described) alongside new features, so own; compared only with other sgRNA predictors.
ctdGAN adds cluster labels, a probabilistic subspace sampling strategy, a cluster-and-class loss and cluster-wise scaling to a conditional GAN, a new generative model; no comparison named.

An approach 'based on active learning SMOTE' with SVM whose combination is not described, so whether it is a new way of applying SMOTE or standard parts cannot be told; compared with class imbalance learning methods not said to be resampling.
Assembled SMOTE generates using local linear partitions from a newly proposed minimal-spanning-tree partition, a new way of applying SMOTE; no comparison named.
GenSMOTE picks the oversampling amount by a genetic algorithm (a search for how much to oversample) before ENN cleaning; evaluated only before against after.

AEDIO detects noise and borderline samples with natural neighbours and replaces them via an improved nutcracker optimization, a new wrapper augmentation; improves SMOTE variants and beats other augmentation methods.

Ensembles of existing oversamplers (for example ProWSyn with SMOTE-IPF) combined in parallel or series with a nearest-to-centre selection of synthetic samples, existing samplers plus a selection step; compared with four baseline oversamplers.
Proposes a novel collaborative adversarial training framework based on a GAN (change not described), so own as a newly named generator; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
Ensemble classifier built on data from different unnamed oversampling techniques used as is, existing samplers inside an ensemble; compared only with standard classifiers.
MOKCCAS is a novel oversampler in kernel canonical correlation adaptive subspaces (mechanism partly described), so own; no comparison named.

SMOGAN chains SMOTE with a GAN that enriches the SMOTE samples, with no change to the GAN stated (it may take SMOTE samples as input), a chain with a standard generator; compared with other augmentation methods.
Proposes a hierarchical SMOTE that respects the class hierarchy for hierarchical multi-label gene function prediction, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared only with TPR and flat ensembles.
Proposes a Two-stage CGAN training framework for imbalanced data, a stated change to training; compared with typical over- and undersampling techniques.
Oversamples malicious JavaScript by generating code with CodeLlama, a standard language model used as is; compared with existing oversampling methods.
New reverse-nearest-neighbourhood oversampler for multi-label data, an oversampler of its own; compared only with unnamed 'comparing methods'.
G-GAN puts a Gaussian minority prior and mixed noise into the GAN latent space with bagging, a stated change to the generator; compared with 11 oversamplers.
Safe level graph is a guide for choosing between Borderline-SMOTE and Safe-Level-SMOTE, a choice among existing samplers; success rate implies the two SMOTEs are compared, borderline on compared.
Proposed MCMC-guided GAN changes how the GAN samples (Bayesian framework with MCMC); compared with SMOTE, Smotified-GAN and GAN.
New 'Triplets' oversampler generating from minority-majority triplets at the boundary, for federated data; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
Augmentation pipeline built on a 'novel inpainting diffusion model' plus OOD post-selection; the diffusion model is claimed new, so own; no comparison with other augmentation named.
WGAN-GP with ordinary LSTM generator and 1D-CNN discriminator whose hyperparameters LSHADE tunes; tuning is not a stated change to the generator; compared only with original data.
HOUM loops SVM-based removal of distant majority points with Safe-Level SMOTE, a chain of existing steps without a stated change; compared with SMOTE, SMOTEENN, SMOTETomek.
HAPMA mixes GMM sampling, interpolation and perturbation with a protocol-aware feature mutation of its own (domain-constrained), so own; compared with SMOTE.
AE-MLELM-SynMin makes samples by crossover and mutation of autoencoder encodings, a generator of its own rather than a named sampler in latent space; compared with SMOTE variants.
S-SMOTE, an improved SMOTE that generates inside a hyper-geometry of the k neighbours; compared with SMOTE.
DSMOTE, a newly named SMOTE variant the authors built for churn data, change only vaguely described; compared with SMOTE.
TMACO, new oversampler with class-alliance seed selection, three-point generation and region filtering; compared with oversampling techniques.
BCGAN conditions a CGAN on a newly defined borderline class, read as a new conditioning; no comparison named.
Mix-up based oversampling proposed alongside a two-task CNN; mixup is standard augmentation with no stated change; no resampling comparison.
An 'improved over-sampling algorithm' generating between boundary samples and neighbours inside a solder inspection method; called improved, so own; no comparison named.
KG-CTGAN chains GSO-optimised K-means clustering with unchanged CTGAN; a standard generator chained with clustering is existing-parts under B2; compared with K-Means SMOTE.
Ad-RuLer adapts a rule-learning algorithm into a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE and KMeansSMOTE.
Spiral oversampling balancing technique (SOBT), a newly named oversampler proposed with feature boosting; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Evidential multiclass re-sampling scheme (undersample ambiguous majority, oversample borderline minority); compared only with ensemble methods.
An improved SMOTE (change not described) proposed inside an AutoML credit-scoring strategy; compared only with credit assessment methods.
CEGAN, a new GAN with classification enhancement for minority data; compared with standard data augmentation methods.
HPACID, a newly named hybrid of oversampling and ensemble that handles boundary values 'in a unique way'; generator not named; compared with ROS, RUS, SMOTE.
BDO, a new boundary-degree-based oversampler using entropy and aided boundary points; compared only with unnamed 'commonly considered methods'.
DS-SMOTE is density clustering then SMOTE interpolation, standard parts under a new name; the comparison test names no resampling method.
ADASYN combined with a self-supervised Wasserstein conditional GAN; self-supervision is a stated change to the GAN's training, so own; no comparison named.
Searches SMOTE's oversampling rate and k by multi-objective optimisation with a state transition algorithm, a search for how much to oversample; compared with unnamed 'other methods'.
New distribution-sensitive oversampler that groups minority samples by location and varies the synthesis rule; compared with existing sampling algorithms.
GraphIC synthesises harder minority nodes and spreads them with a SemiMixup module, a node oversampler of its own; compared only with unnamed baselines.

SynDroid runs unchanged CTGAN with an SVM that discards bad samples plus a KS-CIR test picking classes to enhance; standard generator plus filter is existing-parts; compared with traditional oversampling.
MCBC-SMOTE clusters the majority (elbow method) and oversamples the minority to the average cluster size, read as a new allocation of synthetic examples; compared only with unnamed existing methods.
Proposed hybrid of graded boundary-sensitive undersampling (GBMU) and adaptive scattering-based oversampling (ASMO), newly named methods; only before-after results.
Proposed softsampling and hardsampling combining under- and oversampling, explored alongside other sampling methods; generator not named.
SMOTE-FH, a SMOTE variant with a fractional quasi-norm and weighted Hamming distance for mixed data; compared with ROS, SMOTENC and SMOTEENN.

ACC-SMOTE, called an improved SMOTE: improved ant-colony clustering, SMOTE by sub-cluster share, Tomek links; the stated clustering change makes it own though close to K-means plus SMOTE; no comparison named.
SPMSC, an improved MWMOTE with a new position-based noise filter, mean-shift clustering and cleaning; compared with other sampling methods.
Introduces 'a novel method' for local synthetic instances with no detail on how they are made, so cannot tell if it is new; only with/without comparison.
Proposed Soft-SMOTE improvement (change not described) within an IoT intrusion detection architecture; compared only with state-of-the-art detection approaches.
An over-sampling approach 'that we propose' complements an inverted Dirichlet mixture model, with no detail or named parts; no comparison named.
TRIM, a new cluster-based minority oversampling method that merges and connects minority clusters; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
QC-SMOTE, a quality-controlled SMOTE with trustworthiness scores and best-of-K generation; compared with SMOTE variants and generative oversamplers.
Federated framework sharing noise-perturbed GMM class prototypes with SMOTE augmentation; standard parts, and the contribution is the FL protocol; no resampling comparison.
Hybrid of weight-based oversampling along low-overlap directions and moving overlapping majority samples toward their class centre; compared with several resampling methods.

Tree-based flow-matching diffusion (ForestDiffusion-style) run in PCA, learned or attention-augmented latent spaces, an existing generator in a latent space; compared with ForestDiffusion; borderline.
CWGAN-GP adds class conditioning to WGAN-GP, a combination of two standard generators rather than a new conditioning; compared with other oversamplers; borderline.
CBSO, a new cluster-based synthetic oversampler that keeps samples inside minority regions; improvements reported without a named comparison.
icross-validation searches for a better oversampling amount than full balance for any oversampler, a search for how much to oversample; compared with widely used oversamplers.
LWSF, a new augmentation fusing wavelet packet coefficients of faulty samples with similar references; the five compared methods are not said to be resampling methods.
A forecasting-based nonlinear SMOTE proposed within a voltage-stability learning machine; no resampling comparison named.
HCBST pairs an existing cluster undersampling technique with an oversampler 'derived from' SNOCC; cannot tell if SNOCC is changed; compared only across classifiers.
Plain SMOTE run in a locally linear embedding space and mapped back, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with traditional SMOTE.
'Improved VAE' whose only stated change is class conditioning in the encoder, i.e. a standard conditional VAE; only before-after results; borderline.
Perceptual-DPO fine-tunes a DDPM with a new perceptual preference loss for rare-class images, a stated change to training; results only before against after.
Mamba-DDPM (new architecture) with a boundary sampling algorithm and classifier interaction; compared only with an unnamed traditional imbalanced classification method.
Custom SMOTE, a newly named SMOTE variant with lower memory use (change not described); compared with traditional SMOTE.
TOMO, a new transfer-oriented minority oversampler that also reduces distribution difference; comparisons named are only with CPDP approaches.
DERBO, a new oversampler using differential evolution with an RBF-guided fitness; compared with 'imbalanced learning techniques' not said to be resampling.
GMC-SMOTE, a multiclass SMOTE scheme that shapes essay-score classes into a normal distribution; compared only with the imbalanced data.
CIAR uses RUS plus SMOTE inside bagging and AdaBoost ensembles, existing parts without a stated change; compared only with unnamed baselines.
MC-LDWO, a multiclass weighted oversampler with hyperspheres, density weights and a cutoff threshold; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
DR-SMOTE, a multi-label SMOTE variant with reliable seeds and reference-confined synthesis; compared with seven resampling methods.
Proposed PCT-GAN adds two psychometric regularising losses to a conditional WGAN-GP, a new loss; benchmarked against ROS, SMOTE variants, CTGAN and TVAE.
Deep SMOTE trains a neural regression model to produce SMOTE-style interpolations, a generator of its own; compared with traditional SMOTE.
PDFOS samples from a classical Parzen-window density estimate, KDE sampling under a new name with no stated change; no comparison named.
No abstract; the title suggests a new adversarial minority over-sampling method, so unclear.
AdaSRoF uses SMOTE with differentiated, dynamic sampling rates per rotation-forest member, read as a new allocation rather than plain SMOTE in an ensemble; compared only with classifiers.

Introduces a two-step local augmentation (anchor subsampling, then Gaussian or diffusion kernel draws) with theory; anchor allocation read as own though the Gaussian kernel is KDE-like; compared with SMOTE-like methods.
DiffMB, a Mamba-based DDPM (new architecture) with boundary sampling and classifier interaction; compared only with an unnamed state-of-the-art model.
GAN-E changes the GAN latent prior, discriminator noise and uses multi-scale GANs, stated changes; compared with 14 rebalancing methods.
APOEA is an ensemble with subview optimisation that 'implements an over-sampling scheme' on the critical subview, which is not described; cannot tell if it is new.
Data grouping and local clustering then over-sampling of rare-class clusters 'according to different rates' with cost-sensitive SVM; neither parts nor allocation named enough to tell.
Theory of synthetic oversampling with experiments using LLMs as generators without a stated change to the model; no resampling comparison named.
Proposes a novel semi-supervised oversampling method (not detailed, generator not named); compared only balanced against imbalanced data.
IGAN, a newly named imbalanced GAN whose change is not described; compared only with other deep learning detectors.
No abstract; the title names a new KDE-guided differential-evolution oversampler (Kdebo), so unclear.
CN-SMOTE, a newly named nearest-neighbour synthesis on an encoder-decoder, one part of a skin-lesion framework; not shown to be plain SMOTE in latent space, so own; no comparison named.
GAN-FP couples an infoGAN with a second GAN that enforces sample-label consistency and an inference network, a new architecture; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, undersampling and infoGAN.
TabDDPM-Med is class-conditional TabDDPM 'adapted' for medical data with no stated change, a renamed standard diffusion model; compared with CTGAN and other baselines.
Standard oversampling in an autoencoder space and a GAN for minority sequences, both used without a stated change; no explicit comparison named.
AW-SMOTE, a new oversampler with DBSCAN sub-clusters, weight-based allocation per cluster and adaptive generation; no comparison named.
A 'redesigned', 'enhanced' DeepSMOTE for AMOLED defect images, change not described, so own; only the final recall is reported.
Two-phase method that finds hard-to-classify instances, splits them into noisy and secure, and synthesises around them, a method of its own; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
C-TeDDGAN extends DDGAN with class conditioning and a new temporal correlation loss plus a TSTR/TRTS filter; compared only with unnamed benchmark models.
A proposed Modified SMOTE for binary variables (change not described) in a suicide-risk prediction study; only classifiers compared.
Label-noise filtering framework (mCRF, mRD) into which standard SMOTE is incorporated; the contribution is noise filtering; compared only with noise-robust baselines.
SSI-CBSO, new cluster-based oversampler with adaptive allocation, hypersphere density, Mahalanobis target selection and switching synthesis; no comparison named.
HSRSA searches combinations of random undersampling and SMOTE ratios under an FPR constraint, a search for how much to resample; compared with baseline resampling.
Hybrid sampling that adopts safe double screening as a new undersampler, followed by an unnamed oversampler; the screening-as-undersampling is read as own; no comparison named.
MGOML-NGF learns a neural geometry-aware sampling density with meta-learned control, a new generator; compared with classical and geometry-based resampling.
Introduces MDO, a Mahalanobis-distance multiclass oversampler, inside boosting (MDOBoost); compared with SMOTE, class decomposition and oversampling techniques.
SMOTE NC-GAN feeds SMOTE-NC samples with real data into a GAN, titled a 'modified' GAN, read as a stated change though close to SMOTE then a GAN; compared with SMOTE.
Segment-wise joint 12-lead PCA, then eigenvalue-scaled jitter and mixup in score space, standard augmentation in a PCA space; compared with SMOTE, cWGAN-GP and TimeGAN.
CLUSS clusters the majority classes, applies SMOTE and trains a voted tree ensemble, standard parts without a stated change; no comparison named.
Auxiliary-guided conditional VAE enhanced with contrastive learning, a modified generator, plus ECDNN undersampling; compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
GBC-AST uses GMM clustering, a Modified ADASYN focused on hard-to-learn samples and Tomek links; the modified ADASYN makes it own; compared with other oversampling techniques.
GDDSYN, a new clustering-based weighted oversampler with improved generation paths; compared with unnamed existing methods.
GANHS pairs a dual-discriminator GAN with adaptive neighbourhood-based undersampling, presented as new; compared with 'competitive peers' not said to be resampling.
ADWGKFO allocates synthetic samples per cluster by double weights and filters them by Gaussian-kernel class potential, a new oversampler; compared with other sampling methods.
CSMOTE is only named as clustering-based SMOTE, a name over standard parts with no stated change; compared only with gene predictors.
OC-SMOTE-NN, a SMOTE variant with learnable parameters trained against a discriminator with an orthogonality loss; compared only with unnamed baselines.
HIDIM designs an oversampler that bounds each disjunct by mutual nearest neighbours and crosses or mutates features by importance; compared only with state-of-the-art detection models.
FlowGAN is described as 'an instance of GAN' used to synthesise minority traffic, a standard GAN under a new name; compared with oversampling-balanced data.
DCS uses biased SVM to find support vectors, SMOTE on minority SVs, RUS on majority non-SVs and an SVM ensemble, a chain of existing steps; compared with SMOTE, ROS and undersampling.
New oversampler that creates samples in feature subspaces chosen by Bayesian reinforcement via nonlinear optimisation; compared with '10 existing techniques' not said to be resampling.
AdaBoost-SVM-OBMS with an improved over-sampling method that generates from misclassified samples of both classes; generator not named; no comparison named.
Standard VAE applied to underrepresented tractography bundles without a stated change; compared with duplication and SMOTE.
GASMOTE searches per-instance SMOTE sampling rates with a genetic algorithm, a search for how much to oversample; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
Chains two existing oversamplers, AROSS and WOA-SMOTE, without a stated change; compared with SMOTE, AROSS, Borderline-SMOTE, Safe-Level SMOTE and WOA-SMOTE.
SMOID, a new density-based oversampler typing minority instances via PCA/FAMD maps and kNN; compared with traditional oversampling methods.
DiSMHA chains unchanged Stable Diffusion image synthesis with feature-level SMOTE; compared with the individual augmentation approaches.
CMSOT, a newly named minority-clustering oversampler on MapReduce whose oversampling step is not described or shown standard; compared with unnamed benchmarking techniques.
A standard VAE trained on minority binding-site samples to generate new ones, no stated change; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and class weighting.
MC-RBO, a new multiclass radial-based oversampler using potential functions over all classes; no explicit comparison named.
CMO, a new minority oversampler that pastes minority images onto majority-class backgrounds; compared only with long-tailed benchmarks' state of the art.
K-CGAN, a newly named GAN-based augmentation whose change is not described; compared with SMOTE, B-SMOTE and ADASYN.
MIFS, a new hybrid sampler that defines samples by fused boosting and position information and resamples subsets accordingly; generator not named; no comparison named.
H-SMOTE, a newly named SMOTE variant for few-shot imbalance (change not described); compared with SMOTE.
Learns a parametric majority-to-minority mapping with MMD and triplet losses, a new generator; compared with classical and deep generative baselines.
SVD-CLAHE Boosting oversamples with a 'novel' SVD contrast enhancement plus CLAHE and undersamples with RUS; the claimed-new transform makes it own; compared only with CNN models.

ConDiff: diffusion augmenter whose generation is controlled by feedback from a selection and dynamic-threshold module, read as feedback-guided sampling rather than a separate filter; compared with unnamed baselines.
Improved SMOTE drawing new points from a normal distribution closer to the minority centre; compared with original SMOTE.
Improved SMOTEENN in VAE feature space with a new Chebyshev-distance filter of its own; compared with SMOTE, SMOTEENN and VAE-SMOTEENN.
ENaN, a new extended natural neighbourhood for SMOTE and its variants (ENaNSMOTE); compared with SMOTE and NaNSMOTE.
SP2-SMOTE extends SMOTE for privacy-preserving generation in vertical federated learning; only improvement over no resampling reported.
RUS or SMOTE inside boosting with feature selection (SelectRUSBoost, SelectSMOTEBoost), existing sampling in an ensemble; RUS and SMOTE versions compared; presented is borderline.
VFC-SMOTE, a new streaming version of SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE based on data sketching; compared only with unnamed state of the art.
OptiSCS oversamples only minority classes below a count threshold, a new allocation of synthetic examples, with label smoothing and CNN-BiGRU; compared with generative approaches on cost.
New oversampler for modulation signals that synthesises by sample distribution and cosine distance; compared with other oversampling methods.
GQEO, a new kNN-graph quadrilateral-element interpolation oversampler; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
Morphologically Guided Synthetic Augmentation (MGSA), a newly named augmentation within the WeldNet framework, change not described; compared with SMOTE and focal loss.
Garbled abstract mentions a 'proposed oversampling calculation' with cost-reduction SVM in a sensible kernel space, with no detail; compared with unnamed strategies.
SMOTE with FINCH clustering and a proposed per-cluster allocation by sparsity and weight, plus MLP cleaning; the new allocation makes it own; compared with other oversamplers.
Standard ECG signal transforms (noise, scaling, filtering, warping) plus adaptive per-class synthetic counts from validation F1; the generator itself is standard augmentation (B2).
New bicriteria oversampler choosing evolutionary-generated synthetic examples from a Pareto set (potential, borderline distance); no comparison named.
SMOTE-PSOEV, a new SMOTE variant optimising synthetic samples with PSO and Egyptian vulture (record is retracted); compared with Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and others.
AMEO, a new attention-enhanced oversampler for attack traffic within AOPL; generator kind not named; comparisons not said to be resampling.
Closed-loop per-class augmentation amounts driven by class metrics, using standard classical and GAN augmentation unchanged (B2); compared only with linear training.
CWGAN-GP with a GRU-plus-attention generator presented as overcoming conventional GAN limits, read as a new architecture; no comparison named; borderline.
DA-SMOTE, a new density and distance hybrid SMOTE variant in a bearing-fault CNN ensemble; only before against after.
Proposed pulsar-specific synthesis that aligns peak pulses and sums subplots of several pulsars, a generator of its own; no comparison named.
HIBoost is a hubness-aware boosting algorithm that applies plain SMOTE in each iteration; contribution lies in the boosting weights.
DeepCLSMOTE adds a class-centroid composite loss to DeepSMOTE's autoencoder, a new loss; compared with BAGAN and DeepSMOTE.
iBRF bags trees on data resampled by SMOTE, NCR and RUS with G-mean voting, existing resampling steps in an ensemble; compared with SMOTE, RUS, NCR and CTGAN.
MEB-SMOTE interpolates toward the minimum enclosing ball centre, a new SMOTE variant; no comparison named.
AG-GAN, a newly named adaptive genomic GAN that adjusts to important features, change only vaguely stated; no comparison named.
SONCA, a new oversampler for mixed numerical and categorical variables; only before against after.
Generative oversampling chains a standard WGAN with SMOTE, no stated change to the WGAN; no comparison named.
Evo-TFS evolves synthetic time series by strongly typed genetic programming with time-frequency fitness; compared with existing oversampling methods.
SMOM, a new multiclass kNN oversampler weighting neighbour directions; no explicit comparison named.
GTS generates minority nodes by SMOTE in a transformer feature embedding plus an edge generator, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with an unnamed baseline.
ISMOTE, SMOTE with fuzzy mutual-information kNN attribute weights, a stated change, inside a defect prediction pipeline; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
MT-SMOTE uses task-specific latent sampling spaces with neighbour-constrained interpolation and cross-task filtering, a changed SMOTE; no comparison named.
New borderline oversampler that extrapolates or interpolates by local majority presence; compared with other over-sampling methods.
Stacks existing style-transfer augmentation and DAGAN outputs, with hyperparameters tuned by pufferfish optimisation; no stated change to the generators; compared with SMOTE.
MFC-GAN introduces multiple fake classes into the GAN, a stated change to its classes and loss; compared with AC-GAN samples.
DDSC-SMOTE, a new SMOTE with spectral clustering allocation, seed selection and an improved synthesis formula; compared with seven oversamplers.
New genetic-algorithm oversampler evolving random points into minority points with a neighbourhood fitness; compared with well-established oversamplers.
KGA maps data by KPCA and augments positives with an unchanged GAN, the ratio set by misclassification cost; standard generator in a learned space (B2); compared with SMOTE_ENN and others.
IoV intrusion detection that oversamples minority classes by 'a novel' log-ratio strategy, with outlier detection and metric learning; generator not named; compared with existing detectors.
Proposed Weighted SMOTE (WSMOTE), change not described, in an HCC diagnosis pipeline; compared with unnamed methods.
KNNGAN splits the minority into safe, boundary and unsafe areas by kNN and generates with 'a designed GAN'; newly named and the GAN not shown standard; no comparison named.
LPGOS, a GAN using a variational encoder for the latent posterior, a modified generator, with TrWSBoost; compared with existing oversamplers.
Swarm optimisation searches the best mixture of majority and minority samples to rebuild the training set, a search for how much to resample; compared with unnamed popular methods.
GK-Means samples from multivariate Gaussians over K-means clusters, a fitted-distribution sampler under a new name with no stated change; compared with four oversamplers.

AB-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant that adaptively expands minority regions and generates in clean subregions; no comparison with other oversamplers is named.
GeNSDP is presented as a novel, newly named generative oversampler built on an unspecified lightweight generative model whose design is not described; compared with ROS, SMOTE and COSTE.
MOCGAN chains an autoencoder, a borderline conditional GAN oversampler, evolutionary subset selection and stacking; the GAN is listed as a combined technique, not described as changed.
Standard TVAE followed by a quality-diversity screening of its output, the generator itself unchanged; compared with SMOTE and unfiltered TVAE.
GAN trained with a new evidential loss and a joint training scheme to generate uncertain boundary minority images; compared with conditional GAN augmentation.
Convex-combination oversampling in the kernel empirical feature space (an existing sampler in a transformed space) extended by the paper's own unified preferential oversampling framework; borderline.
ALOD and ALOD-RE are active learning algorithms that incorporate existing resampling and anomaly detection; resampling is an unchanged step of the instance-selection method.
Standard WGAN-div and mixup augmentation with a tuned random sampling strategy; no stated change to the generators.
BODE is a new hybrid oversampler with boundary-aware selection, differential-evolution perturbation and density filtering, compared with eleven oversamplers.
The stream ensemble introduces its own adaptive oversampling strategy that adjusts generation to the current distribution; compared only with existing methods.
Stable Diffusion with LoRA fine-tuning and standard ControlNet Canny-edge conditioning used for oversampling, no stated change to the model; compared only with no augmentation.
MLAWSMOTE is a new multi-label oversampler that learns label weights by matrix factorization and label correlation to label synthetic instances; evaluated only against no oversampling.
SPSO is a new oversampler creating synthetic protein sequences from the minority and majority class distributions in data space; compared only with a cost or threshold method.
ICVAE is an improved conditional VAE whose decoder generates attack samples and whose encoder initialises the DNN; compared with three oversampling methods.
BSMOTE-DCGAN-EL couples Borderline-SMOTE with a new dual-channel autoencoder conditional GAN conditioned on manifold features and membership functions; compared with six oversamplers.
CSBBoost chains cluster-based SMOTE, undersampling and standard ensembles (XGBoost, random forest, bagging) with no described change; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
A new text augmentation that splits sentences at transitional discourse markers and checks polarity with a pre-trained model; combined with, not compared against, oversampling.
SMOTrojan creates SMOTE nodes in feature space and wires them into the netlist graph with its own topology-preserving edge-synthesis module; compared only with HT detection methods.
HUSDOS-Boost is a new boosting algorithm with heuristic undersampling driven by prior boosting results and distribution-based oversampling; compared with current imbalanced-data handling methods.
A new framework that optimises Borderline-SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE with cluster consistency to avoid overlapping samples; no comparison is named.
MCGAN is a modified conditional GAN fed with memristive hyperchaotic noise, a stated change to sampling; compared only with diagnostic networks.
PDR-SMOTE partitions safe, boundary and noisy regions and synthesises differently in each region; compared with other SMOTE variants.
CBR clusters with a heuristic threshold, drops majority singleton outliers and selects which same-class sub-clusters are oversampled, a new allocation; compared with unnamed baseline techniques.
SNEOM is a new oversampler based on the Sanger neural network that can also generate majority samples; no comparison is named.
SeismoFlow is a Glow-style flow with interpolation in its learned latent space, with no stated change to the flow model; evaluated only against no augmentation.
ASIDOTE is a newly named oversampler applying different augmentation methods to abrupt, slow and intermittent fault data; compared only with no augmentation.
VGAN-BL is an improved GAN taking VAE latent vectors as input with a KL similarity loss in the generator; compared with unnamed advanced methods.
A modification of SMOTE applied only to examples misclassified by an ensemble, a new way of applying SMOTE; no comparison is named.
SMOTEFUNA is a new parameter-free oversampler using the furthest neighbour, compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and SWIM.
GDSMOTE is a new oversampler using gradient intervals, root-sample selection and a safety-gradient allocation; compared only with baseline methods.
Autoencoder latent clustering then a structure-conscious, cluster-guided GAN oversampler; the abstract does not say whether the GAN is changed or a standard GAN is applied per cluster.
IIR_BACTGAN prunes non-boundary majority samples and creates minority samples with plain CTGAN; the generator is unchanged despite the new name.
A new parsimonious mixture of Gaussian trees model exploiting time-series smoothness generates the synthetic instances; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
CatBRS is a broad-learning anomaly detector that uses standard SMOTE-Tomek as a rebalancing step; compared only with baseline detectors.
IFT-GAN adds a feature-aware selection module and a new TD-GAN architecture with time-aware GRUs; compared with unnamed peers.
KM-SMOTE combines K-medoids clustering and SMOTE with undescribed sampling weights inside a NILM framework, close to clustering then standard SMOTE; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art techniques.

Synthesises minority nodes in a learned embedding space and adds its own jointly trained edge generator and mixed in-between nodes, more than an existing sampler in a latent space; no comparison is named.
Simplicial SMOTE samples from simplices of a neighbourhood simplicial complex instead of edges, a new SMOTE variant compared with SMOTE and other geometric samplers.
A new self-adjusting window for stream oversampling that selects past instances by minimising cluster distortion before generating synthetic points; compared only across classifiers.
Proposes its own oversampling method that keeps and enhances minority boundary information before CatBoost; compared only with an unnamed conventional method.

A new quadruplet-based class-conditional latent interpolation with stochastic gating and sparsity-aware positive selection, a changed interpolation rather than an existing sampler in latent space; compared with long-tailed recognition methods.
Equal-GAN is a newly named GAN with a tailored tabular architecture whose change is not detailed; compared with TabFairGAN and traditional methods.
BlindSMOTE creates synthetic instances and undersamples purely by evolutionary computation, a new oversampler compared with more than 90 class-imbalance strategies.

A new dual-space generator fusing dynamic-model simulations with measured backgrounds via a frequency-prior Chebyshev mask-UNet and structure-frequency constraints; no comparison with other generators named.
HRSB-SMOTE allocates synthetic samples per HDBSCAN cluster by ratio, sparsity and boundary degree, a new allocation compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and k-means SMOTE.
AD-BL-SMOTE is a newly named adaptive boundary SMOTE variant compared with undersampling, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
DualSS builds its own dual-diffusion generator trained disease-agnostically with a designed latent-space sampling pipeline for positive images; compared with rebalancing baselines.

The proposed multi-label oversampling uses standard non-linear mixup and geometric and colour transforms plus a minibatch sampling approach; the augmentations are unchanged, though the class selection could be read as an own multi-label scheme.
CDMOTE is a newly named cluster-disjunct oversampler whose change is not described; compared with four unnamed algorithms.

Chains standard SMOTE, a safety-level filter of synthetic samples, PCA and ITQ hash-bucket undersampling and AdaBoost without a stated change to the parts; compared with traditional oversampling, undersampling and GAN-based methods.
CUS-Ensemble chains cleaning, clustering undersampling, Borderline-SMOTE and bagged gradient boosting trees, all standard steps; compared with EasyEnsemble.
WTO is a new oversampler synthesising in weighted triangular regions, compared with 11 oversampling methods.
A standard GAN trained on wavelet-packet features generates fault data with no stated change to the GAN; compared only across real, imbalanced and generated datasets.

Feature interpolation in frozen ResNet features restricted to identical labelsets and gated per label on validation data, an own multi-label scheme though close to an existing sampler in a learned space; compared only with losses.
RANDSHUFF is a new oversampler for qualitative data using IVDM neighbours and random-shuffle crossover of attribute values; no comparison with other resamplers is stated.
EMO is a new oversampler building a boundary skeleton from minimal enclosing balls with a spring-mass model, compared with mainstream oversampling methods.
A new genetic-algorithm oversampler that learns the data distribution to generate minority samples, compared with SMOTE-based oversampling.
MC-CCR is a new multi-class oversampler with energy-based regions, simultaneous cleaning and its own multi-class strategy; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
A new fuzzy-rule and constraint-satisfaction framework that produces synthetic minority instances consistent with learned constraints; no comparison is named.
FSDA-SMOTE is a new density-adaptive SMOTE variant proposed within a meta-learning fault diagnosis method; no comparison with resampling named.
DB2SM chains DBSCAN-based removal of nearby majority instances, DBSCAN clustering and standard SMOTE; compared with SMOTE, DBCS and DBSM.
GAN-SMOTE trains a GAN on each sample's k-nearest neighbours to generate local minority samples, a stated change to training; compared with other oversamplers.
IWGAN adds an isomorphic generator-discriminator structure to WGAN, a new architecture; compared with three other GANs and SMOTE.

Incremental SMOTE keeps safe incremental k-means clusters, allocates synthetic counts per cluster and generates at an incremental rate with an improved SMOTE; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.
A framework of preprocessing, conditional GANs and a feedback loop; the abstract does not say whether the feedback changes GAN training or only screens its output.
Prompting GPT-2 to generate synthetic minority texts uses a standard language model as is; compared with conventional over- and undersampling.
A thesis summarising the author's novel resampling strategies that use both minority and majority distributions, binary and multi-class; no comparison is named.
Kernel-PAO concentrates generation near the boundary using KDE posterior probabilities and interpolates in kernel space, a new allocation; compared with SMOTE and uniform oversampling.
SMOTE-CD adapts SMOTE to compositional data with compositional operations; evaluated with regressors on imbalanced composition classes and only against no oversampling.
SMOTE followed by an artificial neural network that screens the generated instances, an existing model used as a cleaner; no comparison is named.
SMOTE-BFT runs standard SMOTE then removes unsafe synthetic instances with belief-function rules, an evidential model used as a cleaner; compared with popular oversamplers.
SMOTE-MRS is a newly named multi-resolution SMOTE whose change is not described; compared with SMOTEENN, SMOTE-Tomek and cost-sensitive learning.

Standard CTGAN with SHAP analysis, k-means prototypes and post-processing of its output (ProtoMix, noise injection, capping, CDF matching), the generator itself unchanged; compared with SMOTE and a basic GAN.
Derives and computes the optimal rebalancing ratio for any sampling method, a search for how much to oversample; compared with conventional 1:1 balancing.
DiffEdu is a conditional latent diffusion rebalancer with no stated change, one component of a student-performance prediction pipeline; compared with unnamed baselines.
DSMOTE is a newly named density-aware oversampler with clustering-guided generation under local density constraints; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
SC-WGAN extends WGAN with a classifier that works with the discriminator during training; compared with contemporary GAN-based solutions.
SE-gcForest inserts standard SMOTE and the EasyEnsemble idea after gcForest's multi-grained scanning, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; no comparison is named.
SMOTExT interpolates BERT embeddings and decodes them to text with the existing xRAG model, an existing sampler in a learned space with a standard language model as decoder; no resampling comparison.
mGNN's oversampling stage trains edge prediction for synthetic minority nodes with cost-sensitive learning, a stated change to the generator; no comparison is named.
SW-SLFN links standard SMOTE with a weighted SLFN through an adjustable balance factor; SMOTE is unchanged and comparison is only with SLFN classifiers.
HOUBC is a newly named hybrid that undersamples then oversamples using both classes, the change not detailed; compared only with conventional schemes.
AS-KDENN runs ADASYN followed by the paper's own KDENN cleaner using distance and local density; compared with four oversampling techniques.
Proposes two new shapelet-based oversampling methods for binary and multi-class time series; compared only with classifiers and time-series algorithms.
BENN trains neural networks on SMOTE and random-undersampling balanced subsets, standard samplers inside an ensemble; compared only with classifiers.
Efficient-DDPM uses an improved U-Net and optimised time steps, a modified diffusion model, within source-free domain adaptation; no comparison with other generators is named.

TaA adds an adaptive density-based Tomek threshold, distance-weighted ADASYN generation and iterative cleaning, three stated novel components; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Tomek links and SMOTE-Tomek.
Besides comparing ten methods, proposes AbusiveLexiconAug, a new lexicon-based text augmentation, compared with random oversampling, undersampling and losses.
FOFO applies standard SMOTE in two steps, first to detected outliers and then to the whole dataset, a chain of existing steps; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
Generates virtual samples and artificial outliers through PCA with the paper's own methodology rather than an existing sampler in PCA space; compared only with unbalanced models.
DeepBalance employs a new fuzzy oversampling method after BiLSTM code representation learning; no comparison with resampling is named.
Proposes ASMOTE, a newly named adaptive SMOTE applied after DPC clustering, inside a weighted random forest; compared only with similar classification models.
A modified SMOTE using Minkowski distance with entropy weights to set how many samples to make; compared only with classifiers.
Standard SMOTE applied within each random-subspace feature subset of an ensemble, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; no comparison is named.
WK-SMOTE is a newly named weighted SMOTE in the SVM kernel feature space with its own hierarchical multi-class framework; compared only with unnamed baselines.
K-CGAN is presented as a novel, newly named conditional GAN whose change is not described; compared with SMOTE-ENN.
Develops its own bi-level resampling for multi-instance learning, undersampling instances and oversampling bags; compared only with baseline and state-of-the-art methods.
A modified Random-SMOTE that clusters minority samples and picks support vectors as parents by cluster-centre distances; compared with unnamed algorithms.
A new oversampling method working in string space, compared with state-of-the-art string oversampling methods.
FLTGAN adds a focal loss to a tabular GAN, a new loss; compared with TGAN and SMOTE.
SBMF's own border-handling and selective border-instance modules undersample low-impact majority border instances and oversample the minority; compared with recent systems.
KCO selects regions by spectral clustering in KPCA space and generates by crossover interpolation of data templates, a newly named oversampler; compared with baseline techniques.
Despite the title, the generator is CTGAN with no stated change, mixed with random undersampling; compared with resampling baselines.
M-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE variant whose change is not described, used after KPCA features; no comparison is named.
A new oversampler that uses a neural gas network to learn the minority-class topology and limit synthetic samples; compared with seven oversamplers including SMOTE and ADASYN.
ASRDO generates within weighted safe hyperspherical regions along new direction vectors; compared with prevalent oversampling methods.
SIGRNN is a newly named sequence-to-sequence RNN generator trained on minority instances, not a standard B2 generator; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and SMOTE-NC.
Standard SMOTE inside AdaBoost with PSO tuning the classifier coefficients, an existing sampler in an ensemble; compared with SMOTE-PSO.
Oversamples support vectors with one-class SVM and SMOTE and proposes a new majority cluster-removal undersampling for an SVM ensemble; no comparison is named.
HHACO-FSOTe is a new ant-colony oversampler building feature values from all minority instances; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
AEMLO is an autoencoder oversampler with an objective tailored to multi-label sampling, a new loss; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

ICDG samples convex-combination coefficients from a learned neighbourhood distribution and adds neighbourhood-consistency weighting, a modified deep generative oversampler; compared with deep-learning and machine-learning oversamplers.
SMOMCCS builds compact coverage spheres around KDE-identified minority sub-clusters with angle-controlled synthesis, a new oversampler compared with SMOTE variants.
A standard progressive Wasserstein GAN generates CAD heart-sound segments, with bandpass post-processing as a separate step; compared with traditional augmentation.
T5W combines T5 paraphrasing with WordNet synonym substitution, a standard language model and standard text augmentation; compared only before and after resampling.
Proposes a geometric SMOTE built on an optimised kernel density estimate to generate rare attack data; compared only with a baseline model.
A new diffusion-GAN with a diffusion-based generator and a noise-sensitive auxiliary-classifier discriminator; compared with six oversampling counterparts.
MSMOTE, which considers the majority class, is presented as a novel SMOTE variant before LSDA and AdaBoost.M2; no comparison is named.
The OSW model combines SMOTE with a GAN whose sampling strategy, constraints, loss and backbone are modified; no comparison with resampling is named.
Existing oversampling followed by a neural-network detector that filters unrealistic synthetic samples, a separate filter with the oversampler unchanged; no comparison with other resampling is named.
G-KNN generates minority samples with crossover and mutation operators and a distance validity rule; compared with KNN plus random oversampling.
Uses BAT and PSO to search SMOTE's oversampling amount and neighbourhood size, a search for how much to oversample; compared with brute-force tuning.
LIMO oversamples minority nodes by adding edges that maximise label informativeness, a new graph oversampler; no comparison is named.
An improved SMOTE described only as a synergy of unnamed existing approaches; the abstract does not let one tell whether it is a new variant or a chain of standard steps.
DL-FSVM oversamples by centre distance in a learned DNN embedding before a fuzzy SVM; the oversampling is a step not presented as new, and no resampling comparison is named.
Artificial Bee Colony sampling that explores, selects, creates and refines synthetic fraud samples, apparently the paper's own; compared only with state-of-the-art methods.
HDAM combines a standard GAN and two conditional GANs with no stated change to them; compared with SMOTE and single GANs.
A GAN with a Bayesian regularizer that learns interpretable latent minority representations, a new loss; compared with unnamed competitors.
BBMO creates boundary minority samples as weighted means towards the closest majority samples; compared with unnamed methods.
MGVAE uses a majority-based prior with majority pre-training and EWC fine-tuning, a modified VAE; compared with other oversampling methods.
DEBCWGAN is a new dual-encoder VAE and balanced conditional WGAN architecture; compared only with classifiers.
NSOTE generates antigen-derived detectors by negative selection and removes noisy ones by minority density; compared with existing resampling methods.
Approx-SMOTE changes SMOTE to use approximate nearest neighbours in parallel on Spark; compared with the original SMOTE.
A three-step under-, over- and undersampling smart-pruning scheme whose sampling methods are not named; the abstract does not show whether the steps are standard.
mZ-cEAMD is a new oversampler combining cyclic exponential averaging of minority data with modified z-score outlier removal; compared with established oversamplers.
SMOTEBoost applies SMOTE inside each boosting round, the codebook's SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; the abstract reports improvement without naming a comparator.
A new genetic-algorithm oversampler with a kNN fitness function, compared with SMOTE-family methods; the record is a retraction notice.
Integrates a K* entropy-based distance into SMOTE and proposes a novel SMOTE and SMaRT combination; compared with random under- and oversampling, SMOTE+VDM and CNN+Tomek.
A new centre-contrastive VAE and a jointly-constrained, prototype-guided conditional diffusion model generate minority samples; compared only with unnamed baselines.
F-LLR applies undersampling and SMOTE selectively by training-score, its own allocation inside an F-measure-tuned lasso logistic regression; compared with RUS, ROS and SMOTE.
Hybrid bootstrap sampling whose oversampling is partially guided by hidden minority patterns, a stated change of the paper's own; compared only before and after rebalancing.
Oversampling by standard contextualised text augmentation with a non-random choice of tweets to augment; the augmentation itself is unchanged, though the selection is claimed as a novel strategy.
Farthest SMOTE interpolates towards the k farthest minority neighbours, a new SMOTE variant; no comparison is named.

DIAO replaces random image oversampling with an entropy-minimising density score, and DIAO-CP adds context-aware object synthesis, a new allocation for segmentation; compared only with no oversampling.
Radius-SMOTE generates within a scaled sampling radius while avoiding majority samples in a critical region, a new oversampler; compared with traditional imbalance processing methods.
SVBO describes the minority class with SVDD and oversamples its support vectors, a new two-phase oversampler compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ROS and cluster-based sampling.
Sets the number of virtual samples statistically and generates them with prior-knowledge-constrained generation filtered by a Siamese network; compared with conventional imbalance handling methods.
A new fuzzy rough set theory based oversampling approach in two variants, compared with other existing oversampling techniques.
A new adversarial network generating faulty samples from a proposed mixture distribution with a designed discriminator and feature matching; compared with other synthetic resampling techniques.

A proposed k-means-based adaptive strategy that oversamples minority boundaries and undersamples redundant majority clusters, read as its own allocation; no named standard sampler and no resampling comparison.
MDBC is an improved oversampler based on Mahalanobis distance and boundary constraints; no comparison with resampling is named.
ADASYNBagging and RSYNBagging put ADASYN and random undersampling inside bagging, existing samplers in an existing ensemble; compared with UnderBagging and SMOTEBagging.
GBSMOTE partitions data with granular-ball computing and then runs standard SMOTE inside each ball, partitioning then standard SMOTE; no comparison is named.
A new radiomics balancing method that perturbs ROIs by erosion, dilation and contour randomisation and re-extracts features, not a standard image augmentation; compared with ROS, ADASYN and SMOTE.
GADBSM tunes the DBSM hybrid sampler's parameters with a genetic algorithm, a search for how to oversample; compared with DBSM.
GT-ACGAN uses a VGAE-latent topology generator inside an auxiliary-classifier GAN, a new architecture; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling algorithms.
MSMOTE modifies SMOTE to consider minority sample groups and remove noise by adaptive mediation; compared with SMOTEBoost.
HyperSMOTE synthesises minority nodes and attaches them to hyperedges with its own trained incidence decoder; no comparison is named.
The paper introduces a simple minority oversampling method for its COVID-19 CNN without naming or describing it, so one cannot tell whether it is new or standard.
RMTO builds a reciprocal minority-neighbour graph with purity and margin screening and candidate rejection; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
DROS generates synthetic samples inside light-cone structures from inner minority areas to the majority boundary; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
A new fuzzy-hypergraph SMOTE that screens noise, sets per-sample oversampling amounts and picks synthesis locations dynamically; compared with 14 oversampling techniques.
MCS is a newly named modified cluster-based oversampler whose change is not described; compared with oversampling and cluster-based sampling.
SMOTE-WDC changes SMOTE to use weighted feature distances and adds density-based noise cleaning; compared only with a baseline.
FS-SMOTE selects minority seeds by a feature-space scoring mechanism, a new SMOTE variant compared with SMOTE and three improved SMOTEs.
A new sampler placing synthetic minority instances around existing ones via a gamma distribution; compared with SMOTE and other state-of-the-art methods.
ProWSyn is a new oversampler weighting minority samples by proximity to the boundary to distribute synthetic samples; no comparison is named.
DAO is a new distance-based arranging oversampler with filtering of synthetic instances in majority areas; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.

AF-SMOTE runs SMOTE and then filters its output with an adversarial discriminator and a boundary utility model, a separate filter over an unchanged SMOTE; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.

DEM-WGAN uses a WGAN discriminator trained on majority data to evaluate and keep synthetic minority samples, an evaluation filter over an unnamed SMOTE-style generator; compared with SMOTE algorithms.
DFSVM uses a feature and centre-distance oversampler in a triplet-loss embedding before a fuzzy SVM; the oversampler is used, not presented as new, and no resampling comparison is named.
TA-GAN trains the generator end to end with the target classifier through a designed feedback mechanism, a stated change to training; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
MWACGAN adds an independent DNN classifier and a Wasserstein gradient-penalty objective to ACGAN, a modified GAN; compared with ADASYN, ACGAN and CGAN.
A new decision-tree-guided approach that applies adaptive synthetic sampling to rare and complex samples near decision boundaries; no comparison with resampling named.
A new hybrid sampler that selects an optimal majority subset with k-means sub-concepts and ant colony optimisation before minority synthesis; compared with sampling ensemble algorithms.
