Two novel imbalanced ensembles differing in whether oversampling and misclassification costs are used; the oversampling is an undescribed ingredient, not presented as new.
Cost-sensitive oversampling makes the probability of generating each synthetic sample proportional to transaction amount, a new allocation; compared with the standard SMOTE-family variants.
A GAN-based method called novel in the title, but the abstract states no change to the GAN, so one cannot tell whether it is modified or standard; compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
IR-SMOTE removes noise per k-means cluster, allocates synthetic counts by KDE and uses a new random-SMOTE-based synthesis; compared with unnamed methods.
EffBaGAN builds BAGAN with new reduced EfficientNet discriminator and residual EfficientNet generator, a new architecture; compared with residual BAGAN.
ADCHSMOTE-TL is a new convex-hull oversampler with Tomek cleaning and power-flow feature computation for TSA data; no comparison is named.
GANs coupled with dual active learning modules that steer GAN training and the sampling of generated data, read as a stated change to training; compared only with imbalanced data.

KSCB couples K-means++ clustering and standard SMOTE with a CNN-BiLSTM classifier; the resampling parts are standard and the end-to-end 'KSCB optimization' of the data distribution is not described as a change to SMOTE, and the comparison is with unnamed sentiment methods.
MMT is a new mixup-style generator that blends head and tail samples drawn by a uniform and a reversed (differential) sampler, a stated change of its own; compared only with unnamed existing methods.

Two new oversampling strategies create minority samples by single or multiple imputation of induced missing values, used inside bagging and boosting; compared with class-imbalance learning methods not stated to be resamplers.

Proposes a federated diffusion model trained across clients plus a class-aware strategy injecting synthetic samples of missing or rare classes, a stated change to training and allocation; no resampling comparison stated.

Standard SMOTE is applied within each temporal attribute subgraph before a Diffusion-HAN detector; the contribution is the anomaly detection model and the comparison is with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
FF-SMOTE is a new firefly-based oversampling technique, compared with other state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
CMR-SMOTE adds a new centrality-guided majority refinement heuristic before BorderlineSMOTE and is compared with BorderlineSMOTE and a random-majority control.
BNNSMOTE is a new borderline nearest-neighbour SMOTE variant, and its augmentation effect is compared with existing imbalance techniques.
BS-GAN chains a standard GAN with Borderline-SMOTE with no stated change to either, as one part of a stacking malware detector; no other resampling compared.

K-means clustering of the minority class followed by standard MWMOTE (k by silhouette) is a chain of existing parts; compared counts only the claim of better separation than 'traditional oversampling techniques', as results are against a 70% baseline.
New resampling method using two SOMs to pick samples for under- and over-sampling with the resampling rates searched by a genetic algorithm; compared with other widely used resampling methods.
A standard GAN, then SMOTE, then XGBoost with no stated change to the generator; compared only with unnamed conventional methods.
CMO-SMOTE is a new misclassification-cost-minimization oriented SMOTE variant derived from a Bayesian analysis; no comparison is named.
CFSMOTE is a new fairness-aware continuous SMOTE variant for data streams, compared with vanilla C-SMOTE.

The hybrid sampler is built from named existing parts (an oversampler combining LR-SMOTE and CCR, then Tomek links) with no change described beyond combining them; results are only RF accuracy, no other resampling compared.
SMOTEHashBoost chains standard SMOTE, hash-based undersampling and AdaBoost; the abstract names no comparison with other resampling.

ADASYN, or majority splitting into low-imbalance subsets each balanced by ADASYN, feeds BiLSTM ensembles; existing parts in a sentiment method compared only with traditional sentiment analysis methods.
A novel oversampling strategy selects which minority instances to oversample by several criteria instead of at random; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
A new hybrid resamples only part of the way and covers the rest by cost-sensitive weights, seeking a balance between the two (how much to resample); compared with traditional sampling techniques.
Pools without duplication the outputs of several existing SMOTE extensions and trains SMOTEBagging; the parts are standard and the abstract reports only before/after rebalancing.

FedSSG's key contribution is a strategy for generating synthetic samples and distributing them across clients to cover rare pathologies and devices (a new allocation); the generator is not named and no resampling comparison is stated.
FE-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant that triangulates simplices around minority samples, compared with 16 oversampling methods.
GLoW SMOTE-D is a new discrete-feature oversampler with multiple selection and weighting, compared with various other oversampling techniques.
An improved multiclass method integrating a dynamic oversampling step (not named as an existing sampler) into multiclass AdaBoost; compared with resampling and boosting methods.
An enhanced gamma-distribution oversampler fits a local three-parameter gamma per minority instance; compared with SMOTE and the original gamma method.
O2PF and OPF-US are new Optimum-Path Forest based oversampling and undersampling methods plus a hybrid; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art techniques.
A changed SMOTE that picks neighbours by an MCD-based robust Mahalanobis distance; no comparison with other resampling is stated.

Siamese-HYNAA is a new generator in which a population optimizer creates candidate minority samples screened by SVM and a Siamese network; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-PSOEV (generator kind is a judgement).

GraphALP generates minority nodes with an LLM, with no stated change to the model, around a pseudo-labeling step and a second LLM oversampling pass (B2 language model); compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

Three oversampling techniques are presented for an improved nearest-neighbour classifier with no detail or names, so whether they are the paper's own cannot be told; compared only with the conventional classifier.
MASI is a newly named resampling algorithm whose mechanism the abstract does not describe; compared with ROS, RUS, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
AxelSMOTE is a new interaction-based oversampler inspired by Axelrod's model, compared with state-of-the-art sampling methods.
Weighted-SMOTE modifies SMOTE so each minority sample generates a number of synthetic samples set by a distance weight; compared with SMOTE.
Proposes five balancing rules setting how many samples over/undersampling should create or remove (a new way of applying resampling); compares sampling methods and augmentation.
A standard GPT-2 generates artificial maintenance reports, mixed with random oversampling; nucleus sampling is a standard decoding choice, not a change to the model.
MDFT-GAN embeds a Transformer-ECA feature extractor into generator and discriminator with a gradient penalty, a new architecture; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
An improved SMOTE developed to overcome SMOTE shortcomings (change not described) feeds an LSTM-AdaBoost ensemble; compared only with credit scoring models.
Extends the model-based synthetic sampling method to generate minority samples that reduce class overlap, a stated change to an existing sampler; compared only with benchmark models.
P-GAN is a physics-constrained GAN enforcing sensor ranges and monotonic depth during generation; evaluated only against no augmentation.
SHWeL, a new stochastic hashed LZJD representation, is said to tackle class imbalance directly and is compared with SMOTE; how it rebalances is not described.
MACO-SMOTE is a new oversampler with a multi-type centroid pool and spherical interpolation, compared with SMOTE and mainstream oversamplers.
The abstract says GLoW SMOTE-D (Gaussian localized weighted SMOTE with distance constraints) is proposed for the imbalance before the LBSLLM classifier; compared only with the state of the art.
POS is a new perturbation-based oversampler with a variance hyperparameter, compared with 11 reference oversampling methods.
ML-ROS-improved adds dynamic thresholding, weighted minority-label sampling and constrained graph augmentation to ML-ROS; several graph augmentation strategies are compared.
A novel over-sampling strategy for salient object detection (a saliency map task) is claimed with no detail or named parts; compared with saliency algorithms only.
OUPS is a newly named oversampler blending SMOTE with propensity scores, compared with SMOTE and PSM.
A novel oversampling method perturbs minority representations in the eigenphase domain, not named as an existing sampler; evaluated only before against after.
MIFF-GAN embeds a multi-attention information extraction module in generator, discriminator and auxiliary classifier with an optimized loss; compared with unnamed benchmark methods.
SVED-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant using support vectors, density-adaptive steps and two-stage filtering, compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
CSSF runs SMOTE within clusters and removes noisy instances, a chain of clustering, SMOTE and filtering with no stated change; compared with SMOTE.
WEMOTE is a newly named oversampler that builds its own word-embedding text vectors and makes minority samples as the mean of two same-class vectors; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
SOM-SMOTE combines SOM clustering with standard SMOTE before a random forest, a chain of existing parts; no comparison with other resampling.
Prefix-WGAN adds a learnable prefix vector and a dual MMD-plus-quality loss to WGAN, a new conditioning and loss; compared with SMOTE, GAN and CGAN.
SA-GAN adds a supervised autoencoder giving a conditional latent space to the GAN, a new architecture; compared with traditional data augmentation.
A new oversampler that picks minority pairs by distance in a DBSCAN sense and synthesizes by weighted arithmetic mean; compared with ROS, RUS and SMOTE.
A preprocessing flow includes a modified SMOTE handling imbalance together with incompleteness; evaluated only before against after.
High-Contribution SMOTE synthesizes from ROC-screened hard minority samples; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
PRO-SMOTE is a new conditional-probability SMOTE, also used inside boosting; compared only with classifiers used alone.
GAN-SMOTE integrates a standard GAN with SMOTE with no stated change to either; compared only with traditional fault detection approaches.
FLY-SMOTE is a modified SMOTE for non-IID federated clients; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
Bal-VAE is described as a novel VAE-based oversampling method that accounts for the imbalanced distribution (newly named generator, change not detailed); compared only with fraud detection baselines.
SMOTE-GPU adapts SMOTE to parallel GPU computation for big data, a new way of applying SMOTE rather than a new sampling rule; no comparison with other resampling is stated.
Abstention-SMOTE synthesizes from minority samples flagged by ROC-based abstaining classifiers; compared with ROS, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
DBCS clusters with DBSCAN and then oversamples the minority and undersamples the majority, a chain of existing steps under a new name; compared with other sampling techniques.
Txt2HSI-LDM(VAE) is a new text-conditioned semi-supervised latent diffusion model with its own VAE and cross-attention; compared with diffusion-model-based methods.
SMOTE-Out, SMOTE-Cosine and Selected-SMOTE are three new SMOTE variants; improvements are reported without naming what they are compared with.
S-SMOTE generates minority samples guided by expert secondary labels; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
Select-SMOTE is described as the authors' own joint sample partitioning and boundary optimization oversampler feeding LightGBM; compared with prevailing sampling methods.
Four new oversampling techniques for ordinal classification are proposed (not described) and tested alongside existing oversamplers.
Constrained Oversampling bounds minority regions with ant colony optimization and oversamples under constraints; compared with benchmark oversampling approaches.
A new class balancing mechanism based on interquartile minority oversampling is proposed with an LSTM-UNet-AdaBoost detector; the comparison includes RUSBoost, a resampling scheme.
MSEO generalizes SMOTE with random direction and scaling vectors; the abstract names no comparison method.
An optimized WGAN-GP with diversity loss, feature matching and noise injection is proposed; compared with other GANs and SMOTE.
FSMOTE is a new fractal-interpolation SMOTE; the comparative experiments are not said to involve other resampling.

Synthetic samples from convex combinations are used unlabeled in a semi-supervised SVM, a new way of applying interpolation oversampling though both parts are standard; no resampling comparison stated.
Four new oversampling approaches based on polynomial fitting (star, bus, curve and mesh topologies); only compared with each other.
GPT-3 used as is, prompted with style-based prompts, generates extra subjective texts (B2 language model; prompting is not a stated change to the model); compared with paraphrasing.
SFC-SMOTE clusters with k-means, filters noisy samples and synthesizes both classes with its own dynamic rate strategy (a new allocation); compared with existing sampling algorithms.
A new framework transforms majority samples into minority ones by optimization through the network with a distribution-matching objective; no resampling comparison named.
FWB-SMOTE is a new feature-weighted Borderline-SMOTE using XGBoost importances; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and others.
Analyst and Worker agents (by implication standard LLMs, model not named or changed) generate texts by prompted lexical and stylistic variation, then humans screen them; compared with SMOTE.
New SMOTE-based resampling methods for mixed scales with suitable distances and new ways of creating synthetic examples from all neighbours; compared with ways ignoring the data's scales.
A new adaptive weighted oversampler using modified density peaks clustering, adaptive sizes and heuristic filtering; compared with existing oversampling techniques.
Three stages of existing steps: random oversampling with noise, SMOTE, then Tomek links computed with DTW; compared with ENN, NCR, OSS and RENN.
A dynamic sampling framework searches the sampled class distribution in a wrapper with RUS, ROS and SMOTE (a search for how much to resample); compared with static sampling.
ISMOTE adds SVM boundary guidance, fault evolution modeling and consistency filtering to SMOTE; compared only with unnamed baseline models and methods.
A methodology searches the near-optimal class distribution for eight resampling methods (how much to resample); compared with full 50% balancing.
A standard VAE generates samples that a new membership function then filters; the generator itself is unchanged (codebook case of a generator followed by a filter).
New oversampling that synthesizes more from tweets with sentiment words and sets the amount on development data (new allocation and amount), combined with and compared to SMOTE and ADASYN.
MO-DGAN is a new multiclass GAN with a class-conditioned VAE and a modified generator; compared with a state-of-the-art GAN and other augmentation and oversampling techniques.
OOF is a new optimization-guided generation framework (PSO with diversity and fitness), compared with nine oversampling methods.

A new oversampling framework for multi-label graphs places virtual minority nodes in central regions and virtual unlabeled nodes at boundaries (new allocation); generator not named, compared with unnamed benchmark models.
OS-CCD is a new oversampler driven by a classification contribution degree, compared with six popular oversampling methods.
Ripple-SMOTE is a newly named oversampler (change not described) used with a weighted loss; compared only with unnamed conventional approaches.
IW-SMOTE weights SMOTE seeds using confusion information from an UnderBagging-like ensemble; compared with state-of-the-art SMOTE-based algorithms.
Cyber-Synth-CGAN states changes to a conditional WGAN-GP (spectral normalization, minority-focused training cycles, a sample-size-gated augmentation policy); compared with SMOTE.
Density-regularized SMOTE-ENC builds new neighbourhood density restrictions into synthetic sample creation and retention (not an existing cleaner); compared only with no oversampling.
SMOTE-COF is a SMOTE improvement selecting sparse minority seeds by a center offset factor; the comparative experiments name no other method.
SCALA is a multiclass balancing scheme of its own with user-defined scaling factors in a one-versus-one strategy; compared with ADASYN and SMOTE.
KMFOS interpolates between instances of pairs of k-means clusters (a new generation rule) and then cleans with CLNI; compared with many oversamplers.

SkewBoost is a new boosting algorithm that adds instances from a SMOTE variation each round and rebalances the total weight cost-sensitively; compared only with published results of unnamed algorithms.
An improved SMOTE whose change the abstract does not describe (codebook case: own); only classifier results are reported.
MS-ResACGAN is a modified AC-GAN with a five-tuple-based oversampling strategy; no comparison with other resampling stated.
A new oversampler builds an Elastic Net hypergraph to filter noise, set per-sample amounts and generate from a Laplacian-shaped Gaussian; compared with popular oversampling methods.
A hybrid of unnamed over- and undersampling setting class boundaries from nearest-neighbour class clusters; the parts and any change cannot be told, and the comparison is with unnamed works.
PF-SMOTE is a new parameter-free SMOTE using boundary and safe minority examples; compared with SMOTE and its variants.
A new geometric oversampler generating inside Delaunay tetrahedra; compared with SMOTE.
SIRSYN applies standard sampling importance resampling to the output of existing synthetic generators, a chain of existing parts; compared with 13 existing methods.
BCBSMOTE chains Tomek links, BIRCH clustering and Borderline-SMOTE with no stated change; compared with baseline sampling techniques.
NRSBoundary-SMOTE oversamples only boundary-region minority samples found by a neighbourhood rough set; compared with SMOTE.
HCAB-SMOTE is a newly named hybrid clustering-adaptive borderline SMOTE whose mechanism is not described; compared with unnamed other methods.
MFC-GAN is a conditioned GAN with multiple fake classes, a new loss and conditioning; compared with common augmentation and oversampling methods.
CP-SMOTE and IO-SMOTE are two new SMOTE variants; compared with conventional SMOTE.
ISMOTE changes SMOTE's generation space around a base sample; compared with seven mainstream oversampling algorithms.
IGFSO-AE trains the autoencoder with a new interactive feature-exchange strategy and interpolates in its hidden space, a stated change to the generator's training; no comparison named.
MCOG-CCR changes CCR with GA-optimized overlap metrics, adaptive weights and an improved sphere expansion; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
The two text oversampling methods are standard text augmentation operations (removing stop words and misspellings, synonym replacement) under new names; compared with each other and other techniques.

BARE creates a SMOTE node and builds its context and semantics with new distillation and meta-path predictor modules, a generator of its own beyond SMOTE in a latent space; compared with unnamed methods.
A 'refined' generative mechanism built on WGAN and Borderline-SMOTE using time-series features; read as an improved generator whose change is not described, compared with unnamed existing strategies.
The oversampler is based on an improved GAN, with fuzzy-integral classifier fusion; compared with related methods on sample quality (MMD, silhouette) and classification.
HGDO is a new oversampler using hypergraph noise filtering and Laplacian-shaped Gaussian generation; compared with popular SMOTE variants.

A fraud detection framework with k-medoids clustering, a new mixed-distance metric and 'cluster-aware oversampling' that is not described, so whether the oversampler is standard cannot be told; compared only with models.
A new fractal-based SMOTE resampling algorithm combined with AdaBoost; compared only with traditional methods.

SpectraGeni is a convolutional conditional VAE with no change to architecture, loss or conditioning stated beyond being designed for spectra (a standard model under a new name); compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and CTGAN.
Garbled abstract describes an enhanced kernel (Hilbert space) border SMOTE with flexible PSO-set oversampling rates inside BRFE-PBKS-SVM; no comparison named.

A new reinforcement learning generator whose agent synthesizes minority samples rewarded by classifier utility and boundary proximity (generator kind not named); compared with RUS, ROS and GAN baselines.

Adaptive cluster-based SMOTE finds minority subgroups by DBSCAN and sets each subgroup's oversampling by its ratio to the largest majority class (a new allocation); compared with other resampling techniques.

Online ELM with granule-core undersampling of the majority and SMOTE generating around minority granule cores and borders, read as a new placement of synthetic examples; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Cluster-MWMOTE combines agglomerative hierarchical clustering with standard MWMOTE, named parts with no further change stated; compared with 16 existing algorithms not said to be resamplers.
An improved generator for VAEGAN gives a new oversampling method; compared only with CNN, LightGBM and LSTM classifiers.
An extensive study of C-SMOTE, a continuous SMOTE variant for drifting data streams presented as the authors' method; compared with baseline models and unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Dynamic oversampling uses standard SMOTE and a standard GAN with variable sampling rates inside a KAN fraud model; the GAN is not changed (B2), and the comparison is with conventional deep models.
DBSMOTE generates along shortest paths to pseudo-centroids of DBSCAN clusters; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and Safe-Level-SMOTE.
SMOG routes samples by difficulty to density-aware SMOTE or a new difficulty-conditioned GAN (new conditioning and allocation); compared with traditional oversampling and GAN-based methods.
A new boundary densification oversampling in multiple kernel feature spaces within an SVM ensemble; compared with imbalanced classification algorithms not said to be resamplers.
OM-SMOTE maps samples to a new space and generates away from class overlap; compared with 11 SMOTE-based algorithms.
A standard VAE used as is generates minority cases for a deep classifier (B2); compared with SMOTE and GAN-based oversampling.
Counterfactual SMOTE is a new oversampler joining SMOTE with counterfactual generation to place samples near the boundary in safe regions; compared with SMOTE and other oversamplers.
cGAN and cVAE conditioned on failure class plus SNR level and maximum amplitude, read as a new conditioning though the models are otherwise standard; compared with SMOTE.
EMPR-Balancer is a new oversampler creating images from EMPR depth-wise components; compared with well-known oversampling methods.
GDDSAD is a new AdaBoost variant with confidence-based weights and its own dynamic under- and oversampling modules, not named as existing samplers; compared with AdaBoost and boosting variants.
Proposes a clustering-based oversampling methodology for synthetic generation (not described further); compared with replication oversampling and plain synthetic generation.
A new rough-fuzzy resampler removes negative-region outliers and generates minority and removes majority samples in positive and boundary regions; no comparison named.
Q-SYNTH is a hybrid GAN with a parameterized quantum circuit generator, a new architecture; compared with a classical GAN and SMOTE.
MetaSeGAN integrates self-attention into the CTGAN generator with metaheuristic optimisation, a stated change; compared with CTGAN, SMOTE, ADASYN and ForestDiffusion.
A hybrid balancing of SMOTE with a novel trimming mechanism of its own (not an existing cleaner) for imbalance and label noise; compared only with classifiers and a baseline.
FIR-FreqGAN adds a frequency-domain loss and FIR kernels in the discriminator; compared with conventional oversampling and GAN-based methods.
K-SMOTE changes SMOTE to interpolate between points and k-means cluster centres, used with RUS and boosting in ECA-IBD; no comparison named.
IFC-HFlowVAE is a flow-enhanced heterogeneous VAE with a new self-circulating refinement anchored by SMOTE samples and local GMM steps; compared with existing augmentation approaches.
CSO-FL is a new oversampler hybridizing chicken swarm optimization and fuzzy logic; compared with SMOTE, a modified SMOTE and TGT.
An improved SMOTE picks boundary minority samples by support degree and interpolates with their neighbours; no comparison named.
A novel augmentation strategy injects synthetic instances along the decision model's boundary (generator not named); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.
GLOS is a multiclass oversampling scheme of its own with a discreteness metric, dispersion-based amounts and group-specific synthesis; no comparison named.
LVQ-SMOTE generates synthetic samples from learning vector quantization codebooks; compared with SMOTE and used with MWMOTE.
DP-SMOTE uses an improved CFSFDP clustering to find subclasses and remove noise and weights boundary data; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
M-ADASYN modifies ADASYN with reciprocal nearest neighbours; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and GAN-based approaches.
SwarmBoost is a new method joining oversampling, PSO-based subsampling and boosting; compared with DataBoost-IM (a data-generation boosting method) and AdaBoost.
HCBS changes SMOTE weighting near minority centre and border, selects k-means clusters and cleans with a variant Borderline-SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and density SMOTE variants.
SMOTEMultiBoost places standard SMOTE inside the existing MultiBoost ensemble; compared with unnamed algorithms and techniques.
Ensembles of cost-sensitive hypernetworks use standard undersampling or SMOTE; the contribution is the hypernetwork ensembles, compared with unnamed state-of-the-art approaches.

Oversampling with a stacked autoencoder that learns the positive class distribution, with no change to the model stated (a standard neural generator); the influence of different oversampling methods is discussed.
A standard latent diffusion model used as is generates IoT attack samples (B2); compared with oversampling and generative baselines.
A new hybrid sampler selects instances after oversampling with a genetic algorithm guided by hypergraph interactions; compared with baseline sampling methods.
Quantum-Enhanced SMOTE interpolates in a variational quantum circuit feature space with quantum kernels; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek and SMOTE-ENN.
LDAM prompts an LLM, with no stated change to the model, to generate samples for tail emotion classes (B2 language model); no comparison named.
FADA-SMOTE-Ms is a new fuzzy adaptive SMOTE choosing an optimal alpha away from the closest majority data; compared with 8 oversampling methods.

BOSME samples minority instances from a Bayesian network fitted by likelihood maximization, a standard fitted distribution with no stated change (read like GMM sampling under B2); compared with SMOTE.
A novel SMOTE-style oversampler that predicts nominal variables with a model instead of interpolating them; compared with existing oversampling approaches.
GNN-CL includes its own adaptive graph oversampling of interpolated nodes and edges whose parameters follow a curriculum; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
A new online transfer algorithm oversamples in SVM kernel space via Gram matrix amplification and across arriving target batches; compared with baseline algorithms.
ITD-LLM-SeqGen uses LLMs, with no stated change, to generate user activity sequences (B2 language model); compared only with the baseline.
A modified ADASYN using Manhattan distance in its kNN step; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
The EWAD-IIoT anomaly framework balances with SMOTE and WGAN samples with no change to the generator stated (the 'ensemble WGAN' seems to be the detector); compared with standalone WGAN and WGAN-GP.
Sampling combines SMOTEENN with a new quantum-inspired noise sculpting step that perturbs boundary samples to diversify synthetic minorities; compared only with classifiers.
ND-S uses natural-neighbour filtering, an improved density peaks clustering and cluster sampling weights before SMOTE; compared with 8 unnamed algorithms.

GSG clusters faults by GMM, allocates intra-cluster SMOTE by inter-cluster density and drops synthetic samples that a second GMM pass does not assign back (own allocation and filter); compared with SMOTE and K-means-SMOTE models.

A new block resampling of extreme versus normal blocks in the joint predictor-forecast space with modified block bootstrapping and a modified SMOTE, for forecasting framed by event classes; compared only with no resampling.
TriEnhance generates minority samples by an unnamed method, filters them with binary feedback and self-trains with pseudo-labels; whether the generator is standard cannot be told.
SMOTE-D is a deterministic modification of SMOTE with per-object amounts; compared with SMOTE.
An inverse-weighted GMM cluster resampling allocates SMOTEENN across GMM clusters (a new allocation); compared with SMOTEENN without the GMM step.
Integrates biased SVM with SMOTEBoost, applying Weighted-SMOTE to support-vector and non-support-vector sets; named existing parts with no change stated and no other resampling compared.
RTB-DDPM adds class-guided sampling, a residual MLP noise predictor and boundary physical constraints to a DDPM; compared with state-of-the-art generative methods.
Three new geometry-aware SMOTE variants (centroid interpolation, angular sampling, adaptive step scaling); compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, K-Means SMOTE, SVM SMOTE and ADASYN.

Oversamples magnetograms in a Gaussian mixture representation, enforces physical consistency by global optimization, then maps to images with deep generative models (constrained generation); evaluated only against no augmentation.
robROSE is a robust version of the ROSE smoothed-bootstrap oversampler that ignores outliers; popular oversamplers are discussed but no comparison is stated.
A modified SMOTE uses SVM support vectors in kernel space and chooses interpolation or extrapolation by neighbour classes, before a QRNN; compared with unnamed methods.
MG-Time trains class-specific GANs with added MMD regularization (a stated loss change) alongside TimeGAN for sequences; no comparison with other resampling named.
WACIL generates pseudo-data for borderline instances by weighted average centroids and filters noise; compared with existing over-sampling techniques.
Smoclust synthesizes minority examples from stream clustering summaries for drifting streams; compared with unnamed existing approaches.

A new GAN with an LSTM-Transformer generator, spectrally normalized discriminator, two-stage training and mixing proportion optimization; compared with traditional oversampling and generation methods.
SBO is a new shape-based oversampler generating immune representatives from CURE-style clusters; compared with renowned re-sampling methods.

A standard Brownian Bridge diffusion model's outputs are filtered via UMAP of a classifier's feature space; the generator is unchanged (codebook case of a generator followed by a filter); compared with CycleGAN.
Conditional adversarial autoencoders used as is generate features for rare attack classes, with no change stated (standard generator under B2); compared with SMOTE.

A label-conditioned VAE-GAN with no stated change generates fraud samples from autoencoder embeddings inside a fusion ensemble framework (standard generator in a latent space); compared with oversampling-based methods.
A standard VAE generates synthetic data in a cluster-based scheme with no change to the model described (B2); compared with traditional oversampling and a GAN.
The 'novel hybrids' chain standard SMOTE with standard CTGAN or TabDDPM (B2); compared with SMOTE variants and the generators alone.
Word-replacement text oversampling that chooses which samples and words to rewrite with a new term weighting (TF-IGM-CW) and revises noisy labels; the augmentation itself is changed, so own.
Water-quality prediction pipeline that proposes a novel M-SMOTE whose change is not described; a newly named oversampler counts as own; only classifiers are compared.
T-SMmOTE interpolates three neighbours and also oversamples the majority class, a changed SMOTE variant; the abstract names no comparison with other resamplers.
Standard SMOTE applied to sentence vectors built from skip-gram embeddings and RNTN composition, an existing sampler in a learned space; only the components are ablated, no resampler comparison.
CTVAE adds contrastive learning to a conditional VAE, a modified generative model; the abstract states no comparison with other resamplers.
Malware classification paper that uses a novel GAN, not described further, to generate opcode sequences for minority classes; a claimed new generator counts as own; no resampler comparison.
SMOTE-family oversampling of latent vectors from a BiLSTM VAE used as an encoder, an existing sampler in a learned space; only classifiers are evaluated.
DOFCM-SMOTE removes outliers and clusters with density-oriented fuzzy c-means, then applies standard SMOTE to the minority cluster, a new name over existing parts; compared with four oversamplers.
NCNN generates synthetic text samples by random walks on a word network, a generator of the paper's own; the six compared approaches are not said to be resampling methods.
Proposes its own self-adaptive oversampler that synthesizes samples near real minority points; results are reported before against after, with no resampler comparison.
Self-supervised activity-recognition network that introduces iSMOTE, an improved SMOTE that labels synthetic samples accurately; compared only with supervised and self-supervised models.
A novel deep-learning imbalance algorithm for edge fault detection, described with no detail or named parts, so it cannot be told whether it is a resampler of its own; no explicit comparison.
STEM chains existing SMOTEENN with standard Mixup under a new name; the chain holds a standard augmentation, so augmentation; no comparison is stated.

Uses text augmentation as oversampling with no stated change to it, so standard augmentation; improvement is reported only against no augmentation, though the undescribed methodology could hide something new.
BFCH-SMOTE builds convex hulls from fused boundary samples and allocates synthetic samples by hull area, a new SMOTE variant; compared with 12 baselines and SMOTE-GAN.

Active-learning method combining outlier detection with an adaptive resampling that is not named or described, so it cannot be told whether the resampler is new; compared only with an unnamed state-of-the-art solution.
Hybrid sampling that removes majority outliers with LOF and uses LOF to pick minority seeds for interpolation in sparse regions, a changed oversampler; compared with SMOTE and no resampling.
K-means cluster-based over- and undersampling plus Tomek-link undersampling, a chain of existing parts with no stated change; compared with other resampling methods.
MLCIO, a new ensemble multi-label oversampler that bounds synthetic samples by Chebyshev inequality; the other approaches compared are not said to be resampling methods.
Fault-diagnosis architecture built on ISCOTE, an improved SCOTE with a scaling factor and iterative optimization; compared with 8 oversampling-based algorithms.
GAN-AE, a new GAN architecture with an autoencoder component and RNNs for variable-length sequences; compared with SMOTE, autoencoders and GAN models.
SMOTified-GAN feeds SMOTE samples to the GAN instead of random noise, a stated change to the generator's input; the next best algorithm tested is not said to be a resampler.
PPDP trims the majority by outlier removal and Mega-Trend-Diffusion and draws minority samples from a distribution shape of its own hypothesis; compared with OSS, SMOTEBoost and NDO.
MLH combines ADASYN, SVM-SMOTE and SMOTE+ENN in two layers with undescribed processing, a new name over existing parts; compared with existing data balancing techniques.
SPCAGAN, a GAN with linear manifold learning and a novel loss function; compared with typical oversampling regimes and previous GAN models.

Presents improved non-clustered and cluster-based oversampling techniques for big data on Hadoop without describing the change, which counts as own; the nod to prior oversampling work is not a stated comparison.

NICE builds minority counterfactuals by propensity-score matching of real feature values on causal features, then filters them, a generator of its own; compared with widely used and counterfactual-based imbalance methods.
LR-SMOTE widens the SMOTE generation space and is presented with an optimized random forest, a changed SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE.
FIGS chains feature importance, a standard GAN and SMOTE but adds a novel imbalance ratio (GIR) that is not described, coded own for that element; compared only with a baseline model.
MLDM, a diffusion model tailored to generate multilabel instances, a modified generative model; compared with other multilabel resampling algorithms.

Training-free intensity-based splitting makes synthetic minority images and a siamese network selects majority images to undersample, both of the paper's own; the existing approaches compared include generative oversampling.
LICIC, a new kernel-PCA oversampler that creates instances from less important components; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
Hybrid sampling with an LSTM-cBiGAN oversampler and a new time-series nearest-neighbour undersampler (TSFNN) of its own; compared with other benchmark sampling methods.
GM4OS co-evolves the oversampling function and the minority pairs with genetic programming and a genetic algorithm, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE.
Proposes three quantum-inspired QSMOTE variants used with PGM classifiers, new SMOTE variants; compared only with a random forest baseline.
Uses a one-dimensional DCGAN to oversample mitotic patterns in a CNN feature space, a standard generator with no stated change; only improvement over no oversampling is reported.
SMOBD, a novel density-based oversampler combined with cost-sensitive SVM; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-ENN.
IWSE adds information weights to minority synthesis and cleans with ENN, a newly named oversampler with a stated change; only ablation and sensitivity, no resampler comparison.
Weighted online sequential ELM whose offline stage oversamples the minority within a principal-curve confidence region, an oversampler of its own; compared only with ELM variants.
Corr-OS synthesizes ectopic beats from the top-K correlated heartbeats, an oversampler of its own presented with a small CNN; compared with the Next-OS augmentation.

Region-partitioned oversampling with RBF undersampling, interpolation in the boundary region, affine shadowsampling in the safe region and class-potential screening, a new scheme; compared with other oversamplers.

Adaptive oversampling placed inside Boosting, Bagging and Random Subspace ensembles (ASOBoost) with no stated change to the sampler; compared with existing class imbalance learning methods that the abstract does not call resampling methods.
OSID3 removes less privileged instances and oversamples high-privileged ones with a statistical strategy of its own; compared only with plain ID3.
New oversampler using genetic-algorithm selection and crossover guided by feature selection; compared with SMOTE, ROS, RUS and no sampling.
KG-SMOTE inserts synthetic samples by a Gaussian distribution around K-means cluster nodes, a new SMOTE variant; results are only before against after.
New oversampler that runs SMOTE along paths of a minimum spanning tree built on a KNN graph of the minority class; no comparison with other resamplers is stated.
No abstract; the title announces a novel synthetic sampling algorithm for rare health outcomes, so unclear.
SMOTEWB refined by a successive one-vs-many balancing strategy, a multiclass oversampling scheme of its own; the common methods compared are not said to be resamplers.
BASMOTE brings the adaptive weighting of ADASYN into Borderline-SMOTE, a changed SMOTE variant; compared with existing oversampling methods.
GraphSmin expands minority samples in a contrastive dual-channel graph embedding with an edge predictor, an existing sampler applied in a learned space; no comparison with resamplers is stated.
iF-ADASYN builds isolation-forest outlier handling and a new anomaly index into ADASYN, a changed oversampler; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.

Standard GAN, VAE and CVAE oversamplers with posterior binarization of dummy features, mixed with SMOTE-type samples at a tunable ratio (Elastic Oversampling); no stated change to the generators; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek and ADASYN.
O-GAN is a GAN used to oversample time series with no stated change to the GAN, a standard generator under a new name; compared with three other oversampling methods.

CAGE splits the minority into clusters and sets each cluster's generative capacity by its complexity, a new allocation of synthetic examples; the generator is not named; compared with global oversampling baselines.
GENNUS augments nucleotide sequences with GANs and SMOTE, with no stated change to the GAN, so a standard generator; compared with traditional SMOTE.
Proposes a generative model that synthesizes minority samples from a feature dictionary built by a pretrained extractor, a new generator; no comparison with resamplers is stated.
WRO, a windowed regression oversampler capturing additive and multiplicative effects between samples, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE and borderline oversampling.
DST clusters the data, computes per-cluster sampling ratios and applies random undersampling or a novel average oversampling, a scheme of its own; compared with RUS, ROS, SMOTE and CBU.
An ensemble with a novel re-sampling method that is neither named nor described, so unclear; compared with other similar re-sampling methods.
ARSO changes how SMOTE selects samples by using annular regions, inside a federated transfer learning framework; compared only with distributed baselines.
MCMO-Boost, a newly named oversampling algorithm built on AdaBoost whose change is not described, counts as own; compared with C4.5, AdaBoost and SMOTE.
G-SMOTE generates samples in a deformable geometric region around each minority instance, a new SMOTE generalization; compared with standard oversampling algorithms.
MNR-SMOTE adds a new mixed nearest-neighbour noise reduction on both classes before SMOTE, a changed SMOTE; compared with 10 oversamplers.

A multivariate VAE oversampler followed by boundary-aware selection of its output, with self-supervised mixup for representations; the generator itself is unchanged; compared with an RHVAE generative baseline.
A new genetic-algorithm oversampler that evolves optimized synthetic minority instances; compared with three existing sampling techniques.

SSVMSMOTE applies SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE to separate halves of the training data and pools them, a chain of existing oversamplers; the paper explores various generation approaches and claims to overcome SMOTE and SVM-SMOTE.
ImGAGN introduces a new GraphGenerator that synthesizes minority nodes with attributes and topology, a new generative model; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
New generator of adversarial minority samples optimized with a triplet loss during training; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art techniques.
ARHS, a newly named hybrid sampling combined with adversarial training, counts as own though its sampling parts are not described; compared with SMOTE and ROS.
LP-SMOTE sets per-label oversampling amounts by logarithmic progressive sampling, a new way of applying SMOTE; results are only before against after.

Extends a graph-based oversampler to widen the area of collinear synthetic patterns for ordinal classification, a changed oversampler; compared with existing solutions that include preprocessing methods.
ACWOS adaptively sets density-peak clusters and assigns per-sample oversampling weights and variable k, a new oversampler; compared with seven imbalanced data processing methods.
G-SMOTENC modifies the SMOTENC encoding and generation for nominal features and uses G-SMOTE selection, a changed SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTENC and a state-of-the-art oversampler.
3D-HyperGAMO, a new adversarial minority oversampling model that generates 3-D hyperspectral patches with a separate classifier; no comparison with resamplers is stated.
DDCO places synthetic samples using per-dimension data characteristics so they stay in the minority region, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and MWMOTE.
MCS-GMM draws Monte Carlo samples from a fitted GMM but weights minority instances by neighbours and density after a three-sigma split into four types, a changed sampler; compared with SMOTE.
OUBoost pairs a new Peak-clustering undersampler of its own with SMOTE inside boosting; no comparison with other resamplers is named.
A deep WGAN-GP generates fault samples with no stated change to the generator, followed by a 1D-CNN diagnoser; compared only with classifier combinations.
HEM-SMOTE selects SMOTE neighbours by a hybrid of Euclidean and Mahalanobis distances, a changed SMOTE; compared with conventional SMOTE and class weighting.
Resampling degree set by a classification intensity computed with a base classifier, a new way of applying resampling; the abstract names no generator; compared only with unnamed traditional methods.
Functional random forest with cost-sensitive splitting whose hybrid sampling uses functional SMOTE and weighted bootstrapping as is; the contribution is the classifier.

BEACoN applies SMOTE in a BioBERT embedding space with a cosine plausibility filter and a PSO-guided optimization whose target is not stated, existing parts; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE with filtering.

Treats synthetic samples as unlabeled and keeps good ones with a new graph semi-supervised algorithm, plus a cost-sensitive NCA reduction and boosting, a scheme of its own; the 15 benchmark methods are not said to be resamplers.
OREM interpolates only inside clean subregions around minority samples, with a multiclass version and a boosting version, a new oversampler; no named comparison.
Generates minority log messages with a standard SeqGAN and no stated change; results only show that oversampling helps.
NASBoost and NASBagging modify SMOTE with new measures to avoid noisy seed samples inside ensembles, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.

KODS constrains oversampled instances with transformer DGA knowledge and expert rules, a knowledge-constrained oversampler of its own though the generator is not named; compared only with unnamed algorithms.
Synthesizes boundary data of sub-clusters from regions estimated by bootstrapping, then uses AdaBoost, a generator of its own; outperforms the re-sampling techniques it discusses.
Has a pretrained language model progressively mask and impute majority rows toward the minority and self-authenticate labels, a new sampling procedure for the generator; no named comparison.
SMOTUNED auto-tunes SMOTE parameters for defect prediction, a search over how SMOTE is applied; compared with SMOTE and a recent class imbalance technique.
A new approach to choosing SMOTE parameter values for SVM, a search over how SMOTE is applied; no comparison with other resamplers.
GWGAN-GP feeds a Gaussian distribution label to a WGAN-GP as new conditioning, a modified generator; compared with other oversampling approaches.
Hybrid CVAE and conditional WGAN with column-specific output heads for counts and zero-inflated columns, then boundary and novelty tests, a modified generator; compared with SMOTE.
iForest-SMOTE picks neighbours by roulette on isolation-forest scores and interpolates in a hypersphere, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.

GENIE-IDS spends a fixed budget of synthetic flows on regions where the detector fails, a new allocation per region, with a conditional tabular generator and a screening gate; baselines share sample and generator-call budgets.
Combines SMOTE with a standard CTGAN for mixed-type failure data, with no stated change to the generator; compared with other similar methods not said to be resamplers.
CQNR generates minority samples in proportion to their cluster distribution without discarding noise, a new oversampler; compared with well-established oversampling methods.
SCUT-DS applies multi-class synthetic oversampling and cluster-based undersampling over stream windows, standard parts with no stated change to the samplers; no comparison is named.
Develops an artificial minority oversampling method for images of foreign objects on onion flakes without describing it, so unclear; results only before against after.
DTWS, a new dynamic time warping sampling method that generates minority load profiles, presented with a Bayesian CNN; no comparison with resamplers.

DKI-GMDM adds a domain-knowledge constraint module to the denoising process and imbalance-aware guidance of the sampling trajectory, a modified diffusion model; compared with TabDDPM and other generative baselines.
BIBO creates samples near decision boundaries from boundary information that joins safe and danger information, a new oversampler; compared with danger- and safe-information oversamplers.
Six new SMOTE-type oversamplers (ODO and DNO) built on new combinations of base and neighbour samples; compared with standard oversampling algorithms.
TS-SMOTE selects minority seeds by a symmetric-triangle scoring mechanism and interpolates among several samples, a changed SMOTE; compared with classical oversamplers.
FireMID uses the firefly metaheuristic as an oversampler after JMIM feature selection, an oversampler of its own; compared with traditional models and oversampling techniques.

Cost-sensitive majority-weighted minority oversampling that sets synthetic counts by imbalance ratio and weights borderline samples by distance and density, a changed oversampler; compared with unnamed imbalanced learning algorithms.
SDSMOTE oversamples according to recognition difficulty read from the spatial distribution, a new SMOTE variant; no named comparison.
MLONC sets an adaptive number of neighbours per label by natural neighbours and assigns labels by label correlation, a new multi-label oversampler; no named comparison.
Introduces modifications to the a priori oversamplers OUPS and Safe Level OUPS, changed oversamplers; compared with LN-SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and Safe-Level-SMOTE.
A standard VAE trained on few defective wafers generates synthetic trace data; the strategies studied concern the input representation, not the model; compared only between classifiers.
I-GAN samples the generator input from a rough minority density, adds a residual to the discriminator loss and reshapes outputs, a modified GAN; compared with 22 sampling methods.
SMOTE-SGA uses a genetic algorithm to set the sampling rate of each instance, a search for how much to oversample; no comparison with other resamplers is stated.
Oversamples faulty modules according to their fault content from the software history, a new way of setting how much to oversample; compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
Oversampling with a modified spectral clustering that sets how many samples to generate in each cluster, a new allocation; compared with k-means clustering-based oversampling.

A biased SOCP-SVM splits support and non-support vectors, then standard SMOTE on minority support vectors and repeated RUS on majority non-support vectors feed an SVM ensemble, a chain of existing parts; no named comparison.
Semi-supervised sleep EEG classifier that also improves SMOTE to remove mixed boundary samples, an improved SMOTE; results only before against after balancing.
New multi-label synthetic oversampler based on local label distribution; no named comparison.

BMCD adapts SMOTE to a large multiclass intrusion dataset, a multiclass oversampling scheme of its own though the adaptation is not described; compared only with and without it and with intrusion detection methods.

OS-GNN generates minority samples in a GNN aggregated feature space without edge synthesis, but the abstract does not say how, so it cannot be told whether the sampler is existing or new; compared with unnamed baselines.
AAC-cGAN adds spectral normalization and adaptive adversarial noise injection to a conditional GAN, a modified generator; oversampled and undersampled setups are assessed against each other.
ANS-REA places the existing Adaptive Neighbor SMOTE inside a recursive ensemble for data streams, existing parts; compared with SMOTE, ANS, RWO, MWMOTE and resampling ensembles.
TSP-SMOTE perturbs a triangle tessellation, scores regions and interpolates among several samples without k-nearest neighbours, a new SMOTE variant; compared with other oversampling methods.

Generates synthetic COVID samples in a deep feature space with a new algorithm for the scatter topology of the minor class and selective generation, a generator of its own; compared with other data augmentation methods.
A genetic-algorithm wrapper searches for regions in which random oversampling generates data, a new way of applying oversampling; compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
SMOTE followed by a new intuitionistic fuzzy rough instance selection that cleans both classes, inside a data reduction method; the cleaner is the paper's own; no comparison is named.
SMOTE-MRS clusters with K-means, applies standard SMOTE in each cluster and tops up with random oversampling, a new name over existing parts; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-ENC and ROS.

Called a novel class-conditional latent diffusion model, but the abstract shows the standard design conditioned on CLIP text prompts of the class, plus selective oversampling; compared with no and traditional augmentation.

Study of GAN training for fraud oversampling that adds an auxiliary contrastive or triplet loss and discriminator rejection sampling, a new loss for the generator; settings compared with the plain min-max GAN.
E-SMOTE weights danger minority samples by a KL-divergence measure before SMOTE interpolation, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.

OBGAN uses one discriminator per class so the generator focuses near the borderline, with architecture and loss designed against mode collapse, a new GAN; the 6 benchmark methods are not said to be resamplers.

SORAG synthesizes virtual minority nodes in central regions and virtual unlabeled nodes in boundary regions of multi-label graphs, a new over-sampling scheme; the generator is not named; compared with unnamed benchmark models.
Dual-AE-SN combines a new membership-function undersampler, non-linear interpolation with a dual autoencoder and a Siamese selector of its own; compared with six sampling techniques.
Proposes Adaptive-SMOTE, which selects Inner and Danger minority groups, and a Gaussian oversampler with dimension reduction, new oversamplers; compared with other sampling methods.
Oversamples only borderline, rare and outlier positives at different rates, a new allocation of synthetic examples; compared with ADASYN, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.

BEFO ranks synthetic gene-expression samples against WGCNA co-expression clusters with random forests and keeps only those more important than real ones, a selection step of its own; compared with five oversampling methods.
Importance-SMOTE oversamples only borderline and edge minority samples in proportion to an importance score and places samples by relative importance, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.
Standard CTGAN applied within multiple feature-selection views feeding an AutoML-weighted ensemble; the contribution is the intrusion detection pipeline; compared with intrusion detection methods.

Generates instances by perturbing random feature subsets of seeds, guided by a per-instance imbalance impact, inside an ensemble, a new oversampler; the reference methods are not said to be resamplers.
DAK-SMOTE stratifies minority samples by local outlier factor and adapts k, a changed SMOTE presented with a transformer; compared with traditional SMOTE.
PTASO uses Poincare distance, two-stage weights and region-specific generators (BEAS, OGS), a new oversampler; no named comparison.
HetGSMOTE extends SMOTE to heterogeneous graphs with node-type, edge-type and metapath information and type-specific edge generators, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed baselines.
Sliding-window minority sequences are generated by an improved VAE-GAN combination, a modified generator; compared with fault detection methods and oversampling techniques.
EBSMOTE grades SMOTE samples by a variance rate, rejects noisy ones and regenerates from the good ones, a new SMOTE variant; the compared methods are not named.
Feature selection approach for fault detection that proposes WSMOTE, a manifold-based weighted SMOTE; no comparison with other resamplers.
SeismoFlow is a Glow-inspired flow model that interpolates in its latent space, with no stated change to the model, an existing sampler in a learned space; only compared with no augmentation.
SOIL conditions a diffusion model on classification probabilities as scores, a new conditioning; outperforms competitors for class imbalance such as SMOTE variants.
Grey-wolf-optimized K-means clustering followed by cluster-based oversampling, existing parts with no stated change; the benchmarking algorithms are not said to be resamplers.
Hybrid of SMOTE and bootstrap sampling in a one-versus-all setup for multiclass health data, existing parts; only variants of the method and classifiers are compared.
A novel adaptive data structure based oversampler for ordinal classes that synthesizes objects from the structure of minority classes; compared with existing techniques for synthetic objects.
Uses an LSTM sequence model, which the abstract treats as an existing generative model, to generate minority samples from parent sequences with no stated change; compared with SMOTE.

DSP-SMOTE undersamples easy majority and oversamples difficult minority examples by a two-way self-paced mechanism with hybrid difficulty, a new SMOTE variant; compared with previous SMOTE-related methods.

MI-SpikingGAN adds spiking neurons, low-frequency wrapping and feature-matching losses and attention-based fusion to the GAN, a new generator; the other methods compared are not said to be resamplers.
A novel semi-supervised adaptive elastic GAN for blood cell images, a new generative model; compared with the conventional semi-supervised WGAN.
Distribution-preserving resampling with a new redundancy-removing undersampler (RRUS) and a core-seed SMOTE (CS-SMOTE), both of its own; compared only with other classifiers.
FB-MIO oversamples by multiple imputation guided by a new missingness-density factor and oscillator, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
SMOTE-ANO-FLS adds new local-set noise detection, adaptive noise modification and probability weights to SMOTE, a changed SMOTE; compared with 7 oversampling methods.
S2MAID combines semi-supervised labelling with a density-based undersampler (UD-density) and a SMOTE-density oversampler of its own and an ensemble; no named comparison.
Generates synthetic samples and accepts or rejects each by its location, a new oversampler with a rejection rule; no explicit comparison with other resamplers.
HS-SMOTE scores sample points with regular hexagons and interpolates among several samples without k-nearest neighbours, a new SMOTE variant; compared with ten sampling methods.
Noise-aware extension of the quantum-inspired QSMOTE that perturbs its similarity estimation, a changed oversampler; compared with plain QSMOTE and no balancing.
Generates minority samples by perturbing majority samples under a counterfactual objective, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
SMOTE plus ENN where the SMOTE rate is set by the out-of-bag error of two-factor random forests, a new way of setting how much to oversample; compared with a traditional sampling algorithm.
GAN-ASMOTE combines a standard GAN with adaptive SMOTE, with no stated change to the generator; no comparison is named.
MBK-SMOTE adds sample density and concentration-area division to SMOTE, an improved SMOTE; compared with standard and improved SMOTE.
MEXT, a parameter-free multiclass oversampler that places synthetic instances by anomalous scores and balances all classes at once; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Safe-Level SMOTE, MDO and DSRBF.
DNOS applies separate denoising processes of its own to majority and minority samples before ADASYN; compared with ADASYN.

CPS-3WS splits each class into risky, critical and safe patterns by posterior probability, removes risky majority and synthesizes from critical minority, a new hybrid sampler; compared with 11 data-level methods.
LOF-Enhanced SMOTE removes boundary noise by LOF and uses a Gaussian kernel similarity in generation, a changed SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.

VIGraph generates minority nodes with a variational graph autoencoder trained with cross-view contrastive learning, adjacency reconstruction and alignment, a modified generative model; no explicit comparison.
No abstract; the title names a new local-distribution weighted oversampler (MMWO), so unclear.
Synthesizes new steganalysis samples from both majority and minority samples, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
VANet introduces Weighted SMOTE, an improved SMOTE that sets sample counts by minority weights; compared only with other networks.
Proposes a new oversampling technique for imbalanced multilabel molecular graphs without describing it, so unclear; compared with MLSMOTE.
Credit rating model with SMOTE and a clustering-improved boundary-sensitive undersampling feeding a dynamic ensemble, existing parts; no named comparison.

SD-KMSMOTE filters noise, clusters minority samples and gives informative sub-clusters larger weights and more synthetic samples, a new oversampler; the existing methods compared are not said to be resamplers.

A new twice-SVM undersampler that deletes majority samples far from the hyperplane, combined with an unnamed oversampler, a scheme of its own; tested only on artificial data without a resampler comparison.
ABS, a newly named sampler that generates synthetic data from concatenated features, with a boosting version (ABSBoost); compared only with a previous study not said to be a resampler.
CORE oversamples the core of the minority and undersamples borderline majority by safe levels, a new hybrid sampler; no named comparison.
EC-WGAN is a conditional WGAN-GP with 1D convolutions in place of dense layers, standard parts under a new name; only its own effectiveness is reported.
CMCOB interpolates within maximal cliques of a cosine nearest-neighbour graph with central and radial boundary strategies, a new multiclass oversampler; compared with multiclass oversampling methods.
Credit risk model whose Borderline-SMOTE generates adaptive numbers per boundary sample with a new interpolation, a changed SMOTE; compared with unnamed methods.
BE-G-SMOTE clusters faults with a GMM, weights clusters by a density function and tunes an SVM-based boundary, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.
LS-SMOTE filters noise with local sets and interpolates toward the sample closest to the majority within each local set, a new SMOTE variant; compared with representative oversamplers.
Uses Gabriel graphs inside Borderline-SMOTE to find borderline samples without a free parameter, a changed SMOTE; compared with standard Borderline-SMOTE.
CycleGAN generates fault samples and a K-means SMOTE plus DCGAN chain enlarges them, standard generators under a new name; no comparison is named.
AKDRSMOTE adds adaptive k and dynamic random disturbance to SMOTE, a changed SMOTE presented with an IHHO-optimized SVM; compared only with fault detection techniques.
DepAug disentangles prosody and semantics with two encoders and a decoder that generates synthetic speech samples, a generator of its own; compared with supervised and self-supervised models.
The same borderline oversampling applied in the kernel's empirical feature space, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with that method in the input space.
A standard conditional GAN generates multivariate flare time series; compared with oversampling, undersampling and synthetic oversampling.
HHO-SMOTe uses Harris hawk optimization to find the SMOTE sampling rate for each dataset, a search for how much to oversample; no resampler comparison.
The CRD module clusters to find minority samples that resemble the majority and oversamples only those, a new allocation of its own though the oversampler is not named; only ablations.
Applies SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek, KMeans-SMOTE and ADASYN as is within a tree of random forests with rule-based fusion; the contribution is the classifier framework.
BGCS models pairwise dependencies of binary features with a Gaussian copula tailored to binary data, then filters with a GPT-2 classifier; compared with SMOTE, CTGAN and the standard Gaussian copula.
TRIM iteratively filters majority data to find precise minority regions whose seed sets drive synthetic generation, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with over-sampling algorithms.
A novel oversampler based on local density distributions for protein interaction sites; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

CWFLAM-VAE, a VAE-based generator named for attention and a class-wise focal loss, coded as a modified generator though the abstract does not say these sit in the VAE; compared with SMOTE, ROS, ADASYN and RUS.
KWSMOTE is the paper's own SMOTE variant with kernel-based neighbour weighting; compared only with unnamed strong baselines.
Threshold SMOTE changes SMOTE's neighbour selection using majority samples and is combined with Attribute Bagging; it is not attributed to prior work, so coded own; compared with SMOTE.
The contribution is a locally linear SVM classifier, combined with unnamed local oversampling and cost-sensitive learning; no new resampling method is described.
VS-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant that generates in selected high-value subspaces; compared with SMOTE and seven other methods.
One of the framework's contributions is an enhancement of SMOTE using a Kalman filter for imbalanced cyber-attack data; no resampling comparison stated.
Uses a standard class-conditional DDPM to generate minority anomalies; the stated novelty is in the weighted contrastive learner, not a change to the generator.
Cluster-Safe Oversampling is a new oversampler with cluster quotas, a new generation rule using cluster centres and a filter; no named resampling comparison.
DCFAD is a proposed diffusion counterfactual model that generates anomalies from real context, a changed generation procedure rather than a plain diffusion model.
C-SMOTE is a new continuous SMOTE meta-strategy for drifting data streams; compared with other stream balancing techniques.
DFBASO is a new fuzzy cluster-based adaptive oversampler with weighted allocation and a mixed synthesis rule; no resampling comparison stated.
k-means SMOTE is described only as k-means clustering plus SMOTE, a chain of existing parts; compared with other popular oversamplers.
EMDO is a new multiclass oversampler that learns ellipsoids with MOPSO and samples by Mahalanobis distance; compared with widely used oversamplers.
MDO is a new multiclass oversampler generating along Mahalanobis probability contours; compared with popular oversampling techniques.
Lightspace-SMOTE is described as dimensionality reduction followed by SMOTE, an existing sampler in a reduced space; compared only with no upsampling and other FDP methods.
The 'improved MAHAKIL' is k-means partitioning followed by standard MAHAKIL in each cluster; no comparison with another resampling method stated.
A modified SMOTE-IPF that incorporates Hamamoto's bootstrap is presented as a changed SMOTE variant for radar interference echoes; no resampling comparison.
LEAO is a new entropy-guided oversampler with attraction-repulsion generation; compared with 12 sampling methods.
Adapts SMOTE with a new multi-view distance metric and an uncertainty-guided generation module as a stated contribution; no resampling comparison.
A synthetic sample generation method for Tangut characters is proposed with no detail on how samples are made; compared only with the original data.
Builds differential-evolution oversampling variants using 16 DE strategies, not shown to be existing samplers; compared with 9 oversampling methods.
A new label-aware loose pairing of fundus and OCT images with class-balanced oversampling is one stated contribution; compared only with state-of-the-art models.
An improved Borderline-SMOTE with neighbour-ratio-based synthesis coefficients; several sampling methods are compared.
SIMO and W-SIMO are new SVM-guided oversamplers; compared with existing imbalanced-learning approaches not said to be resampling methods.
Prompts an unchanged GPT-3 with style-based prompts to generate extra training texts, a standard language model used as is; compared with paraphrasing.
Clusters both classes, then applies standard SMOTE and random undersampling, a chain of existing parts; no comparison with other resampling.
Generates minority graphs with a latent diffusion model and texts with a few-shot LLM, standard generators with no stated change; compared with class-imbalance methods not called resampling.
DB-MTD-SN is a new oversampler: mega-trend-diffusion around support vectors plus a novel Siamese network with a membership-function loss; compared with three oversamplers.
WOA-SMOTE uses whale optimization to search SMOTE's k-neighbours, a new way of applying SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and six sampling techniques.
FSDR-SMOTE is a newly named SMOTE that oversamples adaptively by local density ratios in CNN feature space; compared with traditional oversampling approaches.
Proposes its own spatio-temporal oversampling and selective downsampling for pixel-wise background subtraction; no resampling comparison stated.
V-synth is a new Voronoi-diagram-based oversampler; compared with borderline SMOTE.
DiVuse selects a diverse subset of existing synthetic vulnerabilities, a screening of generator output with no generator change; its seven baselines are not said to be resampling methods.
A VAE trained with a class-wise focal loss to target hard minority cases is a stated loss change; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
Safe SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant that interpolates only between reliable point pairs; compared with six resampling methods.
Proposes novel timing-aware oversampling for minority behaviours beside a SlowFast action detector; compared only with other detector models.
Introduces generative oversampling, which learns a model of the training data to create new points; presented as new and not shown to be a standard model; compared with well-known resampling methods.
Proposes an improved borderline SMOTE, change not described, as one part of a credit-scoring pipeline; compared only with competing models.
SEOA is a new SVM-guided evolutionary oversampler with margin-based quality checks; compared with various oversampling methods.
Tunes the hyperparameters of an unchanged CTGAN with reinforcement learning, a standard generator used as is; no resampling comparison.
Adds double encoders to the GAN used for oversampling, a stated architecture change; no named resampling comparison.
Proposes a hybrid VAE-Transformer generator for multiclass oversampling, a new architecture; comparison not described.
Proposes a newly named E-SMOTE technique for balancing before SVM feature selection, change not described; no comparison stated.
Proposes TabDiT, a newly named deep generative oversampler for federated clients, not shown to be a standard model; baselines unnamed.
M2GDL is a new multi-manifold dictionary-learning oversampler with validation of synthetic points; compared with recent oversamplers.
CA-SMOTE is a new SMOTE extension using both classes to synthesize; compared with SMOTE and other oversamplers.
CTWGAN-GP is a new name for combining standard CTGAN and WGAN-GP, with no further stated change; compared with GAN-based models.
Oversamples NER minority classes by Word2Vec synonym replacement, a standard text augmentation; compared only with no oversampling.
Adapts a Laplace-Gauss SMOTE with dynamic, class-based parameters and thresholds for ordinal data; compared with an existing method that also synthesizes patterns.
R-WDLS is a new density-weighted oversampler with shadow samples and affine combinations; compared with seven oversampling methods.
DDA Oversampling recalibrates minority distributions in latent space with a new density-driven attraction force; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
BCTGAN is a GAN with a new serial CNN-Transformer generator, balanced conditioning and new loss terms; compared with GAN-based methods.
Adds contrastive loss terms to a conditional VAE's training objective, a stated loss change; compared with conventional oversampling and a plain CVAE.
CBB-SMOTE clusters borderline and safe minority samples separately and applies biased oversampling, a new SMOTE variant; compared with SMOTE and Cluster-SMOTE.
Uses active-learning uncertainty and diversity sampling to choose the seed points for SMOTE, a new way of applying it; evaluated against the SMOTE-based methods it extends.
The 'enhanced' diffusion model is described only as a diffusion model combined with oversampling and standard classifier-free guidance; no resampling comparison.
Oversamples positives with an unspecified, unchanged deep generative model; the novelty is a domain-specific choice of which positives to oversample, compared with a general approach.
A modified generative network combining WGAN-GP and VAE with embedded ensemble classifiers trained end to end; compared with SMOTE-based methods.
Introduces an improved SMOTE that integrates clustering with neighbour-based strategies, change only vaguely described, inside a fault diagnosis network; compared with unnamed methods.
SC-GAN conditions a GAN on each student's past sequence to generate the next timestamp, a stated new conditioning; compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.
Sets the SMOTE oversampling rate dynamically from back-propagation MSE, a search for how much to oversample; no resampling comparison stated.
Fuses grey wolf and artificial bee colony optimizers to generate minority samples, a new oversampler; compared with 18 data imbalance handling methods.
FAIA generates minority samples with its own fuzzy adaptive imputation process for imbalanced data streams; comparison partners not named.
gamma-MiniDPC-SMOTE is a cluster-based SMOTE with a modified density-peaks clustering and adaptive parameter selection; no resampling comparison stated.
SMOTE-TLNN-DEPSO relocates detected noisy and borderline samples with DEPSO instead of deleting them, a new resampling step; compared with SMOTE-based filtering methods.
BAOUS uses the BAT algorithm to optimize SMOTE oversampling and random undersampling, a search over how to resample; no resampling comparison.
Synthetic data come from a standard WGAN applied per subspace after the paper's own partitioning, plus filtering; the generator is unchanged.
A new uncertainty-guided oversampling that removes noisy samples and steers generation towards boundary regions; compared only with CNN models.
Uses the authors' custom oversampler BBOT, change not described, in an intrusion detection pipeline; compared only with classifiers.
Uses an improved SMOTE, change not described, with random sample partitioning and block-level sampling on Spark; no resampling comparison.
A new algorithm that generates balanced data by bootstrap under the maximum-entropy principle and selects it by ant colony optimization; compared with other oversamplers.
OK-SMOTE tunes KNN-SMOTE with the firefly algorithm as a multiclass oversampling scheme; compared only with existing IDS.
A proposed noise-removal module applied before and after oversampling enhances existing oversamplers; compared with four common oversamplers without it.
CAPAIO is a new clustering-based, adaptively weighted interpolation oversampler; compared with eleven oversampling algorithms.
ExNN-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant with adaptively determined extended natural neighbours; compared with other SMOTE-related methods.
SROT is a new oversampler that creates synthetic samples from a sparse dictionary; compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.
Combines dynamic SMOTE with a newly named multimodal elicitation conditional GAN whose design is not described; compared only with existing sentiment methods.
IDHR applies instance-density oversampling, then its own distance- and performance-based rule for removing boundary synthetic instances; compared with traditional oversamplers.
Proposes BGOA, a new binary-tree-based graph oversampling algorithm, beside a weighted GNN; no resampling comparison.
Extends SADCO with hyper-cylinders between clusters to generate samples in unknown regions; no comparison partner named.
ADASYN is a new adaptive synthetic sampling approach that weights minority examples by learning difficulty; no named comparison.
CBROSE is described as k-means clustering combined with the basic mechanism of existing synthetic oversampling methods; no comparison with other resampling.
Generates fake-news samples with YAKE extraction and mT5 summarization, standard tools used as is; compared only with baseline models.
Proposes a novel function-fitted oversampling method beside hybrid sampling for multi-label code smells; balancing methods are compared.
IRESAMPLE+ is a modified RESAMPLE technique combined with SMOTE before a stacking classifier; compared only with related diagnosis studies.
SADCO is a new hypersphere-based oversampler with self-adaptive size assignment; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
SMOTE-LMKNN is a new SMOTE with local-mean KNN interpolation and its own noise filter; compared with seven oversamplers.
An autoencoder reduces dimensions and a standard CTGAN generates samples in the latent space, a chain of standard parts; compared with an autoencoder plus standard GAN.
The contribution is an online random forest ensemble in which one forest is trained on standard SMOTE data; compared with unnamed methods.
