ADL-GAN translates real samples across activities or subjects with multi-domain and contrastive losses, a stated new generator design; compared with a conditional GAN.
SS-EASF adapts SMOTE with a spectral-spatial neighbourhood and a new weighted distance space for neighbour selection; compared with an unnamed state-of-the-art method.
Designs its own hybrid sampling of belief rules: threshold-based removal of majority rules and DE-based generation of minority rules; compared with data-level methods.
IOSDS is a new incremental oversampling algorithm for data streams; compared only with base classifiers.
A Bayesian optimization framework searches sampling ratios jointly with classifier hyperparameters, a search for how much to resample; compared with SMOTE.
AC-VAEGAN is an improved AC-GAN architecture with a VAE component and 1-D convolutions; compared with GAN-based methods.
SMOTE-IH filters samples by instance hardness and then applies standard SMOTE, a cleaner followed by SMOTE; compared with SMOTE variants and recent oversamplers.
TLMOTE is a newly named topic-guided language-model text oversampler, not shown to be a standard model used as is; compared with other oversampling techniques.
MC-SMOTE combines clustering-based SMOTE, mild undersampling and ENN and Tomek link cleaning, a chain of existing parts; no comparison with other resampling stated.
Adapts SMOTE with a new multi-view distance metric and an uncertainty-guided generation module as a stated contribution; no resampling comparison.
IFSMOTE is an improvised fractal SMOTE, change not described, for image annotation; compared with SMOTE and FSMOTE.
Applies a standard WGAN to oversample minority nodule classes, a standard generator used as is; compared with augmentation, GAN and DCGAN.
A multi-task ECG classifier balanced with SMOTE plus a newly named waveform scaling augmentation whose design is not described, so coded own.
Generates class-controlled text with a transformer-based Wasserstein autoencoder that the abstract does not say was changed; compared with other synthetic data generators.
Applies existing SMOTE-RSB to features from a pre-trained contrastive encoder, an existing sampler in a learned space; ablations compare oversampling techniques.
TCWGAN-GP puts a transformer-based generator into a conditional WGAN-GP, a stated architecture change; compared with ROS, SMOTE and other augmentation.
G3O picks boundary seeds with a global kNN graph and local imbalance factor and interpolates with perturbations in a CVAE latent space; its own seed allocation makes it more than latent-space SMOTE.
G1No and G1No Gourmet are new 1-nearest-neighbour generative resampling algorithms; compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
A new oversampler that reclassifies minority samples by KNN and interpolates with a Gaussian instead of a uniform distribution; compared with traditional oversamplers.
RCS calibrates minority distributions by a weighted Gaussian mixture of neighbouring class statistics and samples from them, a new generator; baselines unnamed.
Trains a separate plain GAN for each minority attack tactic, standard generators with no stated change; compared only with no augmentation.
CPC-SMOTE applies SMOTE in combined class-specific PCA subspaces, an existing sampler in a PCA space; compared with SMOTE.
A new approach that adds synthetic minority points in non-metric distance spaces for time series; compared only with no augmentation.
Combines the existing GAN-based GANified-SMOTE with latent factor approaches, a new name over named existing parts; no resampling comparison.
LMCSB uses an unchanged large language model to enrich minority texts and filter majority texts; compared only with classifiers.
MISC applies SMOTE to samples on which a mutual-information classifier abstains, a new choice of SMOTE seeds; compared only with the MIC classifier.
APAROS clusters with affinity propagation and applies existing ADASYN and ROS by cluster type, a chain of existing parts; compared with ADASYN, ROS and k-means SMOTE.
P-SMOTE is a new oversampler filling blank spaces along the SVM positive borderline; compared only with SVM alone.
CLUS partitions data by k-means, applies an unnamed oversampler per subset and votes SVMs, a chain of existing parts; compared with unnamed methods.
MLOS is a new oversampler guided by majority Mahalanobis density with constrained synthesis and pairwise cleaning; the 17 comparison methods are not said to be resampling methods.
A novel adaptive over/downsampling technique is one stated contribution of a stacking defect classifier; compared with existing methods only.
LSMOTE is a new link-based SMOTE with Gaussian-process generation and noise filtering; compared with SMOTE and its variants.
Proposes batch-wise SMOTE plus ENN balancing during LSTM training, a new way of applying SMOTE; no resampling comparison.
SYNGO is a new genetic-algorithm text oversampler seeded with minority and borderline majority instances; compared with other oversampling methods.
Feature enhancement based on a diffusion generative model with no stated change to the model; compared with unnamed approaches.
A trust-stratified strategy allocates synthetic samples around high-trust regions without equalizing counts, a new allocation inside a semi-supervised forest; compared with non-resampling baselines.
Adaptively sets how many samples to create, but generates them with standard dictionary-based and transformer language-model augmentation used as is; compared with no augmentation.
GAN-MF is an improved GAN with a modification function for minority data; compared with standard oversampling algorithms.
BROOD is a new sampler adding artificial points on the edge of the training data with assigned class probabilities; no resampling comparison.
A new differentially private upsampler that estimates minority support with kernel SVDD, generates by gradient steps and filters by the majority support; compared with non-private methods.
SPO samples from a multivariate Gaussian with a regularized eigen spectrum, a new structure-preserving oversampler; compared with existing oversamplers.
SMOTE-CS replaces SMOTE's neighbour distance with a feature-ranked induced OWA distance, a changed SMOTE; compared with the original SMOTE.
A new adaptive kernel-space oversampler driven by distance to the decision boundary and local density; no comparison partner named.
KCSMOTE uses K-means++ centroids of safe clusters as SMOTE base points, a changed SMOTE; compared with ADASYN, k-means SMOTE and others.
A new over-sampling technique with a priori noise reduction and selective sampling of the minority class; compared with other over-sampling methods.
Generates balancing data from a Dirichlet process fitted to data partitions, a standard fitted distribution with no stated change; no comparison.
Implements a standard WGAN on signal images to oversample ECG data; no comparison with other resampling.
SMOTE-CDNN follows SMOTE with the authors' own centroid-displacement k-NN noise editing, a new cleaner; compared with state-of-the-art resampling algorithms.

EAC-GAN adds trainable label embeddings to generator and discriminator and an auxiliary classification objective, stated conditioning and loss changes; compared with oversamplers and baseline generators.
VSG-CDC-WCVAE finds sparse regions by CDC clustering and uses a weighted CVAE designed to focus on them, a modified generator; compared with SMOTE and a standard CVAE.
Sets the resampling ratio from support-vector estimates of the class ratio near the boundary, a new way to decide how much to resample; compared with SMOTE and RUS.
MSHR is a new hybrid resampling that replaces silhouette-screened pseudo-negatives with interpolated positives; comparison methods unnamed.
NLDAO is a new parameter-free natural-neighbour density oversampler with noise filtering and uneven allocation; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes MSMOTE, a margin-based SMOTE variant, as one part of a GBDT intrusion detection scheme; no resampling comparison.
ARPMG-MS-SMOTE interpolates multi-scale latent features with physics-guided encoding and abductive correction, a physics-constrained generation; compared with unnamed methods.
A domain-aware SMOTE-ENN that enforces physiological constraints on synthetic samples, a constrained generation; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek.
CFA is a new counterfactual oversampler combining actual feature values of existing instances; compared with SMOTE variants and other oversamplers.
DPB-SMOTE is a new SMOTE for discrete features using probability theory and borderline samples; compared with SMOTE.
Uses a standard conditional WGAN-GP with a separate quality index to screen its output; the generator itself is unchanged.
CBHSID is a new cluster-based hybrid sampler that removes far majority points and generates near sub-cluster centres; compared with data balancing methods.
OAA-DB combines the standard one-against-all decomposition with an unnamed data balancing technique; no resampling comparison.
K-CGAN is a newly named conditional GAN, change not described and not shown to be standard; compared with other oversampling approaches.
ESMOTE-GAN trains standard GANs on undersampled, SMOTE-balanced subsets, a chain of existing parts with an unchanged generator; no resampling comparison.
Per-modality VAEs plus a class-conditional diffusion model in their joint latent space, standard generators used as is; compared with tabular diffusion generators.
A WGAN generates VAE latent codes, and its generator is changed by introducing the variance of generated samples; compared with WGAN, AE+WGAN and SMOTE.
SOM-SMOTE is described only as combining SOM clustering with SMOTE for a radar clutter classifier; no resampling comparison.
Uses a conditional VAE's latent density as a cleaner to drop seeds before standard SMOTE in data space; compared with SMOTE and deep generative models.
QMSVM takes support vectors and misclassified samples from quotient-space granules as SMOTE seeds and majority samples, its own resampling scheme; compared with unnamed algorithms.
Generates minority data using agglomerative hierarchical clustering with Ward's linkage but does not say how samples are made; compared only before and after.
GAN-SAMO adds a self-attention mechanism to GAN oversampling to capture minority correlations, a stated architecture change; compared with unnamed imbalance methods.
TransWGAN-EF builds Transformer latent-sequence encoding into a WGAN, a stated architecture change, and filters its output; comparison methods unnamed.
A newly named Incremental SMOTE-KMeans generating only in reliable clusters, change not described, aligned with a cluster-structured SVM; compared with unnamed methods.
A new fast oversampler for large datasets that avoids k-nearest-neighbour search; compared with the fastest oversamplers in the literature.
A redesigned, enhanced DeepSMOTE for glass crack images, change not described; no comparison stated.
GBO is GAN-based oversampling and SSG chains SVM-SMOTE with a GAN, with no stated change to the GAN; compared with SMOTE-based approaches.
Redesigns five under- and over-sampling techniques to sample inside monotonic chains, new samplers; compared with their standard versions.
A new guided oversampling strategy that inserts NaNs by feature importance and then interpolates; compared only with training on the original data.
KRISMOTE is a new oversampler weighting minority samples by clustering-based sampling-region importance; compared with popular oversamplers.
EDU-CDA is a new mixed-type augmentation pairing conditional SMOTE for continuous with conditional Bernoulli sampling for binary variables; validated against real data only.
Magnify-GAN uses multiple discriminators with different losses and a dynamic coefficient, a new GAN variant; compared with ten sampling methods.
Clusters the data and applies unnamed over- and undersampling in each cluster, a chain of existing parts; compared with SMOTE, NearMiss and SMOTETomek.
Fits a standard VAE to the minority class and samples from it, a standard generator used as is; no comparison stated.
KDENDS_SMOTE guides SMOTE with kernel density ratios and neighbour density selection, a new SMOTE variant; compared with six oversamplers.
RSMOTE is a new self-adaptive SMOTE using relative density and chaos-based reweighting; comparison methods not named.
Develops a novel minority oversampling technique beside a Bayesian network attack forecaster; compared with filtering techniques not said to be resampling.
KM++ SMOTE is a new improved SMOTE whose change is not described; compared with other improved SMOTE algorithms.
ICOTE generates immune-network centroids as synthetic examples, a new oversampler, also with ENN; compared with renowned resampling methods.
Augments wafer maps with a framework built around a convolutional autoencoder, with no stated change to the generator; no resampling comparison.
SEAL trains a latent-space adversarial generator with an added structure loss preserving class covariance, a new loss; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

Generates synthetic neighbourhood samples around training points, inspired by the localized generalization error model, to balance and diversify an ensemble; compared with ensembles not called resampling.
Proposes AdaDepSyn, a new severity-aware adaptive oversampler for depression texts; compared with popular oversampling techniques such as ADASYN.
A preliminary stream method described only as using k nearest neighbours and an oversampling technique, standard parts with no stated change; no comparison.
NCLWO is a new weighted oversampler that expands sampling regions by Newton's cooling law and shifts majority points; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
MISO is a new generator of anchor instances with attention fusion, a mutual-information loss and a coupled adversarial encoder-decoder; compared with unnamed baselines.
FedSig is a new federated graph SMOTE with two-stage minority node synthesis, an edge generator and a regularizer; compared with unnamed methods.
AS-GAN chains ADASYN with a GAN that refines ADASYN samples, with no stated change to the GAN itself; no resampling comparison.
An unchanged LLM generates rare trigger instances guided by graph-based MCMC selection of neighbouring triggers; compared with existing methods only.
The contribution is a boosting ensemble with feature selection that uses standard RUS or SMOTE inside; the RUS and SMOTE versions are compared.
B2M combines instance and class-balanced sampling with feature-space mixup across the two streams, standard parts with no stated generator change; compared with oversampling and mixing methods.
Local digital twins generate synthetic samples in an adaptive framework, but the abstract does not say how; no resampling comparison.
safe-SMOTE is a new minority over-sampling method; compared with SMOTE and no oversampling.
